So much for the exterior facts of the story, but, after all, they are very exterior facts. About the real interest of the business one is necessarily very much in the dark. How was Filmer feeling at the time? How much was a certain unpleasant anticipation present inside that very new and fashionable frock-coat? He was in the halfpenny, penny, sixpenny, and more expensive papers alike, and acknowledged by the whole world as “the Greatest Discoverer of This or Any Age.” He had invented a practicable flying machine, and every day down among the Surrey hills the life-sized model was getting ready. And when it was ready, it followed as a clear inevitable consequence of his having invented and made it﻿—everybody in the world, indeed, seemed to take it for granted; there wasn’t a gap anywhere in that serried front of anticipation﻿—that he would proudly and cheerfully get aboard it, ascend with it, and fly.

===Chinese===
故事的外在事实便到此为止，可毕竟，那都只是非常外在的事实。至于这件事真正的兴味所在，人难免如在五里雾中。菲尔默当时心境如何？在那件崭新的时髦礼服大衣之下，某种不妙的预感到底占了多大分量？他登上了半便士、一便士、六便士乃至更贵的种种报纸，举世都奉他为"当代乃至亘古以来最伟大的发现者"。他发明了一架实用的飞行机器，在萨里丘陵的那一头，与实物同大的模型每一天都在装配就绪。等到它准备就绪，一个顺理成章、不可避免的后果便是——世上每个人似乎都把这当作理所当然，在那众志成城翘首以待的阵线上毫无一处缺口——他将骄傲而愉快地登上去，随之升空，飞翔。

===Original===
But we know now pretty clearly that simple pride and cheerfulness in such an act were singularly out of harmony with Filmer’s private constitution. It occurred to no one at the time, but there the fact is. We can guess with some confidence now that it must have been drifting about in his mind a great deal during the day, and, from a little note to his physician complaining of persistent insomnia, we have the soundest reason for supposing it dominated his nights﻿—the idea that it would be after all, in spite of his theoretical security, an abominably sickening, uncomfortable, and dangerous thing for him to flap about in nothingness a thousand feet or so in the air. It must have dawned upon him quite early in the period of being the Greatest Discoverer of This or Any Age, the vision of doing this and that with an extensive void below. Perhaps somewhen in his youth he had looked down a great height or fallen down in some excessively uncomfortable way; perhaps some habit of sleeping on the wrong side had resulted in that disagreeable falling nightmare one knows, and given him his horror; of the strength of that horror there remains now not a particle of doubt.

===Chinese===
可如今我们相当清楚地知道，做这种事时单纯的骄傲与愉快，与菲尔默的天性是极不相合的。当时谁也没有想到这一点，可事实就是如此。如今我们可以颇有把握地推测，这件事白天一定在他脑中翻来覆去；而从他写给医生抱怨顽固失眠的一张便条来看，我们有最充分的理由断定，它也盘踞了他的夜晚——那念头便是：尽管他在理论上万无一失，可要他在离地约莫一千英尺的一片虚无之中扑腾来扑腾去，到底是一件叫人恶心得要命、既不舒服又危险的事。早在荣任"当代乃至亘古以来最伟大的发现者"之初，他脑际一定就浮起了这幅图景——身下是一片广袤的虚空，自己却要在其中做出这样那样的动作。也许在他青年时代的某时，他曾从极高的地方往下望过，或者曾以一种极不舒服的方式摔下来过；也许是某种睡姿不当的习惯，招来了人所共知的那种难受的坠落噩梦，给了他这份恐惧；这恐惧有多深，如今已不容一丝怀疑。

===Original===
Apparently he had never weighed this duty of flying in his earlier days of research; the machine had been his end, but now things were opening out beyond his end, and particularly this giddy whirl up above there. He was a discoverer and he had discovered. But he was not a flying man, and it was only now that he was beginning to perceive clearly that he was expected to fly. Yet, however much the thing was present in his mind he gave no expression to it until the very end, and meanwhile he went to and fro from Banghurst’s magnificent laboratories, and was interviewed and lionised, and wore good clothes, and ate good food, and lived in an elegant flat, enjoying a very abundant feast of such good, coarse, wholesome fame and success as a man, starved for all his years as he had been starved, might be reasonably expected to enjoy.

===Chinese===
显然，早年的研究生涯里，他从未掂量过飞行这一份义务；机器曾是他追求的终点，可如今事情正在终点之外铺展开来，尤其是头顶上那阵令人眩晕的盘旋。他是发现者，而且他已有所发现。可他并不是一个飞人，直到此时他才开始清楚地意识到，别人指望他去飞。然而，不管这件事在他心头压得多么重，直到最后一刻他都未露半句口风，与此同时，他在班赫斯特那气派的实验室之间进进出出，被人采访、被人奉若上宾，穿着讲究的衣裳，吃着讲究的饮食，住在一套雅致的公寓里，尽情享受着这样一场丰盛宴席——一场又好又粗鄙又健康的声名与成功之宴——像他这般穷饿了大半辈子的人，能这样享受一番也属情理之中。

===Original===
After a time, the weekly gatherings in Fulham ceased. The model had failed one day just for a moment to respond to Filmer’s guidance, or he had been distracted by the compliments of an archbishop. At any rate, it suddenly dug its nose into the air just a little too steeply as the archbishop was sailing through a Latin quotation for all the world like an archbishop in a book, and it came down in the Fulham Road within three yards of a bus horse. It stood for a second perhaps, astonishing and in its attitude astonished, then it crumpled, shivered into pieces, and the bus horse was incidentally killed.

Filmer lost the end of the archiepiscopal compliment. He stood up and stared as his invention swooped out of sight and reach of him. His long, white hands still gripped his useless apparatus. The archbishop followed his skyward stare with an apprehension unbecoming in an archbishop.

Then came the crash and the shouts and uproar from the road to relieve Filmer’s tension. “My God!” he whispered, and sat down.

Everyone else almost was staring to see where the machine had vanished, or rushing into the house.

===Chinese===
过了一段时间，富勒姆的每周聚会便停止了。有一天，那模型有一小会儿没有听从菲尔默的操纵，也许是他被一位大主教的恭维话分了心。总之，就在那位大主教正引经据典地吟诵一段拉丁文、活脱脱像书中走出来的大主教时，模型突然把机头朝空中翘得稍稍陡了些，接着便栽到了富勒姆路上，离一匹公共汽车的马不过三码远。它也许立了一秒钟，那姿态既令人吃惊、又显出它自己也吃了一惊，接着便垮塌下来，碎成齑粉，那匹公共汽车的马也顺带被砸死了。

大主教那句恭维话的后半截，菲尔默没有听见。他站起身，呆呆地望着自己的发明物俯冲着飞出视野、飞出他能触及的范围。他那双修长苍白的手仍紧握着那具已无用的操纵装置。大主教循着他那望向天空的目光也望上去，神情里带着一种与一位大主教身份不符的忧虑。

紧接着，传来了坠毁的声响，路上响起一片叫喊和骚动——倒让菲尔默那根紧绷的弦松了下来。"我的天！"他低声说，坐了下来。

其余的人几乎都在盯着看那架机器消失在何处，或者慌忙往屋里跑。

===Original===
The making of the big machine progressed all the more rapidly for this. Over its making presided Filmer, always a little slow and very careful in his manner, always with a growing preoccupation in his mind. His care over the strength and soundness of the apparatus was prodigious. The slightest doubt, and he delayed everything until the doubtful part could be replaced. Wilkinson, his senior assistant, fumed at some of these delays, which, he insisted, were for the most part unnecessary. Banghurst magnified the patient certitude of Filmer in the *New Paper*, and reviled it bitterly to his wife, and MacAndrew, the second assistant, approved Filmer’s wisdom. “We’re not wanting a fiasco, man,” said MacAndrew. “He’s perfectly well advised.”

And whenever an opportunity arose Filmer would expound to Wilkinson and MacAndrew just exactly how every part of the flying machine was to be controlled and worked, so that in effect they would be just as capable, and even more capable, when at last the time came, of guiding it through the skies.

===Chinese===
大型机器的制造反倒因此进行得更快了。主持其事的是菲尔默，他举止间永远带着那种慢条斯理和小心翼翼，心头则永远压着一份与日俱增的挂虑。他对装置的坚固与牢靠的考究到了惊人的地步。一丝一毫的疑虑，他便让一切停顿，直到可疑的那一部分被换掉为止。他的高级助手威尔金森（Wilkinson）对其中一些耽搁大为光火，坚称它们大多是多余的。班赫斯特在《新报》上盛赞菲尔默那份耐心的笃定，私底下却对他妻子破口大骂，而二助手麦克安德鲁（MacAndrew）则赞同菲尔默的明智。"咱们可不想砸锅，老兄，"麦克安德鲁说，"他这么做完全在理。"

而一有机会，菲尔默便会对威尔金森和麦克安德鲁详尽讲解，飞行机器的每一个部分究竟该如何操纵、如何运转，以使那一刻最终到来时，他们事实上能与之同样熟练、甚至更为熟练地驾着它穿云破雾。

===Original===
Now I should imagine that if Filmer had seen fit at this stage to define just what he was feeling, and to take a definite line in the matter of his ascent, he might have escaped that painful ordeal quite easily. If he had had it clearly in his mind he could have done endless things. He would surely have found no difficulty with a specialist to demonstrate a weak heart, or something gastric or pulmonary, to stand in his way﻿—that is the line I am astonished he did not take﻿—or he might, had he been man enough, have declared simply and finally that he did not intend to do the thing. But the fact is, though the dread was hugely present in his mind, the thing was by no means sharp and clear. I fancy that all through this period he kept telling himself that when the occasion came he would find himself equal to it. He was like a man just gripped by a great illness, who says he feels a little out of sorts, and expects to be better presently. Meanwhile he delayed the completion of the machine, and let the assumption that he was going to fly it take root and flourish exceedingly about him. He even accepted anticipatory compliments on his courage. And, barring this secret squeamishness, there can be no doubt he found all the praise and distinction and fuss he got a delightful and even intoxicating draught.

===Chinese===
照我想，如果菲尔默在这个节骨眼上肯把自己心里的感觉讲清楚、对升空一事摆出一个明确的立场，他完全可以轻而易举地躲过那场痛苦的考验。只要他把事情在心中理清，他大可有许多办法。找一位专科医生证明他心脏虚弱，或胃、或肺有什么毛病来挡驾，谅必对他毫不费力——这条路他没走，倒令我惊讶——又或者，他若够男子气，本可以直截了当、一了百了地宣布他不打算做这件事。可事实是，尽管那恐惧在他心头沉沉地压着，那件事在他心中却绝非清晰鲜明。我猜想，整个这段时间里他一直在对自己说，到时候他总归能应付得来。他就像一个刚被一场大病攫住的人，嘴里说着只是有点不舒服，盼着一会儿就好。与此同时，他拖延着机器的完工，任由"他要去驾驶它"这一假设在他周围生根、疯长。他甚至领受了别人对他勇气的预贺之词。而且，撇开这份秘而不宣的怯意不谈，他所得到的所有赞颂、殊荣与殷勤，无疑是他甘之如饴、乃至为之飘飘然的一杯美酒。

===Original===
The Lady Mary Elkinghorn made things a little more complicated for him.

How *that* began was a subject of inexhaustible speculation to Hicks. Probably in the beginning she was just a little “nice” to him with that impartial partiality of hers, and it may be that to her eyes, standing out conspicuously as he did ruling his monster in the upper air, he had a distinction that Hicks was not disposed to find. And somehow they must have had a moment of sufficient isolation, and the great discoverer a moment of sufficient courage for something just a little personal to be mumbled or blurted. However it began, there is no doubt that it did begin, and presently became quite perceptible to a world accustomed to find in the proceedings of the Lady Mary Elkinghorn a matter of entertainment. It complicated things, because the state of love in such a virgin mind as Filmer’s would brace his resolution, if not sufficiently, at any rate considerably towards facing a danger he feared, and hampered him in such attempts at evasion as would otherwise be natural and congenial.

===Chinese===
玛丽·埃尔金霍恩小姐则让事情对他来说更复杂了几分。

这事是*怎么*开的头，是希克斯永远猜不厌的一道谜。也许一开始，她不过是带着她那种不分亲疏的偏宠，对他稍稍"客气"了一些；而在她眼中，他那样醒目地凌空御着那头巨兽，身上也许有着希克斯不肯承认的一种非凡气度。他们总该有过那么一阵子足够独处的时刻，而这位大发现者也总该有过那么一阵子足够的勇气，含混或冒失地说出了一句半句私己的话。无论它是怎么起的头，总之它确实起了头，而且不久就被世人察觉了——这世人对从玛丽·埃尔金霍恩小姐的行事中看出些消遣来早已习以为常。它把事情搞复杂了，因为在菲尔默这样一张白纸般的心里，恋爱的状态会给他以激励——纵然不足以完全战胜、至少也大大加强了他去面对自己所畏惧危险时的决心，同时也妨碍了他那种原本会顺理成章、出于天性去回避的种种图谋。

===Original===
It remains a matter for speculation just how the Lady Mary felt for Filmer and just what she thought of him. At thirty-eight one may have gathered much wisdom and still be not altogether wise, and the imagination still functions actively enough in creating glamours and effecting the impossible. He came before her eyes as a very central man, and that always counts, and he had powers, unique powers as it seemed, at any rate in the air. The performance with the model had just a touch of the quality of a potent incantation, and women have ever displayed an unreasonable disposition to imagine that when a man has powers he must necessarily have power. Given so much, and what was not good in Filmer’s manner and appearance became an added merit. He was modest, he hated display, but given an occasion where *true* qualities are needed, then﻿—then one would see!

The late Mrs. Bampton thought it wise to convey to Lady Mary her opinion that Filmer, all things considered, was rather a “grub.” “He’s certainly not a sort of man I have ever met before,” said the Lady Mary, with a quite unruffled serenity. And Mrs. Bampton, after a swift, imperceptible glance at that serenity, decided that so far as saying anything to Lady Mary went, she had done as much as could be expected of her. But she said a great deal to other people.

===Chinese===
玛丽小姐究竟对菲尔默怀有怎样的情感、究竟如何看待他，至今仍是可供揣摩之事。三十八岁的人，阅历的智慧已积了不少，却仍未必全然明智；而想象力也还活跃得很，足以凭空造出光环、做成不可能之事。在她眼中，他是个居于核心地位的人物——这一点永远作数——而且他拥有才能，看来是独一无二的才能，至少在天上如此。操纵模型的那一番表演，恰带着几分强力咒语般的意味，而女人们向来有一种不讲道理的倾向，以为一个男人有了才能，便必然有了力量。既然承认了这一层，菲尔默风度与外表上那些不讨喜之处，反倒成了加分的优点。他谦逊，他不爱张扬，但只要遇到需要*真正*品质的场合，那时——那时人们便会刮目相看！

已故的班普顿夫人（Mrs. Bampton）认为，自己有责任让玛丽小姐知道她的看法：通盘算来，菲尔默不过是只"土鳖"。"他确实不是我曾见过的那种男人。"玛丽小姐说，神态从容不迫，毫无波澜。班普顿夫人飞快地、不易察觉地瞥了一眼这份从容，便断定：就向玛丽小姐进言这件事而言，自己已尽到了本分。可到了别人面前，她的话可就多了。

===Original===
And at last, without any undue haste or unseemliness, the day dawned, the great day, when Banghurst had promised his public﻿—the world in fact﻿—that flying should be finally attained and overcome. Filmer saw it dawn, watched even in the darkness before it dawned, watched its stars fade and the grey and pearly pinks give place at last to the clear blue sky of a sunny, cloudless day. He watched it from the window of his bedroom in the new-built wing of Banghurst’s Tudor house. And as the stars were overwhelmed and the shapes and substances of things grew into being out of the amorphous dark, he must have seen more and more distinctly the festive preparations beyond the beech clumps near the green pavilion in the outer park, the three stands for the privileged spectators, the raw, new fencing of the enclosure, the sheds and workshops, the Venetian masts and fluttering flags that Banghurst had considered essential, black and limp in the breezeless dawn, and amidst all these things a great shape covered with tarpauling. A strange and terrible portent for humanity was that shape, a beginning that must surely spread and widen and change and dominate all the affairs of men, but to Filmer it is very doubtful whether it appeared in anything but a narrow and personal light. Several people heard him pacing in the small hours﻿—for the vast place was packed with guests by a proprietor editor who, before all understood compression. And about five o’clock, if not before, Filmer left his room and wandered out of the sleeping house into the park, alive by that time with sunlight and birds and squirrels and the fallow deer. MacAndrew, who was also an early riser, met him near the machine, and they went and had a look at it together.

===Chinese===
终于，没有半点仓促或不妥，这一天破晓了——那个大日子，那个班赫斯特已向他的读者、事实上是向全世界承诺过的日子：飞行终将被实现、被征服。菲尔默眼看着天亮，甚至在天亮之前的黑暗中就守望着，看着星星隐去，看着灰白与珠光般的粉红终于让位于晴朗无云的一天那澄澈的蓝天。他是从班赫斯特那幢都铎式宅邸新建侧楼里自己卧室的窗前望见这一切的。当星辉被吞没、万物从混沌的黑暗中显出形与体的时候，他一定越来越清楚地望见了外园绿亭附近那几丛山毛榉树之外、为庆典做的种种布置：三座供特权观众落座的看台、围场上还崭新的栅栏、一座座棚屋和工场、班赫斯特认为必不可少的威尼斯式旗杆和飘扬的旗帜——在这无风的黎明里都黑黢黢、软塌塌地垂着；而在这一切之间，是一个蒙着防水油布的巨大形体。对人类而言，那个形体是一种奇异而可怕的征兆，一个必将蔓延、扩张、改变并主宰人类一切事务的开端；但对菲尔默来说，它究竟是否还以除了狭隘而个人的角度之外的任何面目出现在他眼前，却很可怀疑。后半夜里有几个人听见他在踱步——因为这位身兼老板的主编最懂得"压缩"之道，把这偌大的宅子塞满了客人。大约五点钟，也许更早，菲尔默便离开了房间，从沉睡的宅子里溜出来，走进了庄园——此时园中已充满阳光、鸟鸣、松鼠和黇鹿。同样惯于早起的麦克安德鲁，在机器附近撞见了他，两人便一同过去看了看它。

===Original===
It is doubtful if Filmer took any breakfast, in spite of the urgency of Banghurst. So soon as the guests began to be about in some number he seems to have retreated to his room. Thence about ten he went into the shrubbery, very probably because he had seen the Lady Mary Elkinghorn there. She was walking up and down, engaged in conversation with her old school friend, Mrs. Brewis-Craven, and although Filmer had never met the latter lady before, he joined them and walked beside them for some time. There were several silences in spite of the Lady Mary’s brilliance. The situation was a difficult one, and Mrs. Brewis-Craven did not master its difficulty. “He struck me,” she said afterwards with a luminous self-contradiction, “as a very unhappy person who had something to say, and wanted before all things to be helped to say it. But how was one to help him when one didn’t know what it was?”

===Chinese===
菲尔默有没有吃早餐，很可怀疑，尽管班赫斯特百般催促。客人们刚一开始三五成群地出现，他似乎便退回了自己的房间。十点钟左右，他从那里走进了灌木林，很可能是他看见了玛丽·埃尔金霍恩小姐在那儿。她正与昔日的同窗好友布鲁伊斯-克雷文夫人（Mrs. Brewis-Craven）一边踱步一边交谈；虽然菲尔默从前没有见过这位夫人，他还是加入了她们，在她们身旁同行了一阵。尽管玛丽小姐谈吐依旧机智妙语连珠，其间却有好几次沉默。场面是棘手的，而布鲁伊斯-克雷文夫人并未能驾驭其中的棘手。"他给我的印象，"她事后说，话语间有一种一目了然的自我矛盾，"是一个极不快乐、有话要说、而最盼望有人帮他说出来的人。可是人家既然不知道他要说什么，又怎么帮得了他呢？"

===Original===
At half-past eleven the enclosures for the public in the outer park were crammed, there was an intermittent stream of equipages along the belt which circles the outer park, and the house party was dotted over the lawn and shrubbery and the corner of the inner park, in a series of brilliantly attired knots, all making for the flying machine. Filmer walked in a group of three with Banghurst, who was supremely and conspicuously happy, and Sir Theodore Hickle, the president of the Aeronautical Society. Mrs. Banghurst was close behind with the Lady Mary Elkinghorn, Georgina Hickle, and the Dean of Stays. Banghurst was large and copious in speech, and such interstices as he left were filled in by Hickle with complimentary remarks to Filmer. And Filmer walked between them saying not a word except by way of unavoidable reply. Behind, Mrs. Banghurst listened to the admirably suitable and shapely conversation of the Dean with that fluttered attention to the ampler clergy ten years of social ascent and ascendency had not cured in her; and the Lady Mary watched, no doubt with an entire confidence in the world’s disillusionment, the drooping shoulders of the sort of man she had never met before.

===Chinese===
十一点半，外园里向公众开放的围场已经挤得水泄不通，沿外园四周那条环形车道，车马如流水般时断时续；而宅邸招待的客人们则三五成群、衣着鲜丽地散布在草坪、灌木林和内园一角，一簇一簇的，都朝飞行机器那边走去。菲尔默与班赫斯特、航空协会主席西奥多·希克尔爵士（Sir Theodore Hickle）三人同行；班赫斯特喜气洋洋、格外惹眼。班赫斯特夫人紧跟在后，与玛丽·埃尔金霍恩小姐、乔治娜·希克尔（Georgina Hickle）和斯特伊斯教长（the Dean of Stays）走在一起。班赫斯特说话滔滔不绝、气派宏大，他所留下的那些间隙，则由希克尔用对菲尔默的恭维话填满。菲尔默走在两人之间，除了不可避免的应答之外一言不发。后面，班赫斯特夫人怀着一种惴惴不安的虔敬，倾听着教长那番极为得体、工稳的谈吐——十年间社交上的攀升与发号施令，并未把她对体貌丰腴的教士所怀的这份惶恐从她身上治好；而玛丽小姐望着那一双耷拉的肩膀——那种她从未见过的男人的肩膀——无疑怀着对世人终将幻灭的十足信心。

===Original===
There was some cheering as the central party came into view of the enclosures, but it was not very unanimous nor invigorating cheering. They were within fifty yards of the apparatus when Filmer took a hasty glance over his shoulder to measure the distance of the ladies behind them, and decided to make the first remark he had initiated since the house had been left. His voice was just a little hoarse, and he cut in on Banghurst in mid-sentence on Progress.

“I say, Banghurst,” he said, and stopped.

“Yes,” said Banghurst.

“I wish﻿—” He moistened his lips. “I’m not feeling well.”

Banghurst stopped dead. “Eh?” he shouted.

“A queer feeling.” Filmer made to move on, but Banghurst was immovable. “I don’t know. I may be better in a minute. If not﻿—perhaps … MacAndrew﻿—”

“You’re not feeling *well*?” said Banghurst, and stared at his white face.

“My dear!” he said, as Mrs. Banghurst came up with them, “Filmer says he isn’t feeling *well*.”

“A little queer,” exclaimed Filmer, avoiding the Lady Mary’s eyes. “It may pass off﻿—”

There was a pause.

It came to Filmer that he was the most isolated person in the world.

===Chinese===
当中央这一行人走进围场观众的视线时，响起了一些欢呼声，但并不怎么整齐，也没什么劲头。他们离装置已不足五十码，这时菲尔默匆匆回头瞥了一眼，估量了一下后面几位女士的距离，决定主动开口——这是他自从出了宅子以来头一回自己起头说话。他的嗓音略带沙哑，打断了班赫斯特正讲在兴头上关于"进步"的高谈阔论。

"我说，班赫斯特，"他说，又顿住了。

"嗯？"班赫斯特说。

"我希望——"他舔了舔嘴唇，"我感觉不大舒服。"

班赫斯特猛地站住了。"啊？"他嚷了一声。

"一种怪怪的感觉。"菲尔默想继续往前走，可班赫斯特纹丝不动。"我也说不清。也许一会儿就好了。要是不好的话——也许……麦克安德鲁——"

你"不大*舒服*"？班赫斯特说着，盯着他苍白的脸。

"亲爱的！"班赫斯特夫人赶上他们时，他喊道，"菲尔默说他不大*舒服*。"

"有点怪怪的，"菲尔默说，避开了玛丽小姐的眼睛，"也许一会儿就过去了——"

一阵沉默。

菲尔默忽然想到，自己是世上最孤独的人。

===Original===
“In any case,” said Banghurst, “the ascent must be made. Perhaps if you were to sit down somewhere for a moment﻿—”

“It’s the crowd, I think,” said Filmer.

There was a second pause. Banghurst’s eye rested in scrutiny on Filmer, and then swept the sample of public in the enclosure.

“It’s unfortunate,” said Sir Theodore Hickle; “but still﻿—I suppose﻿—Your assistants﻿—Of course, if you feel out of condition and disinclined﻿—”

“I don’t think Mr. Filmer would permit *that* for a moment,” said Lady Mary.

“But if Mr. Filmer’s nerve is run﻿—It might even be dangerous for him to attempt﻿—” Hickle coughed.

“It’s just because it’s dangerous,” began the Lady Mary, and felt she had made her point of view and Filmer’s plain enough.

Conflicting motives struggled for Filmer.

“I feel I ought to go up,” he said, regarding the ground. He looked up and met the Lady Mary’s eyes. “I want to go up,” he said, and smiled whitely at her. He turned towards Banghurst. “If I could just sit down somewhere for a moment out of the crowd and sun﻿—”

Banghurst, at least, was beginning to understand the case. “Come into my little room in the green pavilion,” he said. “It’s quite cool there.” He took Filmer by the arm.

Filmer turned his face to the Lady Mary Elkinghorn again. “I shall be all right in five minutes,” he said. “I’m tremendously sorry﻿—”

The Lady Mary Elkinghorn smiled at him. “I couldn’t think﻿—” he said to Hickle, and obeyed the compulsion of Banghurst’s pull.

===Chinese===
"无论如何，"班赫斯特说，"升空得照常进行。也许您到哪儿坐下歇一会儿——"

"我想，是人太多了。"菲尔默说。

又是一阵沉默。班赫斯特的目光审视地停在菲尔默身上，然后扫向围场里那一小撮作为样品的公众。

"真不凑巧，"西奥多·希克尔爵士说，"不过——我想——您的助手们——当然，如果您觉得身体不适、不情愿的话——"

"我想菲尔默先生一刻也不会答应*那样*做。"玛丽小姐说。

"可要是菲尔默先生的勇气已经支撑不住——他若勉强尝试，甚至可能有危险——"希克尔咳了一声。

"正因为危险，"玛丽小姐开口说道，便觉得自己和菲尔默的立场已表达得够清楚了。

相互冲突的动机在菲尔默心中搏斗。

"我觉得我应当上去，"他说，眼睛盯着地面。他抬起头，迎上玛丽小姐的目光。"我要上去，"他说，冲她惨然一笑。他转向班赫斯特。"要是我能找地方坐下歇一会儿，避开这些人和日头——"

至少班赫斯特开始明白了这是怎么回事。"到我绿亭里那间小屋去吧，"他说，"那儿挺凉快。"他挽住菲尔默的胳膊。

菲尔默又把脸转向玛丽·埃尔金霍恩小姐。"我五分钟就好，"他说，"真是对不住极了——"

玛丽·埃尔金霍恩小姐冲他微微一笑。"我简直想不通——"他对希克尔说，便顺从了班赫斯特的拉扯。

===Original===
The rest remained watching the two recede.

“He is so fragile,” said the Lady Mary.

“He’s certainly a highly nervous type,” said the Dean, whose weakness it was to regard the whole world, except married clergymen with enormous families, as “neurotic.”

“Of course,” said Hickle, “it isn’t absolutely necessary for him to go up because he has invented﻿—”

“How *could* he avoid it?” asked the Lady Mary, with the faintest shadow of scorn.

“It’s certainly most unfortunate if he’s going to be ill now,” said Mrs. Banghurst a little severely.

“He’s not going to be ill,” said the Lady Mary, and certainly she had met Filmer’s eye.

“You’ll be all right,” said Banghurst, as they went towards the pavilion. “All you want is a nip of brandy. It ought to be you, you know. You’ll be﻿—you’d get it rough, you know, if you let another man﻿—”

“Oh, I want to go,” said Filmer. “I shall be all right. As a matter of fact I’m almost inclined *now*﻿—. No! I think I’ll have that nip of brandy first.”

===Chinese===
余下的人站在原地，望着那两人渐渐走远。

"他太脆弱了。"玛丽小姐说。

"他无疑属于高度神经质的类型。"教长说。他的毛病，就是把除了拖儿带女的已婚教士之外的全世界都视作"神经质"。

"当然，"希克尔说，"并不因为是他发明的，就非得他亲自上去不可——"

"他怎么能*不*上去呢？"玛丽小姐反问，带着一缕极淡的轻蔑。

"要是他偏偏这时候病了，那真是太不凑巧了。"班赫斯特夫人说，语气有点严厉。

"他不会病的。"玛丽小姐说——她无疑是与菲尔默对上了眼神的。

"你没事的，"他们朝绿亭走去时班赫斯特说，"你只是要呷一口白兰地。这件事本该你自己来，你明白。你要是——你要是让别的男人代你——你可就难堪了，你知道——"

"噢，我要去，"菲尔默说，"我没事的。其实我现在几乎都有点*想*——不！我想先呷那口白兰地。"

===Original===
Banghurst took him into the little room and routed out an empty decanter. He departed in search of a supply. He was gone perhaps five minutes.

The history of those five minutes cannot be written. At intervals Filmer’s face could be seen by the people on the easternmost of the stands erected for spectators, against the window pane peering out, and then it would recede and fade. Banghurst vanished shouting behind the grand stand, and presently the butler appeared going pavilionward with a tray.

===Chinese===
班赫斯特把他带进那间小屋，翻出一只空酒瓶。他走出去找酒。他大约离开了五分钟。

这五分钟的历史无从落笔。在最东边那座看台上的观众，时不时能看见菲尔默的脸贴着窗玻璃朝外张望，随即又退回去、隐没了。班赫斯特在大看台后面喊着什么不见了踪影，不久，管家端着托盘朝绿亭走来。

===Original===
The apartment in which Filmer came to his last solution was a pleasant little room very simply furnished with green furniture and an old bureau﻿—for Banghurst was simple in all his private ways. It was hung with little engravings after Morland and it had a shelf of books. But as it happened, Banghurst had left a rook rifle he sometimes played with on the top of the desk, and on the corner of the mantelshelf was a tin with three or four cartridges remaining in it. As Filmer went up and down that room wrestling with his intolerable dilemma he went first towards the neat little rifle athwart the blotting-pad and then towards the neat little red label

> “.22 long.”

The thing must have jumped into his mind in a moment.

===Chinese===
菲尔默作出最后决断的那间屋子，是一间宜人的小房间，陈设十分简单：几件绿色的家具，一张旧写字台——因为班赫斯特私下的一切排场都很简朴。墙上挂着几幅临摹莫兰（Morland）的小版画，还有一个书架。可巧，班赫斯特把他偶尔把玩的一杆打鸟步枪留在了书桌顶上，壁炉架的一角搁着一只小铁罐，里面还剩三四发子弹。菲尔默在屋里来回踱步，与那无法忍受的两难苦苦搏斗，他一会儿走向横在吸墨纸上那杆齐整的小步枪，一会儿走向那张齐整的红色小标签——

> ".22 口径长弹。"

这个念头，一定是一瞬间跳进他脑海的。

===Original===
Nobody seems to have connected the report with him, though the gun, being fired in a confined space, must have sounded loud, and there were several people in the billiard-room, separated from him only by a lath-and-plaster partition. But directly Banghurst’s butler opened the door and smelt the sour smell of the smoke, he knew, he says, what had happened. For the servants at least of Banghurst’s household had guessed something of what was going on in Filmer’s mind.

===Chinese===
似乎没有人把那声枪响与他联系起来，尽管枪是在密闭空间里开的，声音一定很大，而且台球室里就有几个人，与他只隔着一堵板条抹灰的墙。但班赫斯特的管家一打开门，闻到那股烟的酸涩味，他说，他就知道出了什么事。因为班赫斯特宅子里的仆人们，至少已隐约猜到菲尔默心里在翻腾些什么。

===Original===
All through that trying afternoon Banghurst behaved as he held a man should behave in the presence of hopeless disaster, and his guests for the most part succeeded in not insisting upon the fact﻿—though to conceal their perception of it altogether was impossible﻿—that Banghurst had been pretty elaborately and completely swindled by the deceased. The public in the enclosure, Hicks told me, dispersed “like a party that has been ducking a welsher,” and there wasn’t a soul in the train to London, it seems, who hadn’t known all along that flying was a quite impossible thing for man. “But he might have tried it,” said many, “after carrying the thing so far.”

In the evening, when he was comparatively alone, Banghurst broke down and went on like a man of clay. I have been told he wept, which must have made an imposing scene, and he certainly said Filmer had ruined his life, and offered and sold the whole apparatus to MacAndrew for half-a-crown. “I’ve been thinking﻿—” said MacAndrew at the conclusion of the bargain, and stopped.

===Chinese===
整个那个难熬的下午，班赫斯特表现得正如他所认为的一个男人在无可挽回的灾难面前应有的样子；他的客人们多半也做到了不去点破那件事——尽管想完全装作没看穿是不可能的——那就是：班赫斯特已被死者相当精心、相当彻底地涮了一道。据希克斯告诉我，围场里的观众散得"像一群刚刚把赖账者浸过水之后散去的人"，而开往伦敦的火车上，似乎没有一个人不是早就知道：飞行对人类来说根本就是不可能的事。"可他既然把事情做到这一步了，"许多人说，"总该试一试啊。"

到了晚上，身边比较没人的时候，班赫斯特垮了下来，举止像个没了血气的泥人。有人告诉我，他哭了——那场面一定颇为壮观——他确实说菲尔默毁了他的一生，并以半克朗的价钱把整套装置作价卖给了麦克安德鲁。"我一直在想——"麦克安德鲁在成交之后说，又顿住了。

===Original===
The next morning the name of Filmer was, for the first time, less conspicuous in the *New Paper* than in any other daily paper in the world. The rest of the world’s instructors, with varying emphasis, according to their dignity and the degree of competition between themselves and the *New Paper*, proclaimed the “Entire Failure of the New Flying Machine,” and “Suicide of the Impostor.” But in the district of North Surrey the reception of the news was tempered by a perception of unusual aerial phenomena.

===Chinese===
第二天早上，菲尔默这个名字头一次在《新报》上比全世界任何一家日报都更不显眼。世上其他的舆论导师们，根据各自的体面程度和与《新报》竞争的激烈程度，以不同语气宣告了"新飞行机器彻底失败"和"骗子自杀"。但在北萨里地区，这一消息的传来，却因人们察觉到一些异常的空中现象而有所缓和。

===Original===
Overnight Wilkinson and MacAndrew had fallen into violent argument on the exact motives of their principal’s rash act.

“The man was certainly a poor, cowardly body, but so far as his science went he was *no* impostor,” said MacAndrew, “and I’m prepared to give that proposition a very practical demonstration, Mr. Wilkinson, so soon as we’ve got the place a little more to ourselves. For I’ve no faith in all this publicity for experimental trials.”

And to that end, while all the world was reading of the certain failure of the new flying machine, MacAndrew was soaring and curvetting with great amplitude and dignity over the Epsom and Wimbledon divisions; and Banghurst, restored once more to hope and energy, and regardless of public security and the Board of Trade, was pursuing his gyrations and trying to attract his attention, on a motor car and in his pyjamas﻿—he had caught sight of the ascent when pulling up the blind of his bedroom window﻿—equipped, among other things, with a film camera that was subsequently discovered to be jammed. And Filmer was lying on the billiard table in the green pavilion with a sheet about his body.

===Chinese===
头天夜里，威尔金森和麦克安德鲁曾为他们这位东家鲁莽之举的确切动机大吵了一架。

"这人确实是个可怜的胆小鬼，可就他的科学而言，他绝不是*骗子*，"麦克安德鲁说，"威尔金森先生，只要这地方稍微清静些、归咱们自己用，我就准备给这个论断一个非常实际的演示。因为我压根儿不信这种大庭广众之下的试验。"

为此，当全世界正在读着新飞行机器注定失败的消息时，麦克安德鲁正大幅度而庄严地翱翔、腾跃于埃普索姆（Epsom）和温布尔登（Wimbledon）两片选区的上空；而班赫斯特，又一次恢复了希望和干劲，不顾公共安全和贸易委员会，正坐着汽车、穿着睡衣——他在拉开卧室窗帘时瞥见了这次升空——追着麦克安德鲁的盘旋，想引起他的注意；车上还配备着一架电影摄影机，事后发现这架机器卡住了没拍成。而菲尔默，正躺在绿亭那张台球桌上，身上盖着一条床单。

## In the Abyss / 在深渊中

===Original===
The lieutenant stood in front of the steel sphere and gnawed a piece of pine splinter. "What do you think of it, Steevens?" he asked.
"It's an idea," said Steevens, in the tone of one who keeps an open mind.
"I believe it will smash—flat," said the lieutenant.
"He seems to have calculated it all out pretty well," said Steevens, still impartial.
"But think of the pressure," said the lieutenant. "At the surface of the water it's fourteen pounds to the inch, thirty feet down it's double that; sixty, treble; ninety, four times; nine hundred, forty times; five thousand, three hundred—that's a mile—it's two hundred and forty times fourteen pounds; that's—let's see—thirty hundredweight—a ton and a half, Steevens; *a ton and a half* to the square inch. And the ocean where he's going is five miles deep. That's seven and a half—"
"Sounds a lot," said Steevens, "but it's jolly thick steel."
The lieutenant made no answer, but resumed his pine splinter. The object of their conversation was a huge ball of steel, having an exterior diameter of perhaps nine feet. It looked like the shot for some titanic piece of artillery. It was elaborately nested in a monstrous scaffolding built into the framework of the vessel, and the gigantic spars that were presently to sling it overboard gave the stern of the ship an appearance that had raised the curiosity of every decent sailor who had sighted it, from the Pool of London to the Tropic of Capricorn. In two places, one above the other, the steel gave place to a couple of circular windows of enormously thick glass, and one of these, set in a steel frame of great solidity, was now partially unscrewed. Both the men had seen the interior of this globe for the first time that morning. It was elaborately padded with air cushions, with little studs sunk between bulging pillows to work the simple mechanism of the affair. Everything was elaborately padded, even the Myers apparatus which was to absorb carbonic acid and replace the oxygen inspired by its tenant, when he had crept in by the glass manhole, and had been screwed in. It was so elaborately padded that a man might have been fired from a gun in it with perfect safety. And it had need to be, for presently a man was to crawl in through that glass manhole, to be screwed up tightly, and to be flung overboard, and to sink down—down—down, for five miles, even as the lieutenant said. It had taken the strongest hold of his imagination; it made him a bore at mess; and he found Steevens, the new arrival aboard, a godsend to talk to about it, over and over again.

===Chinese===
中尉站在那只钢球前面，嘴里嚼着一根松木片。"你看这事怎么样，斯蒂文斯（Steevens）？"他问。
"算是个主意吧。"斯蒂文斯说，那语气活像个暂且还不下定论的人。
"依我看它会压瘪——扁扁的。"中尉说。
"他好像把一切都算得相当周全了。"斯蒂文斯说，仍然不偏不倚。
"可你想想那压力吧，"中尉说，"在水面上是每平方英寸十四磅，三十英尺下去翻一番，六十英尺三倍，九十英尺四倍，九百英尺四十倍；五千三百英尺——也就是一英里——便是十四磅的两百四十倍；那就是——让我算算——三十英担——一吨半呐，斯蒂文斯；每平方英寸一吨半。而他要下去的那片海域深五英里。那就是七吨半——"
"听上去是不少，"斯蒂文斯说，"可那钢板也厚实得很呐。"
中尉没有回话，只重新叼起他那根松木片。他俩议论的对象，是一只巨大的钢球，外径大约九英尺。它看上去像是一门史无前例的巨炮所用的炮弹。它被精心地嵌在一座庞大的支架里，支架搭进了船体的骨架；那几根稍后就要把它吊出去抛下海的巨型桅杆，使船尾显得奇形怪状，从伦敦池（Pool of London）到南回归线（Tropic of Capricorn），一路上凡是见过它的稍懂行的水手，无一不好奇。钢球上有两处，一上一下，钢板让位于两块厚得惊人的圆形玻璃窗；其中一块嵌在一个极其坚固的钢框里，此刻已被拧开了一部分。这两个人都是当天早上才头一回看见这圆球的内部。里头精心衬着一层层的气垫，鼓鼓的枕头之间嵌着小按钮，用来操纵这玩意儿那简单的机关。样样东西都裹得严严实实，连那台迈尔斯装置（Myers apparatus）也是——这台装置是用来吸收碳酸气，并补充舱中人所消耗的氧气的，等人从玻璃舱口钻进去、被拧紧密封，它便开始工作。这衬垫厚实到了这般地步：便是把人装在里头从大炮发射出去，也安然无恙。它也确有必要如此，因为再过一会儿，就要有一个人从那个玻璃舱口爬进去，被严严实实地拧紧密封，被抛下海去，往下沉、沉、沉，一直沉上五英里，正像中尉所说的那样。这件事攫住了他的想象力，令他着迷得难以自拔；他在餐桌上已经成了个惹人厌的碎嘴子；好不容易船上新来了个斯蒂文斯，他便当真视若天赐的听众，可以一遍又一遍地谈论此事。

===Original===
"It's my opinion," said the lieutenant, "that that glass will simply bend in and bulge and smash, under a pressure of that sort. Daubrée has made rocks run like water under big pressures—and, you mark my words—"
"If the glass did break in," said Steevens, "what then?"
"The water would shoot in like a jet of iron. Have you ever felt a straight jet of high pressure water? It would hit as hard as a bullet. It would simply smash him and flatten him. It would tear down his throat, and into his lungs; it would blow in his ears—"
"What a detailed imagination you have!" protested Steevens, who saw things vividly.
"It's a simple statement of the inevitable," said the lieutenant.
"And the globe?"
"Would just give out a few little bubbles, and it would settle down comfortably against the day of judgment, among the oozes and the bottom clay—with poor Elstead spread over his own smashed cushions like butter over bread."
He repeated this sentence as though he liked it very much. "Like butter over bread," he said.

===Chinese===
"依我看呀，"中尉说，"在那样的压力下，那块玻璃只会往里凹、鼓胀，然后碎裂。多布雷（Daubrée）曾在极大的压力下让岩石像水一样流动——你记着我的话——"
"万一玻璃真给压碎了，"斯蒂文斯问，"那会怎样？"
"水会像一道铁柱似的射进来。你挨过高压水柱直直一冲吗？那劲头跟子弹一样硬。它会把里头那人当场砸烂、压扁。它会灌进他的喉咙，钻进他的肺；它会从他耳朵里灌进去——"
"你的想象力可真够细致的！"斯蒂文斯抗议道，他这人一向把事情想得栩栩如生。
"我不过是把不可避免的事直说出来罢了。"中尉说。
"那这圆球呢？"
"也只是冒上几个小气泡，舒舒服服地沉到海底的淤泥和黏土里去，安然等到审判日那一天——而可怜的埃尔斯特德（Elstead）呢，就会像面包上抹的黄油一样，平平整整地摊在他自己那堆被砸烂的衬垫上。"
他把这句话又重复了一遍，似乎十分欣赏自己这个说法。"像面包上抹的黄油。"他说。

===Original===
"Having a look at the jigger?" said a voice, and Elstead stood behind them, spick and span in white, with a cigarette between his teeth, and his eyes smiling out of the shadow of his ample hat-brim. "What's that about bread and butter, Weybridge? Grumbling as usual about the insufficient pay of naval officers? It won't be more than a day now before I start. We are to get the slings ready today. This clean sky and gentle swell is just the kind of thing for swinging off a dozen tons of lead and iron; isn't it?"
"It won't affect you much," said Weybridge.
"No. Seventy or eighty feet down, and I shall be there in a dozen seconds, there's not a particle moving, though the wind shriek itself hoarse up above, and the water lifts halfway to the clouds. No. Down there"—He moved to the side of the ship and the other two followed him. All three leant forward on their elbows and stared down into the yellow-green water.

===Chinese===
"在瞧这台新鲜玩意儿？"一个声音说道。埃尔斯特德站在他俩身后，一身白装整洁利落，嘴里叼着支香烟，眼睛从宽宽的帽檐阴影里含笑望出来。"什么面包黄油的，韦布里奇（Weybridge）？又像往常一样，抱怨海军军官的薪水不够花？不出一天我就要下去了。今天我们得把吊索备好。这样晴朗的天、这样温和的涌浪，正适合把十几吨铅和铁吊出去；是不是？"
"对你影响不大。"韦布里奇说。
"是啊。往下七八十英尺，十几秒钟我就到那儿了，上面便是风把嗓子喊哑、海水掀到半空里去，下面也纹丝不动。可不。在下面——"他走到船舷边，另外两人跟了过去。三个人都把胳膊搭在栏杆上俯身朝那黄绿色的海水望去。

===Original===
"*Peace*," said Elstead, finishing his thought aloud.
"Are you dead certain that clockwork will act?" asked Weybridge presently.
"It has worked thirty-five times," said Elstead. "It's bound to work."
"But if it doesn't?"
"Why shouldn't it?"
"I wouldn't go down in that confounded thing," said Weybridge, "for twenty thousand pounds."
"Cheerful chap you are," said Elstead, and spat sociably at a bubble below.

===Chinese===
"*宁静*。"埃尔斯特德把他这一句心里话说出了口。
"你有十足的把握那发条装置到时候会动？"韦布里奇过了一会儿问。
"它已经试过三十五次了。"埃尔斯特德说，"准没问题。"
"万一不动呢？"
"凭什么不动？"
"我才不会钻进那该死的玩意儿里下去，"韦布里奇说，"就是给我两万镑我也不干。"
"你这人可真够鼓劲儿的。"埃尔斯特德说，朝着下方一个气泡亲热地吐了口唾沫。

===Original===
"I don't understand yet how you mean to work the thing," said Steevens.
"In the first place, I'm screwed into the sphere," said Elstead, "and when I've turned the electric light off and on three times to show I'm cheerful, I'm swung out over the stern by that crane, with all those big lead sinkers slung below me. The top lead weight has a roller carrying a hundred fathoms of strong cord rolled up, and that's all that joins the sinkers to the sphere, except the slings that will be cut when the affair is dropped. We use cord rather than wire rope because it's easier to cut and more buoyant—necessary points, as you will see.
"Through each of these lead weights you notice there is a hole, and an iron rod will be run through that and will project six feet on the lower side. If that rod is rammed up from below, it knocks up a lever and sets the clockwork in motion at the side of the cylinder on which the cord winds.
"Very well. The whole affair is lowered gently into the water, and the slings are cut. The sphere floats—with the air in it, it's lighter than water—but the lead weights go down straight and the cord runs out. When the cord is all paid out, the sphere will go down too, pulled down by the cord."
"But why the cord?" asked Steevens. "Why not fasten the weights directly to the sphere?"
"Because of the smash down below. The whole affair will go rushing down, mile after mile, at a headlong pace at last. It would be knocked to pieces on the bottom if it wasn't for that cord. But the weights will hit the bottom, and directly they do, the buoyancy of the sphere will come into play. It will go on sinking slower and slower; come to a stop at last, and then begin to float upward again.
"That's where the clockwork comes in. Directly the weights smash against the sea bottom, the rod will be knocked through and will kick up the clockwork, and the cord will be rewound on the reel. I shall be lugged down to the sea bottom. There I shall stay for half an hour, with the electric light on, looking about me. Then the clockwork will release a spring knife, the cord will be cut, and up I shall rush again, like a soda-water bubble. The cord itself will help the flotation."

===Chinese===
"我还没弄明白你打算怎么操纵这玩意儿呢。"斯蒂文斯说。
"首先，我被密封在钢球里，"埃尔斯特德说，"等我先把电灯开关按上三下，好让他们看见我精神不错，就由那台吊车把我吊到船尾外头，那一大串大铅锤就吊在我下面。最上面那只铅锤上装着一个卷筒，卷着一百寻粗绳，那是把铅锤和钢球连在一起的唯一东西——除了吊索，可吊索等这玩意儿一抛下水就会被割断。我们用绳而不用铁链，是因为绳子好割，浮力也大些——这两点都是关键，你往后看就明白了。
"你看，每只铅锤里都打通了一个洞，一根铁杆会穿过洞，下端伸出六英尺。如果这根铁杆从下头往上一顶，就触发一根杠杆，启动缠绳圆筒旁边的发条装置。
"是这样。整套家伙被缓缓放下水，吊索被割断。钢球浮在水面上——里头有空气，比水轻——可那些铅锤径直下沉，绳子被放出来。绳子一放完，钢球也跟着被绳子拽着往下沉。
"可为什么要这绳子呢？"斯蒂文斯问，"为什么不直接把铅锤拴在钢球上？"
"为的是不让它到底时撞碎。整套家伙会一路狂冲而下，一英里接一英里，最后是头也不回地往下扑。要不是有这根绳子，到底就撞个粉碎了。可铅锤先撞到底，它们一撞，钢球的浮力就起了作用。它会越沉越慢，终于停住，接着开始重新往上浮。
"发条装置就是这时候派上用场的。铅锤一撞上海底，铁杆就被顶穿，触发发条，绳子又重新卷回卷筒上。我便被一路拽到海底。在那儿我会待上半个钟头，把电灯开亮，四下里看看。然后发条放开一柄弹簧刀，把绳子割断，我便又像苏打水里的气泡一样往上冲。绳子本身也能帮助浮力。"

===Original===
"And if you should chance to hit a ship?" said Weybridge.
"I should come up at such a pace, I should go clean through it," said Elstead, "like a cannon ball. You needn't worry about that."
"And suppose some nimble crustacean should wriggle into your clockwork—"
"It would be a pressing sort of invitation for me to stop," said Elstead, turning his back on the water and staring at the sphere.

===Chinese===
"万一你正好撞上一艘船呢？"韦布里奇说。
"我冲上来的那股劲头，会一下子把它穿个对穿，"埃尔斯特德说，"跟炮弹一样。这倒不用你操心。"
"再万一，哪只手脚麻利的甲壳动物钻进你的发条装置里呢——"
"那可就是一道催我留下来的请帖了。"埃尔斯特德说，转过身背对着海，盯着那钢球。

---

===Original===
They had swung Elstead overboard by eleven o'clock. The day was serenely bright and calm, with the horizon lost in haze. The electric glare in the little upper compartment beamed cheerfully three times. Then they let him down slowly to the surface of the water, and a sailor in the stern chains hung ready to cut the tackle that held the lead weights and the sphere together. The globe, which had looked so large on deck, looked the smallest thing conceivable under the stern of the ship. It rolled a little, and its two dark windows, which floated uppermost, seemed like eyes turned up in round wonderment at the people who crowded the rail. A voice wondered how Elstead liked the rolling. "Are you ready?" sang out the commander. "Ay, ay, sir!" "Then let her go!"
The rope of the tackle tightened against the blade and was cut, and an eddy rolled over the globe in a grotesquely helpless fashion. Someone waved a handkerchief, someone else tried an ineffectual cheer, a middy was counting slowly, "Eight, nine, ten!" Another roll, then with a jerk and a splash the thing righted itself.
It seemed to be stationary for a moment, to grow rapidly smaller, and then the water closed over it, and it became visible, enlarged by refraction and dimmer, below the surface. Before one could count three it had disappeared. There was a flicker of white light far down in the water, that diminished to a speck and vanished. Then there was nothing but a depth of water going down into blackness, through which a shark was swimming.

===Chinese===
到十一点钟，他们已经把埃尔斯特德吊出了船外。这一天晴朗而平静，地平线隐没在薄霭之中。上层小舱里那道电光欢快地闪了三下。随后他们缓缓把他放到水面上，船尾链旁有一名水手俯身待命，准备割断把铅锤和钢球拴在一起的绳索。这只在甲板上看着挺大的圆球，到了船尾下面便小得难以想象。它略略滚动着，浮在最上面的那两扇黑乎乎的圆窗，活像两只因惊愕而圆睁的眼睛，望着挤在船栏边的那一群人。有个声音琢磨着埃尔斯特德对这种颠簸感觉如何。"准备好了吗？"舰长高声问。"好了，长官！""那就放！"
吊绳在刀刃上一绷，被割断了，一个漩涡怪诞无助地翻过钢球。有人挥动手帕，有人试着欢呼了一声却没成气候，一名见习军官在慢慢地数："八，九，十！"又滚了一下，接着猛地一抖，扑通一响，这家伙正了过来。
它似乎停了片刻，随即迅速地缩小，然后海水合拢在它上面；透过水面看下去，它因折射而放大了些，也朦胧了些。还没等人数到三，它便消失了。深水中闪了一道白光，缩成一个小点，也没了。剩下的只是一片往黑暗中沉下去的深水，有一条鲨鱼正从中游过。

===Original===
Then suddenly the screw of the cruiser began to rotate, the water was crickled, the shark disappeared in a wrinkled confusion, and a torrent of foam rushed across the crystalline clearness that had swallowed up Elstead. "What's the idee?" said one A.B. to another.
"We're going to lay off about a couple of miles, 'fear he should hit us when he comes up," said his mate.
The ship steamed slowly to her new position. Aboard her almost everyone who was unoccupied remained watching the breathing swell into which the sphere had sunk. For the next half-hour it is doubtful if a word was spoken that did not bear directly or indirectly on Elstead. The December sun was now high in the sky, and the heat very considerable.

===Chinese===
紧接着，巡洋舰的螺旋桨猛然转动起来，水面被搅皱了，鲨鱼在一团皱巴巴的混乱里消失不见，一股泡沫的洪流冲过那片把埃尔斯特德吞下去的、水晶般清透的海水。"这是干什么？"一名一等水兵问另一名。
"咱们要开到两英里外去停着，怕他上来的时候撞上咱们。"他的同伴说。
船缓缓驶到了新的位置。船上几乎每一个没事的人都留下来盯着那片钢球沉进去的、起伏呼吸着的涌浪。接下来的半个钟头里，全船上下所说的话，怕没有一句不与埃尔斯特德直接或间接相关。十二月的太阳此刻高悬空中，热得相当可以。

===Original===
"He'll be cold enough down there," said Weybridge. "They say that below a certain depth sea water's always just about freezing."
"Where'll he come up?" asked Steevens. "I've lost my bearings."
"That's the spot," said the commander, who prided himself on his omniscience. He extended a precise finger southeastward. "And this, I reckon, is pretty nearly the moment," he said. "He's been thirty-five minutes."
"How long does it take to reach the bottom of the ocean?" asked Steevens.
"For a depth of five miles, and reckoning—as we did—an acceleration of two feet per second, both ways, is just about three-quarters of a minute."
"Then he's overdue," said Weybridge.
"Pretty nearly," said the commander. "I suppose it takes a few minutes for that cord of his to wind in."
"I forgot that," said Weybridge, evidently relieved.

===Chinese===
"他在底下可够冷的。"韦布里奇说，"人说，过了某个深度，海水就总是接近冰点了。"
"他从哪儿上来呢？"斯蒂文斯问，"我已经搞不清方位了。"
"就是那地方。"舰长说，他一向以自己无所不知为傲。他伸出一根精确的手指，指向东南方。"而这一刻嘛，"他说，"我看也差不多了。他已经下去三十五分钟了。"
"下到海底要多长时间？"斯蒂文斯问。
"按五英里的深度，照我们那样算——每秒两英尺的加速度，下去上来都算——大约四分之三分钟。"
"那他已经超时了。"韦布里奇说。
"差不离儿。"舰长说，"我看，他这绳子收进去也得花几分钟。"
"我把这茬儿给忘了。"韦布里奇说，显然松了一口气。

===Original===
And then began the suspense. A minute slowly dragged itself out, and no sphere shot out of the water. Another followed, and nothing broke the low oily swell. The sailors explained to one another that little point about the winding-in of the cord. The rigging was dotted with expectant faces. "Come up, Elstead!" called one hairy-chested salt impatiently, and the others caught it up, and shouted as though they were waiting for the curtain of a theatre to rise.
The commander glanced irritably at them.
"Of course, if the acceleration's less than two," he said, "he'll be all the longer. We aren't absolutely certain that was the proper figure. I'm no slavish believer in calculations."
Steevens agreed concisely. No one on the quarterdeck spoke for a couple of minutes. Then Steevens' watchcase clicked.

===Chinese===
接下来便开始了那种悬心的等待。一分钟慢慢地拖了过去，并没有什么钢球从水里射出来。又过了一分钟，那低低油亮的海面依旧毫无动静。水手们彼此解释着那点关于绳子收进去的小道理。桅具上星星点点都是翘首以待的脸。"上来吧，埃尔斯特德！"一个胸口毛茸茸的老水手不耐烦地喊道，旁人也跟着喊起来，就像是在等着戏园子的幕布升起来似的。
舰长恼怒地瞥了他们一眼。
"当然，要是加速度不到两英尺，"他说，"他那会儿就更长些。咱们也不能完全肯定那个数字就对。我可绝非那种对算术盲目相信的人。"
斯蒂文斯简短地表示同意。后甲板上有一两分钟没人说话。然后是斯蒂文斯的表壳"嗒"的一响。

===Original===
When, twenty-one minutes after, the sun reached the zenith, they were still waiting for the globe to reappear, and not a man aboard had dared to whisper that hope was dead. It was Weybridge who first gave expression to that realisation. He spoke while the sound of eight bells still hung in the air. "I always distrusted that window," he said quite suddenly to Steevens.
"Good God!" said Steevens; "you don't think—?"
"Well!" said Weybridge, and left the rest to his imagination.
"I'm no great believer in calculations myself," said the commander dubiously, "so that I'm not altogether hopeless yet." And at midnight the gunboat was steaming slowly in a spiral round the spot where the globe had sunk, and the white beam of the electric light fled and halted and swept discontentedly onward again over the waste of phosphorescent waters under the little stars.

===Chinese===
又过了二十一分钟，太阳升到了天顶，他们仍在等待那只圆球重新出现，船上没有一个人敢低声说希望已经破灭。头一个把这层觉悟说出口的是韦布里奇。他说话时，八响钟声的余韵还飘在空中。"我一直信不过那扇窗户。"他突如其来地对斯蒂文斯说。
"老天爷！"斯蒂文斯说，"你该不是以为——？"
"嗯！"韦布里奇说，剩下的便由对方自己去想象。
"我自己对算术也没什么大信心，"舰长迟疑地说，"所以我还没有完全绝望。"到了半夜，炮艇还在缓缓地以螺旋航线绕着钢球沉没之处行驶，电光灯那道白色的光柱，在那一片漫着磷光的海面上奔逃、停下、又不满地继续扫过去，头顶上是细碎的星辰。

===Original===
"If his window hasn't burst and smashed him," said Weybridge, "then it's a cursed sight worse, for his clockwork has gone wrong, and he's alive now, five miles under our feet, down there in the cold and dark, anchored in that little bubble of his, where never a ray of light has shone or a human being lived, since the waters were gathered together. He's there without food, feeling hungry and thirsty and scared, wondering whether he'll starve or stifle. Which will it be? The Myers apparatus is running out, I suppose. How long do they last?"
"Good heavens!" he exclaimed; "what little things we are! What daring little devils! Down there, miles and miles of water—all water, and all this empty water about us and this sky. Gulfs!" He threw his hands out, and as he did so, a little white streak swept noiselessly up the sky, travelled more slowly, stopped, became a motionless dot, as though a new star had fallen up into the sky. Then it went sliding back again and lost itself amidst the reflections of the stars and the white haze of the sea's phosphorescence.
At the sight he stopped, arm extended and mouth open. He shut his mouth, opened it again, and waved his arms with an impatient gesture. Then he turned, shouted "Elstead ahoy!" to the first watch, and went at a run to Lindley and the searchlight. "I saw him," he said. "Starboard there! His light's on, and he's just shot out of the water. Bring the light round. We ought to see him drifting, when he lifts on the swell."

===Chinese===
"要是他那扇窗户没破、没把他砸烂，"韦布里奇说，"那情形可就更糟了——那意味着他的发条出了毛病，此刻他还活着，在我们脚下五英里深的地方，在那寒冷和黑暗之中，抛锚似地系在他那只小小的气泡里，那一带，自打海水汇聚以来，从未有过一线光照进去，也从未有过人烟。他在那里头，没有食物，又饿又渴又怕，不知道自己到底会饿死还是憋死。到底是哪一样呢？迈尔斯装置快用完了吧，我猜。这种装置能撑多久？"
"老天爷！"他忽然叫起来，"我们可真是渺小啊！我们这帮胆大包天的小疯子！底下呢，一英里接一英里深的海水——全是水，而我们周围这空空荡荡的水，这片天。一道道深渊啊！"他张开双臂，就在他这动作的同时，一道白色的细痕悄然无声地掠上天空，移动得越来越慢，停住，化成一个一动不动的点，仿佛一颗新星倒着落进了天上。然后它又往下滑回去，在群星的倒影和海面磷光的白色雾霭里隐没了。
看见这一幕，他戛然止步，伸着胳膊，张着嘴。他合上嘴，又张开，急躁地挥动双臂。然后他转身朝第一班值更的人喊了一声"埃尔斯特德，喂！"便拔脚奔向林德利（Lindley）和探照灯。"我看见他了。"他说，"右舷！他的灯亮着，刚刚从水里冒出来。把灯转过去。等他随涌浪浮上来，我们应当能看见他漂流。"

===Original===
But they never picked up the explorer until dawn. Then they almost ran him down. The crane was swung out and a boat's crew hooked the chain to the sphere. When they had shipped the sphere, they unscrewed the manhole and peered into the darkness of the interior (for the electric light chamber was intended to illuminate the water about the sphere, and was shut off entirely from its general cavity).
The air was very hot within the cavity, and the indiarubber at the lip of the manhole was soft. There was no answer to their eager questions and no sound of movement within. Elstead seemed to be lying motionless, crumpled up in the bottom of the globe. The ship's doctor crawled in and lifted him out to the men outside. For a moment or so they did not know whether Elstead was alive or dead. His face, in the yellow light of the ship's lamps, glistened with perspiration. They carried him down to his own cabin.
He was not dead, they found, but in a state of absolute nervous collapse, and besides cruelly bruised. For some days he had to lie perfectly still. It was a week before he could tell his experiences.
Almost his first words were that he was going down again. The sphere would have to be altered, he said, in order to allow him to throw off the cord if need be, and that was all. He had had the most marvellous experience. "You thought I should find nothing but ooze," he said. "You laughed at my explorations, and I've discovered a new world!" He told his story in disconnected fragments, and chiefly from the wrong end, so that it is impossible to retell it in his words. But what follows is the narrative of his experience.

===Chinese===
可是他们一直没找到这位探险家，直到天将破晓。那时他们险些撞上他。吊车被转到船外，一艇人把链条钩到钢球上。把钢球吊上船后，他们拧开舱口，向里头那一片黑暗窥视（因为那盏电灯是为照亮钢球四周的水而设的，与舱内的整个空腔完全隔开）。
舱里的空气滚烫，舱口橡胶唇边已经发软。他们急切地连声追问，里面没有任何回答，也没有一丝动静的声音。埃尔斯特德似乎一动不动地蜷在圆球的底部。船医爬进去，把他递给外头的人。有一阵子，他们分不清埃尔斯特德是死是活。在船上灯火昏黄的光里，只见他满脸油光，全是汗水。他们把他抬到他自己舱里。
他们发觉他没有死，但精神已经彻底崩溃，此外浑身都是青肿的重伤。一连几天他都得一动不动地躺着。过了一个星期，他才能把自己经历的事讲出来。
他几乎是开口头一句话，便说自己还要再下去一趟。他说，钢球只需做一处改装——必要时能让他自行割断绳索——仅此而已。他这一趟经历之奇妙，无以言表。"你们以为我除了淤泥什么也看不到，"他说，"你们嘲笑我这场考察，可我发现了一个新世界！"他的故事讲得东鳞西爪，还多半是从结尾倒着讲，因此已经无法用他自己的话复述了。下面所述，便是他那番经历的经过。

===Original===
It began atrociously, he said. Before the cord ran out, the thing kept rolling over. He felt like a frog in a football. He could see nothing but the crane and the sky overhead, with an occasional glimpse of the people on the ship's rail. He couldn't tell a bit which way the thing would roll next. Suddenly he would find his feet going up, and try to step, and over he went rolling, head over heels, and just anyhow, on the padding. Any other shape would have been more comfortable, but no other shape was to be relied upon under the huge pressure of the nethermost abyss.
Suddenly the swaying ceased; the globe righted, and when he had picked himself up, he saw the water all about him greeny-blue, with an attenuated light filtering down from above, and a shoal of little floating things went rushing up past him, as it seemed to him, towards the light. And even as he looked, it grew darker and darker, until the water above was as dark as the midnight sky, albeit of a greener shade, and the water below black. And little transparent things in the water developed a faint glint of luminosity, and shot past him in faint greenish streaks.
And the feeling of falling! It was just like the start of a lift, he said, only it kept on. One has to imagine what that means, that keeping on. It was then of all times that Elstead repented of his adventure. He saw the chances against him in an altogether new light. He thought of the big cuttlefish people knew to exist in the middle waters, the kind of things they find half digested in whales at times, or floating dead and rotten and half eaten by fish. Suppose one caught hold and wouldn't let go. And had the clockwork really been sufficiently tested? But whether he wanted to go on or to go back mattered not the slightest now.

===Chinese===
他说，开头简直糟透了。绳子还没放出去之前，这玩意儿就不停地翻滚。他觉得自己像是一只足球里头的青蛙。除了吊车和头顶的天，他什么也看不见，偶尔瞥一眼船栏上那些人。他一点也摸不清这玩意儿下一刻会朝哪一面滚。忽然他会发现自己的脚朝了天，便想踩稳，结果连翻带滚、头脚不分、横七竖八地摔在那层衬垫上。换作任何别的形状，都会舒服得多；可在最深深渊那种巨大的压力下，任何别的形状都靠不住了。
忽然，颠簸停止了；钢球正了过来。等他爬起来，只见四周的海水是一色青蓝，一道淡淡的光从上方滤下来；一群小小的漂浮生物，似乎是朝着那光，从他身边急急地冲上去。就在他张望的当儿，海水越来越暗，越来越暗，直到上方一片漆黑，与子夜的天一般，只是带一点更绿的色调，下方则黑得彻底。水中那些透明的小东西，发出一丝隐隐约约的光，化作一道道淡绿色的光线从他身边掠过。
还有那种下坠的感觉！他说，那就像电梯刚启动的一刹那——只是它不停。人得想象一下那是什么意思，那种"不停"。正是在那时候，埃尔斯特德对自己这趟冒险生出了悔意。种种对自己不利的概率，在他眼里换上了一副全新的光景。他想起了人们知道生存在中段水域里的大王乌贼，那种偶尔在鲸鱼肚子里发现半消化状态的、或者漂浮死了发臭、被鱼啃掉半边的东西。万一一只抓住不放呢？再说，那台发条装置果真够充分地试验过了吗？然而此刻他想继续也罢，想回头也罢，都已丝毫由不得他了。

===Original===
In fifty seconds everything was as black as night outside, except where the beam from his light struck through the waters, and picked out every now and then some fish or scrap of sinking matter. They flashed by too fast for him to see what they were. Once he thinks he passed a shark. And then the sphere began to get hot by friction against the water. They had underestimated this, it seems.
The first thing he noticed was that he was perspiring, and then he heard a hissing growing louder under his feet, and saw a lot of little bubbles—very little bubbles they were—rushing upward like a fan through the water outside. Steam! He felt the window, and it was hot. He turned on the minute glow-lamp that lit his own cavity, looked at the padded watch by the studs, and saw he had been travelling now for two minutes. It came into his head that the window would crack through the conflict of temperatures, for he knew the bottom water is very near freezing.
Then suddenly the floor of the sphere seemed to press against his feet, the rush of bubbles outside grew slower and slower, and the hissing diminished. The sphere rolled a little. The window had not cracked, nothing had given, and he knew that the dangers of sinking, at any rate, were over.

===Chinese===
五十秒之内，外头已是一片漆黑，唯有他那盏灯的光柱穿过海水，时不时照见某条鱼，或是一片正在下沉的碎屑。它们一掠而过，他根本来不及看清是什么。有一次他觉得自己经过了一条鲨鱼。再然后，钢球因与水摩擦开始发热。看来，这一点他们先前是低估了。
他头一件注意到的事，是自己浑身冒汗，紧接着便听见脚下有一种嘶嘶声越来越响，又看见外面水里许多小小的气泡——真是极小的气泡——像扇面似的往上冲。蒸汽！他摸了摸窗户，是热的。他扭开照亮舱内那盏极小的微光灯，看了一眼按钮旁边那只裹着衬垫的表，得知自己已经行进了两分钟。他陡地想到，窗户会不会因两边温度相争而开裂，因为他知道，海底的水是接近冰点的。
忽然，钢球的地板似乎朝他脚底压上来，外头气泡的奔流越来越慢，嘶嘶声也小了下去。钢球微微滚了一下。窗户没有裂，什么东西也没有坏，他便知道——至少，下沉这一段路上的危险已经过去了。

===Original===
In another minute or so he would be on the floor of the abyss. He thought, he said, of Steevens and Weybridge and the rest of them five miles overhead, higher to him than the very highest clouds that ever floated over land are to us, steaming slowly and staring down and wondering what had happened to him.
He peered out of the window. There were no more bubbles now, and the hissing had stopped. Outside there was a heavy blackness—as black as black velvet—except where the electric light pierced the empty water and showed the colour of it—a yellow-green. Then three things like shapes of fire swam into sight, following each other through the water. Whether they were little and near or big and far off he could not tell.
Each was outlined in a bluish light almost as bright as the lights of a fishing smack, a light which seemed to be smoking greatly, and all along the sides of them were specks of this, like the lighter portholes of a ship. Their phosphorescence seemed to go out as they came into the radiance of his lamp, and he saw then that they were little fish of some strange sort, with huge heads, vast eyes, and dwindling bodies and tails. Their eyes were turned towards him, and he judged they were following him down. He supposed they were attracted by his glare.
Presently others of the same sort joined them. As he went on down, he noticed that the water became of a pallid colour, and that little specks twinkled in his ray like motes in a sunbeam. This was probably due to the clouds of ooze and mud that the impact of his leaden sinkers had disturbed.
By the time he was drawn down to the lead weights he was in a dense fog of white that his electric light failed altogether to pierce for more than a few yards, and many minutes elapsed before the hanging sheets of sediment subsided to any extent. Then, lit by his light and by the transient phosphorescence of a distant shoal of fishes, he was able to see under the huge blackness of the superincumbent water an undulating expanse of greyish-white ooze, broken here and there by tangled thickets of a growth of sea lilies, waving hungry tentacles in the air.

===Chinese===
再过一分钟光景，他就要落在深渊的底上了。他说，他想到了斯蒂文斯和韦布里奇，还有船上那一班人——在他头顶上五英里的地方，对他而言，此刻所处的位置比陆地上空所飘过的最高的云离我们还要远——他们正缓缓地开着船，朝下张望，纳闷他到底出了什么事。
他从窗户向外张望。气泡没有了，嘶嘶声也停了。外面是一种浓重的黑——黑得像最黑的丝绒——只有电光刺穿了那一片空荡荡的水，照出它的颜色——一种黄绿色。接着，三个像火形状一样的东西游进了视野，一个跟着一个穿过水来。它们是小小的、近近的，还是大大的、远远的，他分辨不出。
每一只都镶着一圈蓝光，亮得几乎和渔船的灯火差不多，那光似乎冒得很厉害的烟，它们周身还点缀着一粒粒的这种光点，像船上较亮的小舷窗。它们一进入他那盏灯的光辉之内，身上的磷光便似乎熄灭了，他这才看清，那是几条怪模怪样的小鱼，头很大，眼很鼓，身子和尾巴却细得可怜。它们的眼都朝他望着，他断定它们正跟着他往下走。他猜想它们是被他这道光吸引过来的。
不久，又有几条同类的鱼加入了它们。他继续往下走，注意到海水变成了一种苍白的颜色，光柱里有些小粒在闪烁，像阳光里的尘埃。这大概是因为他那几个铅锤撞进海底，搅起了一团团淤泥和浊水。
等他被拽到那几个铅锤那里时，他已经身处一团浓浓的白色雾气里，他的电灯往里只能照透几码远，过了好几分钟，悬在水中的一片片泥沙才稍稍沉下去一些。然后，借着他的灯光，又借着远处一群鱼一闪而过的磷光，他终于在头顶那庞大无边的黑水之下，看见一片起伏的灰白色淤泥平原，这里那里有一簇簇纠缠在一起的海百合丛，像一片片树林子，饥肠辘辘地把触手在水中摆来摆去。

===Original===
Farther away were the graceful, translucent outlines of a group of gigantic sponges. About this floor there were scattered a number of bristling flattish tufts of rich purple and black, which he decided must be some sort of sea-urchin, and small, large-eyed or blind things having a curious resemblance, some to woodlice, and others to lobsters, crawled sluggishly across the track of the light and vanished into the obscurity again, leaving furrowed trails behind them.
Then suddenly the hovering swarm of little fishes veered about and came towards him as a flight of starlings might do. They passed over him like a phosphorescent snow, and then he saw behind them some larger creature advancing towards the sphere.
At first he could see it only dimly, a faintly moving figure remotely suggestive of a walking man, and then it came into the spray of light that the lamp shot out. As the glare struck it, it shut its eyes, dazzled. He stared in rigid astonishment.
It was a strange vertebrated animal. Its dark purple head was dimly suggestive of a chameleon, but it had such a high forehead and such a braincase as no reptile ever displayed before; the vertical pitch of its face gave it a most extraordinary resemblance to a human being.
Two large and protruding eyes projected from sockets in chameleon fashion, and it had a broad reptilian mouth with horny lips beneath its little nostrils. In the position of the ears were two huge gill-covers, and out of these floated a branching tree of coralline filaments, almost like the treelike gills that very young rays and sharks possess.
But the humanity of the face was not the most extraordinary thing about the creature. It was a biped; its almost globular body was poised on a tripod of two frog-like legs and a long thick tail, and its fore limbs, which grotesquely caricatured the human hand, much as a frog's do, carried a long shaft of bone, tipped with copper. The colour of the creature was variegated; its head, hands, and legs were purple; but its skin, which hung loosely upon it, even as clothes might do, was a phosphorescent grey. And it stood there blinded by the light.

===Chinese===
更远处，是一群巨大海绵那婀娜而半透明的轮廓。这片海底上还散布着一簇簇毛茸茸的、扁扁的、富丽的紫黑色东西，他断定这必定是某种海胆；还有一些小小的、生着大眼或全无眼睛的生物，样子出奇地像——有的像潮虫，有的像龙虾——慢吞吞地爬过光柱的范围，又消失在黑暗里，身后留下一条条犁过的痕迹。
忽然，那群盘桓着的小鱼猛地一齐转向，朝他扑来，像是一群椋鸟飞过来一般。它们从他头顶掠过，像下了一场磷光雪；他这才看见它们后面有个稍大些的生物，正朝着钢球走过来。
起初他只能隐隐看见它，一个隐约移动的身影，远远瞧着，依稀像是一个行走的人。然后它走进了灯光喷射出来的范围。强光一照，它睁不开眼，被晃得闭上了双眼。他惊得发僵地盯着。
这是一只古怪的脊椎动物。它那深紫色的头依稀有些像变色龙，可它的额头之高、脑壳之大，是任何爬行动物所未曾显示过的；它的脸几近垂直，这使它与人类产生了极其惊人的相似。
两只大而凸出的眼睛，以变色龙的方式从眼窝里伸出来；它有一条宽阔的、爬行动物式的嘴，角质嘴唇生在小小的鼻孔下方。耳朵的位置上是两片巨大的鳃盖，从里头飘出一棵珊瑚丝状分枝的树，几乎和小小的鳐鱼与鲨鱼所具有的那种树枝状的鳃一模一样。
但是，这张脸上的人形意味，还并非这只生物最惊人之处。它是两足的；它那近乎球形的身子，由两条蛙腿和一条又长又粗的尾巴这副三脚架支撑着；它的前肢——极其滑稽地模仿着人手，正如蛙之所为——握着一根长长的骨头杆子，尖端包着铜。这生物的色彩斑驳；它的头、手、腿是紫色；可它那宽松地披在身上的皮，像衣服一般，是磷光色的灰。它就站在那里，被光照得睁不开眼。

===Original===
At last this unknown creature of the abyss blinked its eyes open, and, shading them with its disengaged hand, opened its mouth and gave vent to a shouting noise, articulate almost as speech might be, that penetrated even the steel case and padded jacket of the sphere. How a shouting may be accomplished without lungs Elstead does not profess to explain. It then moved sideways out of the glare into the mystery of shadow that bordered it on either side, and Elstead felt rather than saw that it was coming towards him. Fancying the light had attracted it, he turned the switch that cut off the current. In another moment something soft dabbed upon the steel, and the globe swayed.
Then the shouting was repeated, and it seemed to him that a distant echo answered it. The dabbing recurred, and the globe swayed and ground against the spindle over which the wire was rolled. He stood in the blackness and peered out into the everlasting night of the abyss. And presently he saw, very faint and remote, other phosphorescent quasi-human forms hurrying towards him.
Hardly knowing what he did, he felt about in his swaying prison for the stud of the exterior electric light, and came by accident against his own small glow-lamp in its padded recess. The sphere twisted, and then threw him down; he heard shouts like shouts of surprise, and when he rose to his feet, he saw two pairs of stalked eyes peering into the lower window and reflecting his light.

===Chinese===
终于，这只深渊里的未知生物眨了眨眼，把它们睁开，用空着的那只手遮着光，张开嘴，发出了一种叫喊般的声响，几乎像言语一般清晰可辨，竟穿透了钢球的外壳和软衬。这种没肺的东西怎样发出喊叫，埃尔斯特德自称无法解释。随后它侧身移出强光，退入两侧那一片幽暗莫测的阴影里。埃尔斯特德与其说看见，不如说感觉到，它正朝他过来。他以为是灯光把它引来的，便扳下电闸切断了电流。不一会儿，有什么柔软的东西"啪"地拍在钢壳上，钢球晃了一下。
接着那叫喊声又起，他似乎听见远处有一个回声在应答。那拍击声再次传来，钢球晃动，在缠绳的轴上摩擦。他站在这一片漆黑里，向外张望那深渊永恒的夜。不久，他看见——非常微弱、非常遥远——别的几个磷光色的、半人形的东西，正匆匆朝他赶来。
他几乎不知道自己在做什么，在晃动的囚笼里摸索着外灯的按钮，却碰巧撞到了裹着衬垫、嵌在凹槽里他自己那盏小微光灯。钢球一扭，把他摔倒了；他听见几声叫喊，像是惊诧的叫喊；等他爬起来，看见两对长在肉柄上的眼睛，正从下窗往里张望，把他的灯光反射回来。

===Original===
In another moment hands were dabbing vigorously at his steel casing, and there was a sound, horrible enough in his position, of the metal protection of the clockwork being vigorously hammered. That, indeed, sent his heart into his mouth, for if these strange creatures succeeded in stopping that, his release would never occur. Scarcely had he thought as much when he felt the sphere sway violently, and the floor of it press hard against his feet. He turned off the small glow-lamp that lit the interior, and sent the ray of the large light in the separate compartment out into the water. The sea-floor and the manlike creatures had disappeared, and a couple of fish chasing each other dropped suddenly by the window.
He thought at once that these strange denizens of the deep sea had broken the rope, and that he had escaped. He drove up faster and faster, and then stopped with a jerk that sent him flying against the padded roof of his prison. For half a minute, perhaps, he was too astonished to think.
Then he felt that the sphere was spinning slowly, and rocking, and it seemed to him that it was also being drawn through the water. By crouching close to the window, he managed to make his weight effective and roll that part of the sphere downward, but he could see nothing save the pale ray of his light striking down ineffectively into the darkness. It occurred to him that he would see more if he turned the lamp off, and allowed his eyes to grow accustomed to the profound obscurity.
In this he was wise. After some minutes the velvety blackness became a translucent blackness, and then, far away, and as faint as the zodiacal light of an English summer evening, he saw shapes moving below. He judged these creatures had detached his cable, and were towing him along the sea bottom.

===Chinese===
再一转眼，便有无数只手在他这钢壳上使劲地拍打；还有一种——在他这种处境里听起来可怕之极的声音——那发条装置外面的金属保护罩正被狠狠地敲打着。这一下真把他吓得魂飞魄散，因为假如这些怪东西当真把那东西搞停了，他便永远别想脱身了。他刚想到这里，便感到钢球剧烈地晃了一下，球底重重地压在他脚上。他关掉照亮舱内那盏小灯，让分隔舱里大灯的光柱射进水里。海底和那些人形生物都不见了；一对互相追逐的鱼忽然从窗外坠下来。
他顿时以为，这些深海里的怪居民扯断了绳子，他已经脱身了。他越上越快，然后猛地一顿，把他整个摔到囚笼那衬着软垫的顶上。大约有半分钟，他惊得不能思想。
接着他感觉到钢球在缓缓地旋转，并且摇动，似乎还在水里被拖着走。他紧贴着窗户，设法用自己的重量把钢球的这一面压到下面去，但除了自己那道光柱徒劳地射进黑暗之外，什么也看不见。他想到，要是把灯关掉，让眼睛适应这深沉的幽暗，便能看见更多。
他这一着是聪明的。过了几分钟，丝绒般的漆黑化作了一种半透明的黑；接着，远远地，像英国夏夜里的黄道光一般微弱，他看见底下有形体在移动。他料想是这些生物解开了他的绳索，正沿着海底拖着他走。

===Original===
And then he saw something faint and remote across the undulations of the submarine plain, a broad horizon of pale luminosity that extended this way and that way as far as the range of his little window permitted him to see. To this he was being towed, as a balloon might be towed by men out of the open country into a town. He approached it very slowly, and very slowly the dim irradiation was gathered together into more definite shapes.
It was nearly five o'clock before he came over this luminous area, and by that time he could make out an arrangement suggestive of streets and houses grouped about a vast roofless erection that was grotesquely suggestive of a ruined abbey. It was spread out like a map below him. The houses were all roofless enclosures of walls, and their substance being, as he afterwards saw, of phosphorescent bones, gave the place an appearance as if it were built of drowned moonshine.
Among the inner caves of the place waving trees of crinoid stretched their tentacles, and tall, slender, glassy sponges shot like shining minarets and lilies of filmy light out of the general glow of the city. In the open spaces of the place he could see a stirring movement as of crowds of people, but he was too many fathoms above them to distinguish the individuals in those crowds.
Then slowly they pulled him down, and as they did so, the details of the place crept slowly upon his apprehension. He saw that the courses of the cloudy buildings were marked out with beaded lines of round objects, and then he perceived that at several points below him, in broad open spaces, were forms like the encrusted shapes of ships.
Slowly and surely he was drawn down, and the forms below him became brighter, clearer, more distinct. He was being pulled down, he perceived, towards the large building in the centre of the town, and he could catch a glimpse ever and again of the multitudinous forms that were lugging at his cord. He was astonished to see that the rigging of one of the ships, which formed such a prominent feature of the place, was crowded with a host of gesticulating figures regarding him, and then the walls of the great building rose about him silently, and hid the city from his eyes.
And such walls they were, of waterlogged wood, and twisted wire-rope, and iron spars, and copper, and the bones and skulls of dead men. The skulls ran in zigzag lines and spirals and fantastic curves over the building; and in and out of their eye-sockets, and over the whole surface of the place, lurked and played a multitude of silvery little fishes.

===Chinese===
然后，他隔着海底平原的起伏，看见了某种隐隐约约、远远的东西——一道宽阔的、淡淡的光带，朝着左右延伸，直伸到他那扇小窗所能看到的尽头。他正被拖向那道光带，就像一只气球，被一群人从旷野拖进一座城镇一般。他非常缓慢地接近过去，那一片朦胧的光辉也极其缓慢地聚拢成更为清晰的形状。
差不多到了五点钟他才来到这片光带的上方，到那时他已经能辨出一种布局——它叫人联想到街道和房屋，环绕着一座没有屋顶的庞大建筑，那建筑古怪地叫人联想到一处废毁的修道院。它像一张地图似的在他脚底下铺开。那些房屋全是没有屋顶的围墙，其建筑材料——他后来才看清——乃是磷光的骨头，这使得那地方看上去像是由淹没在水下的月光建成的。
这地方的深处洞穴里，摇曳的海百合树伸出它们的触手，又高又细、玻璃一般的海绵，像闪光的尖塔和薄纱光似的百合花，从那座城市总体的光辉里射出来。这地方的空地上，他能看见一种骚动的运动，像是人群在动，可他在它们头顶上隔着好几寻深，分辨不清人群里的个体。
然后他们缓缓地把他拉了下去，与此同时，这地方的细节也缓缓地爬进了他的知觉。他看见那些云雾般建筑物的走向，都用一行行圆形物件的串珠标了出来；接着他又察觉，他下方几处开阔的空地上，有几个形体，像是被贝壳之类裹满的船壳的样子。
他无可避免地被缓缓地拽了下去，下方那些形体变得越来越亮、越来越清、越来越分明。他察觉到，自己正被拉向城市中央那座大建筑，并不时瞥见那一群群正拽着他绳子的繁多身影。他惊讶地看见，其中一艘船——这艘船是此地极其显眼的一处景物——的桅具上挤满了一群指手画脚的身影，全都朝他望着。然后，那座大建筑的墙便静悄悄地在他四周升起，把城市从他眼前遮去。
那些墙是这样的：泡透了的木头、扭绞着的铁绳、铁桅、铜，还有死人骨头和骷髅。骷髅在建筑物上排成"之"字形、螺旋形和各种奇形怪状的曲线；在骷髅的眼窝里进进出出，在整座建筑的整个表面上，潜伏着、嬉戏着一群银色的小鱼。

===Original===
Suddenly his ears were filled with a low shouting and a noise like the violent blowing of horns, and this gave place to a fantastic chant. Down the sphere sank, past the huge pointed windows, through which he saw vaguely a great number of these strange, ghostlike people regarding him, and at last he came to rest, as it seemed, on a kind of altar that stood in the centre of the place.
And now he was at such a level that he could see these strange people of the abyss plainly once more. To his astonishment, he perceived that they were prostrating themselves before him, all save one, dressed as it seemed in a robe of placoid scales, and crowned with a luminous diadem, who stood with his reptilian mouth opening and shutting, as though he led the chanting of the worshippers.
A curious impulse made Elstead turn on his small glow-lamp again, so that he became visible to these creatures of the abyss, albeit the glare made them disappear forthwith into night. At this sudden sight of him, the chanting gave place to a tumult of exultant shouts; and Elstead, being anxious to watch them, turned his light off again, and vanished from before their eyes. But for a time he was too blind to make out what they were doing, and when at last he could distinguish them, they were kneeling again. And thus they continued worshipping him, without rest or intermission, for the space of three hours.

===Chinese===
忽然，他耳边充满了一种低低的呐喊，和一种像猛烈吹响号角的声音，紧接着变成了一段奇异的吟唱。钢球沉了下去，从那一扇扇高大尖顶的窗户前经过——透过窗户，他隐约看见大批这种古怪、鬼魂般的人正朝他张望——最后，他似乎是停在了一种祭坛上，祭坛立在整座建筑的正中央。
此刻他所处的位置，使他又一次能清清楚楚地看见这些深渊里的怪人。他惊讶地发现，他们正在他面前五体投地，唯独一个除外——那一个看上去穿着一件盾鳞（placoid scales）做的袍子，头上戴着一顶发光的王冠，他那张爬行动物式的嘴一开一合，似乎在领着礼拜者们吟唱。
一种古怪的冲动使埃尔斯特德又打开了那盏小微光灯，让这些深渊里的生物得以看见他——虽然这光使他们即刻消失在夜里。骤然看见他，吟唱化成了一片狂喜的呐喊；埃尔斯特德急着要看他们，便又把灯关掉，从他们眼前消失。可一时之间他两眼发黑，辨不清他们在干什么，等他终于能分辨出来时，他们又跪下了。就这样，他们不停地膜拜他，无休无止，整整三个钟头。

===Original===
Most circumstantial was Elstead's account of this astounding city and its people, these people of perpetual night, who have never seen sun or moon or stars, green vegetation, nor any living, air-breathing creatures, who know nothing of fire, nor any light but the phosphorescent light of living things.
Startling as is his story, it is yet more startling to find that scientific men, of such eminence as Adams and Jenkins, find nothing incredible in it. They tell me they see no reason why intelligent, water-breathing, vertebrated creatures, inured to a low temperature and enormous pressure, and of such a heavy structure, that neither alive nor dead would they float, might not live upon the bottom of the deep sea, and quite unsuspected by us, descendants like ourselves of the great Theriomorpha of the New Red Sandstone age.
We should be known to them, however, as strange, meteoric creatures, wont to fall catastrophically dead out of the mysterious blackness of their watery sky. And not only we ourselves, but our ships, our metals, our appliances, would come raining down out of the night. Sometimes sinking things would smite down and crush them, as if it were the judgment of some unseen power above, and sometimes would come things of the utmost rarity or utility, or shapes of inspiring suggestion. One can understand, perhaps, something of their behaviour at the descent of a living man, if one thinks what a barbaric people might do, to whom an enhaloed, shining creature came suddenly out of the sky.

===Chinese===
关于这座惊人的城市和它的居民——这些永夜之民，从未见过日月星辰、绿色草木，也从未见过任何活的、呼吸空气的生物，他们不知火为何物，所知的光只有活物身上发出来的磷光——埃尔斯特德的叙述极其详尽。
他的故事固然骇人听闻，然而更骇人听闻的是：像亚当斯（Adams）和詹金斯（Jenkins）这样有声望的科学家，竟觉得其中并无不可信之处。他们告诉我，他们看不出有何理由，能否定下面这种可能：一种有智力的、以鳃呼吸的、有脊椎的生物，习惯于低温和惊人的压力，骨骼结构如此沉重，无论死活都不会浮起——他们完全可以栖息在深海的海底，而我们一点也察觉不到；他们和我们一样，都是新红砂岩（New Red Sandstone）时代那伟大的兽形类（Theriomorpha）的后裔。
然而，在他们眼里，我们是古怪的、像流星一样的生物，习惯于从他们那水的天空那神秘的黑暗中，灾难性地坠落下来死掉。不仅是我们自身，连我们的船、我们的金属、我们的器物，都会从那片夜空里像下雨一般落下去。有时下沉的东西会击中、砸死他们，仿佛是上面某种看不见的力量所降的惩罚；有时落下来的又是最稀有、最有用的物件，或者是某种令人振奋、富于启发的形体。当活人降下时他们的种种行为，我们或许多少能理解一二——只要想一想：对一个野蛮民族而言，若有一个光环罩身、浑身发光的生物，忽然从天上降下来，他们会怎样。

===Original===
At one time or another Elstead probably told the officers of the *Ptarmigan* every detail of his strange twelve hours in the abyss. That he also intended to write them down is certain, but he never did, and so unhappily we have to piece together the discrepant fragments of his story from the reminiscences of Commander Simmons, Weybridge, Steevens, Lindley, and the others.
We see the thing darkly in fragmentary glimpses—the huge ghostly building, the bowing, chanting people, with their dark chameleon-like heads and faintly luminous clothing, and Elstead, with his light turned on again, vainly trying to convey to their minds that the cord by which the sphere was held was to be severed. Minute after minute slipped away, and Elstead, looking at his watch, was horrified to find that he had oxygen only for four hours more. But the chant in his honour kept on as remorselessly as if it was the marching song of his approaching death.
The manner of his release he does not understand, but to judge by the end of cord that hung from the sphere, it had been cut through by rubbing against the edge of the altar. Abruptly the sphere rolled over, and he swept up, out of their world, as an ethereal creature clothed in a vacuum would sweep through our own atmosphere back to its native ether again. He must have torn out of their sight as a hydrogen bubble hastens upward from our air. A strange ascension it must have seemed to them.
The sphere rushed up with even greater velocity than, when weighted with the lead sinkers, it had rushed down. It became exceedingly hot. It drove up with the windows uppermost, and he remembers the torrent of bubbles frothing against the glass. Every moment he expected this to fly. Then suddenly something like a huge wheel seemed to be released in his head, the padded compartment began spinning about him, and he fainted. His next recollection was of his cabin, and of the doctor's voice.

===Chinese===
关于他在深渊里那奇异的十二小时里的每一个细节，埃尔斯特德大概或早或晚都对"雷鸟号"（*Ptarmigan*）上的军官们讲过。他也确曾打算把这些写下来，可始终没动笔，因此我们不得不遗憾地从西蒙斯舰长（Commander Simmons）、韦布里奇、斯蒂文斯、林德利和其他人的回忆中，把他这故事彼此矛盾的残片拼凑起来。
我们只能在支离破碎的一瞥里隐约看见这件事——那座庞大如鬼魅的建筑，那些膜拜吟唱着的人，长着变色龙似的黑头，衣衫微微发光；还有埃尔斯特德，他重新把灯开亮，徒劳地想让他们明白：拴住钢球的那根绳子必须割断。一分钟一分钟地溜了过去，埃尔斯特德看着表，骇然发觉自己只剩四个钟头的氧气了。然而为他而作的吟唱却毫无怜悯地继续着，仿佛是他渐近之死的进行曲。
他究竟是怎么脱身的，他自己也不明白，但据钢球上挂下来的那段绳头判断，那是被祭坛的边缘磨断的。钢球猝然一滚，他从他们的世界里升了上去，宛如一个裹着真空的精灵，会从我们的大气层里一掠而过，回到它本来的太空。他从他们眼前消失之快，想必像一只氢气泡从我们空气里上升那般。在他们看来，这必定是一次奇异的升天。
钢球往上冲的速度，比带着铅锤往下冲时还要快。它变得极其热。它是窗户朝上地往上冲，他记得那股气泡洪流在玻璃上翻腾起沫。每一瞬间他都盼着玻璃会爆开。然后忽然间，他脑袋里仿佛有个巨大的轮子被松了开来，那衬着软垫的舱室开始围着他旋转，他便晕了过去。他下一刻的记忆，是自己的舱房，和大夫的声音。

===Original===
But that is the substance of the extraordinary story that Elstead related in fragments to the officers of the *Ptarmigan*. He promised to write it all down at a later date. His mind was chiefly occupied with the improvement of his apparatus, which was effected at Rio.
It remains only to tell that on February 2, 1896, he made his second descent into the ocean abyss, with the improvements his first experience suggested. What happened we shall probably never know. He never returned. The *Ptarmigan* beat about over the point of his submersion, seeking him in vain for thirteen days. Then she returned to Rio, and the news was telegraphed to his friends. So the matter remains for the present. But it is hardly probable that no further attempt will be made to verify his strange story of these hitherto unsuspected cities of the deep sea.

===Chinese===
然而，这便是埃尔斯特德零零碎碎地向"雷鸟号"军官们讲述的那番非凡经历的主要内容。他答应过日后要把这一切写下来。他的心思主要花在改进他的装置上，这项改进是在里约（Rio）完成的。
剩下要说的只是：1896 年 2 月 2 日，他带着第一次经验所提示的几处改进，第二次下到那海洋的深渊里去。究竟发生了什么，我们大概永远无从知晓。他再也没有回来。"雷鸟号"在他下潜的那处海面上来回搜寻了十三天，徒劳无功。然后她驶回里约，消息由电报拍给了他的亲友。事情至此便如此悬着。但是，要说日后不会再有人去设法证实他这桩关于深海那些前所未闻的城市的奇闻，那恐怕不大可能。

## In the Avu Observatory / 阿武天文台

===Original===
The observatory at Avu, in Borneo, stands on the spur of the mountain. To the north rises the old crater, black at night against the unfathomable blue of the sky. From the little circular building, with its mushroom dome, the slopes plunge steeply downward into the black mysteries of the tropical forest beneath. The little house in which the observer and his assistant live is about fifty yards from the observatory, and beyond this are the huts of their native attendants.

Thaddy, the chief observer, was down with a slight fever. His assistant, Woodhouse, paused for a moment in silent contemplation of the tropical night before commencing his solitary vigil. The night was very still. Now and then voices and laughter came from the native huts, or the cry of some strange animal was heard from the midst of the mystery of the forest. Nocturnal insects appeared in ghostly fashion out of the darkness, and fluttered round his light. He thought, perhaps, of all the possibilities of discovery that still lay in the black tangle beneath him; for to the naturalist the virgin forests of Borneo are still a wonderland full of strange questions and half-suspected discoveries. Woodhouse carried a small lantern in his hand, and its yellow glow contrasted vividly with the infinite series of tints between lavender-blue and black in which the landscape was painted. His hands and face were smeared with ointment against the attacks of the mosquitoes.

Even in these days of celestial photography, work done in a purely temporary erection, and with only the most primitive appliances in addition to the telescope, still involves a very large amount of cramped and motionless watching. He sighed as he thought of the physical fatigues before him, stretched himself, and entered the observatory.

===Chinese===
婆罗洲（Borneo）阿武（Avu）的那座天文台，矗立在一条山脊上。北面耸立着那座古老的火山口，入夜以后黑黝黝地衬在深不可测的碧蓝夜空之下。从那座带着蘑菇形圆顶的圆形小屋向外望去，山坡陡然下坠，没入下方热带丛林那一片黑魆魆的神秘之中。观测员和他的助手住的那间小屋，离天文台约莫有五十码；再往外，便是他们那些本地仆从的茅舍。

塔迪（Thaddy）是首席观测员，此刻正发着一点低烧，卧床不起。他的助手伍德豪斯（Woodhouse）在独自一人开始守夜之前，驻足片刻，默默地凝望了一会儿这热带的夜色。夜静极了。茅舍那头时而传来人语和笑声，要不便是那密林深处的神秘之中，响起某只奇异走兽的啼叫。夜行的虫豸幽灵般地从黑暗里现身，绕着他那盏灯火扑扑飞舞。他心里也许想到了脚下那片黑压压的盘根错节之处，仍藏着种种发现的可能；因为对一个博物学家来说，婆罗洲的原始丛林至今仍是一片奇境，里面满是古怪的问题和半能预感到的发现。伍德豪斯手里提着一盏小小的风灯，那一点昏黄的光亮，与眼前这幅风景画中淡紫蓝到漆黑之间那无穷无尽的层层颜色，形成了鲜明而生动的对比。为了防蚊子叮咬，他的双手和脸都涂满了药膏。

即便是在今天这个天体摄影盛行的时代，在一座纯属临时搭建的屋子里，除了望远镜之外只用最简陋的器材干活，仍需要长时间蜷着身子、一动不动地守着观测。一想到摆在面前的这副体力上的辛苦，他便叹了口气，伸了伸腰，走进了天文台。

===Original===
The reader is probably familiar with the structure of an ordinary astronomical observatory. The building is usually cylindrical in shape, with a very light hemispherical roof capable of being turned round from the interior. The telescope is supported upon a stone pillar in the centre, and a clockwork arrangement compensates for the Earth’s rotation, and allows a star once found to be continuously observed. Besides this, there is a compact tracery of wheels and screws about its point of support, by which the astronomer adjusts it. There is, of course, a slit in the movable roof which follows the eye of the telescope in its survey of the heavens. The observer sits or lies on a sloping wooden arrangement, which he can wheel to any part of the observatory as the position of the telescope may require. Within it is advisable to have things as dark as possible, in order to enhance the brilliance of the stars observed.

===Chinese===
读者诸君大概对寻常天文台的结构并不陌生。这类建筑通常呈圆筒形，顶上是一个极轻的半球形屋顶，能从内部转动。望远镜由中央一根石柱支撑，另有一套发条装置用以抵消地球自转的影响，使一颗星一经找到，便可持续观测下去。此外，在它的支点周围，还有一套由齿轮和螺杆组成的精密机件，天文学家用它来校准。当然，那道随望远镜的目光巡视天穹而移动的屋顶上，必然有一道狭缝。观测者或坐或躺，靠在一块倾斜的木板上，随着望远镜方位的需要，可以把这块木板推到天文台里的任何一处。屋子里最好尽可能昏暗，以衬托出所观测星辰的光辉。

===Original===
The lantern flared as Woodhouse entered his circular den, and the general darkness fled into black shadows behind the big machine, from which it presently seemed to creep back over the whole place again as the light waned. The slit was a profound transparent blue, in which six stars shone with tropical brilliance, and their light lay, a pallid gleam, along the black tube of the instrument. Woodhouse shifted the roof, and then proceeding to the telescope, turned first one wheel and then another, the great cylinder slowly swinging into a new position. Then he glanced through the finder, the little companion telescope, moved the roof a little more, made some further adjustments, and set the clockwork in motion. He took off his jacket, for the night was very hot, and pushed into position the uncomfortable seat to which he was condemned for the next four hours. Then with a sigh he resigned himself to his watch upon the mysteries of space.

There was no sound now in the observatory, and the lantern waned steadily. Outside there was the occasional cry of some animal in alarm or pain, or calling to its mate, and the intermittent sounds of the Malay and Dyak servants. Presently one of the men began a queer chanting song, in which the others joined at intervals. After this it would seem that they turned in for the night, for no further sound came from their direction, and the whispering stillness became more and more profound.

===Chinese===
伍德豪斯走进这间圆形的小屋时，风灯忽地一亮，整片大黑暗便退到大机器背后，缩成几团漆黑的阴影；随即灯火渐暗，那黑暗仿佛又悄悄爬了回来，重新笼罩了整个地方。屋顶上那道狭缝是一汪幽深透明的蓝，当中有六颗星带着热带夜空特有的明亮闪烁，那星光如一抹苍白的微光，落在乌黑的望远镜镜筒上。伍德豪斯先转了转屋顶，再走到望远镜前，先拧动这一个齿轮，再拧那一个，那根巨大的圆筒便缓缓地转到一个新的方位。然后他对着寻星镜——也就是那架小小的副望远镜——望了一眼，再把屋顶略略挪一挪，又调整了几处，便上好了发条。夜里极热，他脱去外套，把自己推进那张接下来四个钟头里逃也逃不开的、极不舒服的座椅，安放妥当。然后他叹了口气，听天由命地坐下来，守望那太空的奥秘。

天文台里此刻一点声息也没有，风灯一点一点暗下去。外面偶尔传来某只走兽惊恐或痛苦的叫声，或是呼唤配偶的啼鸣，还有马来族和达雅克族（Dyak）仆从断断续续的声响。过了一会儿，其中一个人起头唱起一支古怪的、吟唱般的歌，其余的人不时跟着搭上一句。唱罢，他们似乎就都歇下了，因为那一边再也没传来什么声响，四下里那种带细语的寂静，愈发深沉了。

===Original===
The clockwork ticked steadily. The shrill hum of a mosquito explored the place and grew shriller in indignation at Woodhouse’s ointment. Then the lantern went out and all the observatory was black.
