Woodhouse shifted his position presently, when the slow movement of the telescope had carried it beyond the limits of his comfort.

===Chinese===
发条稳稳地走着，发出滴答滴答的声音。一只蚊子尖锐的嗡嗡声在屋里探来探去，嗅到伍德豪斯身上的药膏，更是尖利地恼怒起来。随后风灯熄了，整座天文台都陷进了漆黑。

望远镜缓缓移动，移出了他觉得舒坦的范围，伍德豪斯便换了个姿势。

===Original===
He was watching a little group of stars in the Milky Way, in one of which his chief had seen or fancied a remarkable colour variability. It was not a part of the regular work for which the establishment existed, and for that reason perhaps Woodhouse was deeply interested. He must have forgotten things terrestrial. All his attention was concentrated upon the great blue circle of the telescope field—a circle powdered, so it seemed, with an innumerable multitude of stars, and all luminous against the blackness of its setting. As he watched he seemed to himself to become incorporeal, as if he too were floating in the ether of space. Infinitely remote was the faint red spot he was observing.

Suddenly the stars were blotted out. A flash of blackness passed, and they were visible again.

===Chinese===
他正在观察银河（Milky Way）里的一小簇星，其中一颗，他的上司曾看见——或自以为看见——颜色有异常的变化。这并不是这座天文台设立的例行工作，也许正因为如此，伍德豪斯才格外来了兴致。尘世上的种种，他想必都忘了。他全部的注意力都凝在望远镜视野里那片蓝色的大圆上——那个圆仿佛撒满了数不清的星星，衬着一片漆黑，颗颗熠熠生辉。他这样凝望下去，仿佛觉得自己也化作了一个没有躯壳的东西，好像也漂浮在了太空的以太之中。他观察着的那一点微弱红光，远得几乎不可究诘。

忽然间，星子全都不见了。一道黑色一闪而过，星子便又显现出来。

===Original===
“Queer,” said Woodhouse. “Must have been a bird.”

The thing happened again, and immediately after the great tube shivered as though it had been struck. Then the dome of the observatory resounded with a series of thundering blows. The stars seemed to sweep aside as the telescope—which had been unclamped—swung round and away from the slit in the roof.

“Great Scott!” cried Woodhouse. “What’s this?”

===Chinese===
"古怪，"伍德豪斯说，"想必是只鸟。"

这情形又来了一次，紧接着，那根巨大的镜筒猛地一颤，像是被什么东西敲了一下。随即天文台的圆顶响起一连串雷鸣般的重击。望远镜——方才它的紧固件已松脱——荡了开去，从屋顶那道狭缝旁移开，星子仿佛也被扫到一边去了。

"老天爷！"伍德豪斯惊呼，"这是怎么回事？"

===Original===
Some huge vague black shape, with a flapping something like a wing, seemed to be struggling in the aperture of the roof. In another moment the slit was clear again, and the luminous haze of the Milky Way shone warm and bright.

The interior of the roof was perfectly black, and only a scraping sound marked the whereabouts of the unknown creature.

===Chinese===
一团硕大而模糊的黑影，带着一件扑扇着、像是翅膀的东西，似乎正在屋顶那道开口里挣扎。转眼之间，狭缝又空了出来，银河那片朦胧的光辉重新温暖而明亮地照了进来。

圆顶内侧漆黑一团，只有一阵刮擦的声音，标示出那只来历不明的活物身在何处。

===Original===
Woodhouse had scrambled from the seat to his feet. He was trembling violently and in a perspiration with the suddenness of the occurrence. Was the thing, whatever it was, inside or out? It was big, whatever else it might be. Something shot across the skylight, and the telescope swayed. He started violently and put his arm up. It was in the observatory, then, with him. It was clinging to the roof apparently. What the devil was it? Could it see him?

He stood for perhaps a minute in a state of stupefaction. The beast, whatever it was, clawed at the interior of the dome, and then something flapped almost into his face, and he saw the momentary gleam of starlight on a skin like oiled leather. His water-bottle was knocked off his little table with a smash.

===Chinese===
伍德豪斯已经从座椅上挣扎着爬起来，站直了身子。事情来得太突然，他浑身剧烈地打颤，冷汗直冒。那东西——管它是什么——究竟在里面，还是在外面？不管别的怎样，它块头不小。有什么东西从天窗前掠过，望远镜晃了一晃。他猛地一惊，抬手护住头。这么说，它已经跟他一道进了天文台。看样子它正攀在屋顶上。这究竟是什么鬼东西？它能看见他吗？

他大概有一分钟光景站着发愣。那只兽——管它是什么——在圆顶里侧一阵乱抓，紧接着有什么东西扑到了他脸前，几乎贴着他，他借着星光的微弱一闪，瞥见了一层像涂油皮革似的皮。他的水壶从小桌上一带，"砰"的一声摔得粉碎。

===Original===
The sense of some strange bird-creature hovering a few yards from his face in the darkness was indescribably unpleasant to Woodhouse. As his thought returned he concluded that it must be some night-bird or large bat. At any risk he would see what it was, and pulling a match from his pocket, he tried to strike it on the telescope seat. There was a smoking streak of phosphorescent light, the match flared for a moment, and he saw a vast wing sweeping towards him, a gleam of grey-brown fur, and then he was struck in the face and the match knocked out of his hand. The blow was aimed at his temple, and a claw tore sideways down to his cheek. He reeled and fell, and he heard the extinguished lantern smash. Another blow followed as he fell. He was partly stunned, he felt his own warm blood stream out upon his face. Instinctively he felt his eyes had been struck at, and, turning over on his face to save them, tried to crawl under the protection of the telescope.

===Chinese===
明知黑暗中有一只奇异的似鸟活物，就在离他脸不过几码的地方扑腾——这种念头给伍德豪斯带来的难受，简直无法形容。待神志稍稍回拢，他断定那定是某种夜鸟，或是只大蝙蝠。不管冒多大险，他也要瞧个究竟。他从口袋里摸出一根火柴，想在望远镜的座椅上划着。一道磷光冒着烟划过，火柴忽地燃起片刻，他只见一只巨大的翅膀朝他扑来，一抹灰褐色的绒毛一闪，接着脸上便挨了一记，火柴也被打飞了。这一击冲着他的太阳穴而来，一只爪子顺着他的脸颊向下一划。他踉跄着摔倒，听见那盏熄灭的风灯"哐啷"一声摔了个粉碎。他倒地时又挨了一下。他半边身子都打懵了，只觉得自己温热的鲜血顺着脸往下淌。他本能地感到对方分明是冲着他的眼睛来的，便翻过身，脸朝下护住双眼，挣扎着想往望远镜底下爬，以借它的遮蔽。

===Original===
He was struck again upon the back, and he heard his jacket rip, and then the thing hit the roof of the observatory. He edged as far as he could between the wooden seat and the eyepiece of the instrument, and turned his body round so that it was chiefly his feet that were exposed. With these he could at least kick. He was still in a mystified state. The strange beast banged about in the darkness, and presently clung to the telescope, making it sway and the gear rattle. Once it flapped near him, and he kicked out madly and felt a soft body with his feet. He was horribly scared now. It must be a big thing to swing the telescope like that. He saw for a moment the outline of a head black against the starlight, with sharply-pointed upstanding ears and a crest between them. It seemed to him to be as big as a mastiff’s. Then he began to bawl out as loudly as he could for help.

At that the thing came down upon him again. As it did so his hand touched something beside him on the floor. He kicked out, and the next moment his ankle was gripped and held by a row of keen teeth. He yelled again, and tried to free his leg by kicking with the other. Then he realised he had the broken water-bottle at his hand, and, snatching it, he struggled into a sitting posture, and feeling in the darkness towards his foot, gripped a velvety ear, like the ear of a big cat. He had seized the water-bottle by its neck and brought it down with a shivering crash upon the head of the strange beast. He repeated the blow, and then stabbed and jabbed with the jagged end of it, in the darkness, where he judged the face might be.

===Chinese===
他又在背上挨了一下，听见外套"嘶啦"一声撕裂，那东西接着撞在了天文台的屋顶上。他竭力把身子往木板座与望远镜目镜之间那点空隙里挤，把身体转过来，主要把两只脚露在外面。凭着脚，他至少还能踢上几脚。他仍旧一头雾水。那怪兽在黑暗里东撞西撞，不久又攀上了望远镜，弄得它一阵摇晃、齿轮嘎嘎作响。有一次它扑到他跟前，他疯了一般踢出去，脚底触到了一团软绵绵的身体。他这下怕得要命。能把望远镜荡成那样的，必是一只大东西。他借着星光，有一瞬间看清了一个脑袋的轮廓——黑黝黝地衬在星光之前，竖着两只尖尖的耳朵，两耳之间还有一撮冠毛。在他看来，那脑袋几乎有獒犬（mastiff）的脑袋那么大。于是他开始放开嗓子，拼命地呼救。

那东西闻声又扑下来。这一扑之间，他的手在身旁的地板上触到了一样东西。他一脚踢出去，紧接着，脚踝便被一排利齿紧紧咬住了。他又叫了一声，想用另一只脚蹬开，把腿抽出来。这才发觉手边就有那只摔破的水壶，便一把抓起，挣扎着坐起身，在黑暗里朝脚那边摸去，摸到了一只天鹅绒般光滑的耳朵，像大猫的耳朵。他攥住水壶的颈，带着"咔嚓"一声碎响，砸在那怪兽的脑袋上。他又砸了一下，然后用那参差不齐的断口，朝着他估摸着脸所在的地方，在黑暗里又戳又捣。

===Original===
The small teeth relaxed their hold, and at once Woodhouse pulled his leg free and kicked hard. He felt the sickening feel of fur and bone giving under his boot. There was a tearing bite at his arm, and he struck over it at the face, as he judged, and hit damp fur.

There was a pause; then he heard the sound of claws; and the dragging of a heavy body away from him over the observatory floor. Then there was silence, broken only by his own sobbing breathing, and a sound like licking. Everything was black except the parallelogram of the blue skylight with the luminous dust of stars, against which the end of the telescope now appeared in silhouette. He waited, as it seemed, an interminable time.

===Chinese===
那些小牙松开了，伍德豪斯乘机把腿一抽，狠狠一脚踢过去。他感到靴底下皮毛与骨头塌陷下去的那种令人作呕的感觉。他的胳膊被狠狠咬了一口，皮肉撕裂，他朝着脸所在的方向还了一拳，打在湿漉漉的皮毛上。

停顿了一下；随即他听见了爪子的声音，还有一个沉重的身躯在天文台地板上拖拽着、离他而去的声音。接着便是一片寂静，只余下他自己抽泣般的喘息，以及一种像是舔舐的声响。四下里漆黑一片，只有那块平行四边形的天窗透出一片蓝，里头撒着点点星光；望远镜的尽头此刻便映在这片星光前，剪出一道黑色的侧影。他等着，仿佛等了漫长得没有尽头的一段时间。

===Original===
Was the thing coming on again? He felt in his trouser-pocket for some matches, and found one remaining. He tried to strike this, but the floor was wet, and it spat and went out. He cursed. He could not see where the door was situated. In his struggle he had quite lost his bearings. The strange beast, disturbed by the splutter of the match, began to move again. “Time!” called Woodhouse, with a sudden gleam of mirth, but the thing was not coming at him again. He must have hurt it, he thought, with the broken bottle. He felt a dull pain in his ankle. Probably he was bleeding there. He wondered if it would support him if he tried to stand up. The night outside was very still. There was no sound of anyone moving. The sleepy fools had not heard those wings battering upon the dome, nor his shouts. It was no good wasting strength in shouting. The monster flapped its wings and startled him into a defensive attitude. He hit his elbow against the seat, and it fell over with a crash. He cursed this, and then he cursed the darkness.

Suddenly the oblong patch of starlight seemed to sway to and fro. Was he going to faint? It would never do to faint. He clenched his fists and set his teeth to hold himself together. Where had the door got to? It occurred to him he could get his bearings by the stars visible through the skylight. The patch of stars he saw was in Sagittarius and southeastward; the door was north—or was it north by west? He tried to think. If he could get the door open he might retreat. It might be the thing was wounded. The suspense was beastly. “Look here!” he said, “if you don’t come on, I shall come at you.”

===Chinese===
那东西又要扑过来了吗？他在裤兜里摸了摸火柴，摸出仅剩的一根。他想把它划着，可地板是湿的，火星一冒便灭了。他骂了一句。他看不见门在哪儿。方才一番挣扎，他早已辨不清方向。火柴的嗤嗤声惊动了那怪兽，它又动了起来。"时辰到了！"伍德豪斯心头忽然闪过一丝诙谐，喊了一声；可那东西并没有再扑过来。他想，自己用那只破水壶必是伤了它了。他觉得脚踝一阵钝痛。那里八成在流血。他不知道，自己若想站起身，这条腿还撑不撑得住。外面的夜很静。没有任何人走动的声响。那帮贪睡的蠢材，竟没听见扑在圆顶上的翅膀声，也没听见他的呼喊。再喊也是白费力气。那怪兽扑扇了一下翅膀，惊得他立刻摆出防守的架势。他的胳膊肘撞在座椅上，座椅"哗啦"一声翻倒。他为这骂了一句，接着又为这黑暗骂了一句。

忽然间，那一长方形的星光仿佛左右摇晃起来。他是不是要晕过去了？万万不能晕。他攥紧双拳，咬紧牙关，把自己撑住。门到底跑到哪儿去了？他忽然想到，可以从天窗里看得见的星辰来辨方向。他所见的那一片星属于人马座（Sagittarius），在东南方；门在正北——还是北偏西？他拼命地想。只要把门打开，他就能退出去。那东西也许已经受了伤。这样干等着，真是难熬到了极点。"喂！"他说，"你再不过来，我可要过去了。"

===Original===
Then the thing began clambering up the side of the observatory, and he saw its black outline gradually blot out the skylight. Was it in retreat? He forgot about the door, and watched as the dome shifted and creaked. Somehow he did not feel very frightened or excited now. He felt a curious sinking sensation inside him. The sharply-defined patch of light, with the black form moving across it, seemed to be growing smaller and smaller. That was curious. He began to feel very thirsty, and yet he did not feel inclined to get anything to drink. He seemed to be sliding down a long funnel.

He felt a burning sensation in his throat, and then he perceived it was broad daylight, and that one of the Dyak servants was looking at him with a curious expression. Then there was the top of Thaddy’s face upside down. Funny fellow, Thaddy, to go about like that! Then he grasped the situation better, and perceived that his head was on Thaddy’s knee, and Thaddy was giving him brandy. And then he saw the eyepiece of the telescope with a lot of red smears on it. He began to remember.

===Chinese===
于是那东西开始顺着天文台的一侧往上爬，他看着它黑色的轮廓一点一点地把天窗遮住。它在退却吗？他忘了那扇门，只望着圆顶摇晃、嘎吱作响。不知怎的，他此刻竟不觉得怎么害怕，也不觉得怎么激动。他心里只感到一种古怪的下坠之感。那一小块边界分明的光亮，连同在上面移动的黑色身形，似乎越缩越小。真古怪。他开始觉得非常口渴，却又一点也不想找点什么来喝。他仿佛正顺着一条长长的漏斗往下滑去。

他感到喉咙里一阵灼烧，这才看出已是天光大亮，一名达雅克族的仆人正一脸好奇地望着他。接着，塔迪那张脸的上半截倒着出现了。好个塔迪，竟这副模样四处走动！随即他把局势看得更明白了，发觉自己的头正枕在塔迪的膝上，塔迪正在喂他喝白兰地。再接着，他看见了望远镜的目镜，上头沾着好些红色的污渍。他开始记起来了。

===Original===
“You’ve made this observatory in a pretty mess,” said Thaddy.

The Dyak boy was beating up an egg in brandy. Woodhouse took this and sat up. He felt a sharp twinge of pain. His ankle was tied up, so were his arm and the side of his face. The smashed glass, red-stained, lay about the floor, the telescope seat was overturned, and by the opposite wall was a dark pool. The door was open, and he saw the grey summit of the mountain against a brilliant background of blue sky.

===Chinese===
"你把这天文台搞得一塌糊涂。"塔迪说。

那个达雅克小伙子正把一个鸡蛋打到白兰地里搅。伍德豪斯接过来，坐起身。他感到一阵钻心的疼痛。脚踝已经包扎过了，胳膊和脸侧也都包扎过了。摔碎的玻璃带着红红的血迹散落在地板上，望远镜的座椅翻在一旁，对面墙根底下还有一摊暗红的水洼。门开着，可以望见山巅灰色的峰顶，衬在一片湛蓝得耀眼的天空之前。

===Original===
“Pah!” said Woodhouse. “Who’s been killing calves here? Take me out of it.”

Then he remembered the Thing, and the fight he had had with it.

“What *was* it?” he said to Thaddy—“the Thing I fought with?”

“*You* know that best,” said Thaddy. “But, anyhow, don’t worry yourself now about it. Have some more to drink.”

===Chinese===
"呸！"伍德豪斯说，"是谁在这儿宰牛了？把我抬出去。"

这时他才记起了那东西，以及他与它那一场恶斗。

"它是什么？"他对塔迪说，"我与之搏斗的那东西？"

"这个你最清楚不过了，"塔迪说，"不过，无论如何，这会儿先别为它伤神了。再喝一点吧。"

===Original===
Thaddy, however, was curious enough, and it was a hard struggle between duty and inclination to keep Woodhouse quiet until he was decently put away in bed, and had slept upon the copious dose of meat extract Thaddy considered advisable. They then talked it over together.

“It was,” said Woodhouse, “more like a big bat than anything else in the world. It had sharp, short ears, and soft fur, and its wings were leathery. Its teeth were little but devilish sharp, and its jaw could not have been very strong or else it would have bitten through my ankle.”

“It has pretty nearly,” said Thaddy.

===Chinese===
话虽如此，塔迪心里好奇得很，在责任心与好奇心之间着实费了一番挣扎，才把伍德豪斯按住，让他安安稳稳地被抬到床上躺好，又服下了塔迪认为必不可少的那一大剂肉汁，睡了一觉。他们这才坐下来，把事情细细谈了一遍。

"它呀，"伍德豪斯说，"比世上任何东西都更像一只大蝙蝠。耳朵又短又尖，一身软毛，翅膀是皮革似的。牙齿小小的，却锋利得要命；它的颚骨想必备也不算太有劲，不然的话，就会把我脚踝一口咬穿了。"

"差一点儿就咬穿了。"塔迪说。

===Original===
“It seemed to me to hit out with its claws pretty freely. That is about as much as I know about the beast. Our conversation was intimate, so to speak, and yet not confidential.”

“The Dyak chaps talk about a Big Colugo, a Klang-utang—whatever that may be. It does not often attack man, but I suppose you made it nervous. They say there is a Big Colugo and a Little Colugo, and a something else that sounds like gobble. They all fly about at night. For my own part, I know there are flying foxes and flying lemurs about here, but they are none of them very big beasts.”

“There are more things in Heaven and Earth,” said Woodhouse—and Thaddy groaned at the quotation—“and more particularly in the forests of Borneo, than are dreamt of in our philosophies. On the whole, if the Borneo fauna is going to disgorge any more of its novelties upon me, I should prefer that it did so when I was not occupied in the observatory at night and alone.”

===Chinese===
"我觉得它出爪子相当随便。这怪兽，我所知道的大概也就这么多。可以这么说，我们之间那番交道算是颇为亲热，却谈不上推心置腹。"

"那些达雅克人说起一种大鼯猴（Big Colugo），一种'克朗乌坦'（Klang-utang）——也不知那是个什么。这种东西不常袭击人，不过我看，是你把它惹毛了。他们说有大鼯猴和小鼯猴，还有一种名字听起来像'咯咯'叫的东西。都夜里出来飞。就我自己所知，这一带倒是有狐蝠和鼯猴，不过没一种算得上是大个儿的走兽。"

"天地之间，"伍德豪斯说——这一句引文听得塔迪唉了一声——"尤其是婆罗洲的丛林里，比我们的哲学所能梦想的，还要多出许多东西。总的来说，倘若婆罗洲的动物群还要再往外吐出什么新奇的玩意儿来，我宁愿它趁我夜里不独自守在天文台里的时候再吐。"

## Jimmy Goggles the God / 成为神的吉米·护目镜

===Original===
“It isn’t everyone who’s been a god,” said the sunburnt man. “But it’s happened to me—among other things.”
I intimated my sense of his condescension.
“It don’t leave much for ambition, does it?” said the sunburnt man.

===Chinese===
“并不是人人都有当神的经历，”那个晒得黝黑的人说。“可这事就落到了我头上——除了别的种种之外。”
我表示领会了他这番屈尊降贵的意思。
“这事儿把人的野心都消磨光了，不是吗？”晒黑的人说。

===Original===
“I was one of those men who were saved from the *Ocean Pioneer*. Gummy! how time flies! It’s twenty years ago. I doubt if you’ll remember anything of the *Ocean Pioneer*?”
The name was familiar, and I tried to recall when and where I had read it. The *Ocean Pioneer*? “Something about gold dust,” I said vaguely, “but the precise—”
“That’s it,” he said. “In a beastly little channel she hadn’t no business in—dodging pirates. It was before they’d put the kybosh on that business. And there’d been volcanoes or something and all the rocks was wrong. There’s places about by Soona where you fair have to follow the rocks about to see where they’re going next. Down she went in twenty fathoms before you could have dealt for whist, with fifty thousand pounds worth of gold aboard, it was said, in one form or another.”

===Chinese===
“我是从‘海洋先驱号’（*Ocean Pioneer*）上被救下来的人之一。乖乖！时间过得真快！都是二十年前的事了。我拿不准你还记不记得‘海洋先驱号’？”
这名字听着耳熟，我试着回想自己是在何时何地读到过。“海洋先驱号”？“好像跟金粉有点关系，”我含含糊糊地说，“但确切的内容——”
“就是它，”他说。“在一条她本不该去的鬼狭窄的水道里——为了躲海盗。那时候他们还没取缔那行营生。那一带又有火山什么的，连礁石都长得不对劲。索纳（Soona）附近有些地方，你得追着礁石跑才能看清它们下一刻要往哪儿去。她沉下去二十英寻深，你连一局惠斯特牌都还没发完呢——据说船上载着价值五万英镑的黄金，这样那样地折算着。”

===Original===
“Survivors?”
“Three.”
“I remember the case now,” I said. “There was something about salvage—”

===Chinese===
“幸存者？”
“三个。”
“我现在想起这桩案子了，”我说，“好像跟打捞有点——”

===Original===
But at the word salvage the sunburnt man exploded into language so extraordinarily horrible that I stopped aghast. He came down to more ordinary swearing, and pulled himself up abruptly. “Excuse me,” he said, “but—salvage!”
He leant over towards me. “I was in that job,” he said. “Tried to make myself a rich man, and got made a god instead. I’ve got my feelings—”
“It ain’t all jam being a god,” said the sunburnt man, and for some time conversed by means of such pithy but unprogressive axioms. At last he took up his tale again.

===Chinese===
可一听到“打捞”这个词，那晒黑的人便爆出一串不堪入耳的脏话，吓得我瞠目结舌。他渐渐换成平常的咒骂，又猛地刹住。“恕我失礼，”他说，“可——打捞！”
他朝我探过身来。“我参与了那档子事，”他说。“本想让自己变成个富翁，结果倒被造成了神。我心里是有感触的——”
“当神也不全是甜头，”晒黑的人说，接着用诸如此类精辟却没什么进展的格言谈论了好一会儿。末了他才又接上话头。

===Original===
“There was me,” said the sunburnt man, “and a seaman named Jacobs, and Always, the mate of the *Ocean Pioneer*. And him it was that set the whole thing going. I remember him now, when we was in the jolly-boat, suggesting it all to our minds just by one sentence. He was a wonderful hand at suggesting things. ‘There was forty thousand pounds,’ he said, ‘on that ship, and it’s for me to say just where she went down.’ It didn’t need much brains to tumble to that. And he was the leader from the first to the last. He got hold of the Sanderses and their brig; they were brothers, and the brig was the *Pride of Banya*, and he it was bought the diving dress—a secondhand one with a compressed air apparatus instead of pumping. He’d have done the diving too, if it hadn’t made him sick going down. And the salvage people were mucking about with a chart he’d cooked up, as solemn as could be, at Starr Race, a hundred and twenty miles away.

===Chinese===
“当时有我，”晒黑的人说，“还有一个叫雅各布斯（Jacobs）的水手，以及‘海洋先驱号’的大副奥尔韦斯（Always）。正是他张罗起了整件事。我现在还记得，我们坐在小艇上的时候，他就用一句话把整个主意灌进了我们脑子里。他可真是个出主意的好手。‘那条船上有四万英镑，’他说，‘而她沉在哪儿，只有我说了算。’这用不着多聪明的脑瓜也能想明白。他从头到尾都是我们的头儿。他搭上了桑德斯兄弟（the Sanderses）和他们的双桅帆船；他们是两兄弟，那艘帆船叫‘班尼亚的骄傲号’（*Pride of Banya*），正是他去买的潜水服——一具二手货，用的是压缩空气装置，不用人在上面泵气。本来该他下去的，要不是他一下水就犯恶心的话。而那些正经打捞的人呢，正一百二十英里外的斯塔尔雷斯（Starr Race），围着一张他精心伪造的海图煞有介事地瞎忙活。

===Original===
“I can tell you we was a happy lot aboard that brig, jokes and drink and bright hopes all the time. It all seemed so neat and clean and straightforward, and what rough chaps call a ‘cert.’ And we used to speculate how the other blessed lot, the proper salvagers, who’d started two days before us, were getting on, until our sides fairly ached. We all messed together in the Sanderses’ cabin—it was a curious crew, all officers and no men—and there stood the diving-dress waiting its turn. Young Sanders was a humorous sort of chap, and there certainly was something funny in the confounded thing’s great fat head and its stare, and he made us see it too. ‘Jimmy Goggles,’ he used to call it, and talk to it like a Christian. Asked if he was married, and how Mrs. Goggles was, and all the little Goggleses. Fit to make you split. And every blessed day all of us used to drink the health of Jimmy Goggles in rum, and unscrew his eye and pour a glass of rum in him, until, instead of that nasty mackintosheriness, he smelt as nice in his inside as a cask of rum. It was jolly times we had in those days, I can tell you—little suspecting, poor chaps! what was a-coming.

===Chinese===
“我可以告诉你，在那艘双桅帆船上我们可真是一伙快活人，成天说说笑笑、喝酒、怀着美妙的指望。一切看起来那么利落、干净、直截了当，是那些粗人称作的‘稳当买卖’。我们常琢磨那一伙正经打捞的——比我们早出发两天的人——不知进展如何，直想得笑岔了气。我们都在桑德斯兄弟的船舱里一块儿吃饭——船员组成颇为奇特，全是头头脑脑，没有一个兵——那套潜水服就立在那儿等着轮到它上场。小桑德斯（Young Sanders）是个爱逗乐的小伙子，那玩意儿硕大的肥脑袋和直瞪瞪的眼神确实有几分滑稽，他也能让我们都看出这点来。他管它叫‘吉米·护目镜’（Jimmy Goggles），还像对待正经人似的跟它说话。问它结了婚没有，戈格尔太太可好，还有那群小戈格尔们怎么样了。逗得人肚子都要笑破。我们每天都要用朗姆酒为吉米·护目镜的健康干杯，拧开它的眼睛往里头灌一杯朗姆酒，直到它里头不再有那股难闻的胶皮味，而是像一只朗姆酒桶那样闻着香喷喷的。那些日子可真快活，我告诉你——可怜的家伙们哪曾料到，等着我们的是什么。

===Original===
“We weren’t going to throw away our chances by any blessed hurry, you know, and we spent a whole day sounding our way towards where the *Ocean Pioneer* had gone down, right between two chunks of ropy grey rock—lava rocks that rose nearly out of the water. We had to lay off about half a mile to get a safe anchorage, and there was a thundering row who should stay on board. And there she lay just as she had gone down, so that you could see the top of the masts that was still standing perfectly distinctly. The row ended in all coming in the boat. I went down in the diving-dress on Friday morning directly it was light.

===Chinese===
“你知道，我们不会因为急着赶工就白白丢掉机会，我们花了整整一天边测水深边朝‘海洋先驱号’沉没的地方摸过去——正好夹在两大块灰色的绳状熔岩之间，那些熔岩几乎露出水面。我们不得不在半英里外下锚以求稳妥，接着大吵了一架，争谁该留在船上。她就那样躺在那儿，和沉下去时一模一样，你甚至能清清楚楚地看见还立着的那些桅杆的顶端。争吵的结果是谁都进了小艇。星期五一清早天刚亮，我就穿着潜水服下去了。

===Original===
“What a surprise it was! I can see it all now quite distinctly. It was a queer-looking place, and the light was just coming. People over here think every blessed place in the tropics is a flat shore and palm-trees and surf, bless ’em! This place, for instance, wasn’t a bit that way. Not common rocks they were, undermined by waves; but great curved banks like ironwork cinder heaps, with green slime below, and thorny shrubs and things just waving upon them here and there, and the water glassy calm and clear, and showing you a kind of dirty gray-black shine, with huge flaring red-brown weeds spreading motionless, and crawling and darting things going through it. And far away beyond the ditches and pools and the heaps was a forest on the mountain flank, growing again after the fires and cinder showers of the last eruption. And the other way forest, too, and a kind of broken—what is it?—amby-theatre of black and rusty cinders rising out of it all, and the sea in a kind of bay in the middle.

===Chinese===
“那景象真叫人吃惊！我现在仍能看得一清二楚。那是个样子古怪的地方，天光才刚亮起来。咱们这边的人以为热带的每一个地方都是平坦的海岸、椰子树和拍岸的浪花，他们可真是好心肠！就说这地方吧，压根儿不是那么回事。那不是被海浪掏空的普通礁石，而是巨大的弧形堆岸，像铁厂的炉渣堆，底下覆着绿色的黏泥，上面到处有带刺的灌木之类的东西在摇摆，海水平静清澈如玻璃，映出一种脏兮兮的灰黑色光泽，大片大片红褐色的海草纹丝不动地铺展开，还有些爬的、窜的东西在其中穿梭。远远地越过那些沟渠、水洼和石堆，山坡上有一片森林，在上一次喷发的烈火和火山灰雨之后重新长了起来。另一边也是森林，还有一座残破的——怎么说来着？——像露天剧场似的黑色锈迹斑斑的火山灰堆，从这一切之间拔起，大海则嵌在中间的一个海湾里。

===Original===
“The dawn, I say, was just coming, and there wasn’t much colour about things, and not a human being but ourselves anywhere in sight up or down the channel. Except the *Pride of Banya*, lying out beyond a lump of rocks towards the line of the sea.
“Not a human being in sight,” he repeated, and paused.

===Chinese===
“我说，天刚刚破晓，万物都没什么颜色，沿着水道上下游放眼望去，除了我们自己，连一个人影也看不见。只有‘班尼亚的骄傲号’远远地泊在一堆礁石外面，朝着海天一线的方向。
“一个人影也看不见，”他重复了一遍，停顿了一下。

===Original===
“I don’t know where they came from, not a bit. And we were feeling so safe that we were all alone that poor young Sanders was a-singing. I was in Jimmy Goggles, all except the helmet. ‘Easy,’ says Always, ‘there’s her mast.’ And after I’d had just one squint over the gunwale, I caught up the bogey, and almost tipped out as old Sanders brought the boat round. When the windows were screwed and everything was all right, I shut the valve from the air-belt in order to help my sinking, and jumped overboard, feet foremost—for we hadn’t a ladder. I left the boat pitching, and all of them staring down into water after me, as my head sank down into the weeds and blackness that lay about the mast. I suppose nobody, not the most cautious chap in the world, would have bothered about a lookout at such a desolate place. It stunk of solitude.

===Chinese===
“他们是从哪儿冒出来的，我一点都不知道。我们正觉得万无一失，以为周围就只有我们自己，可怜的小桑德斯还唱起了歌。我已经穿好了吉米·护目镜，就差头盔了。‘稳着点，’奥尔韦斯说，‘那就是她的桅杆。’我朝船舷外只瞥了一眼，便一把抄起那个家伙，老桑德斯（old Sanders）把小艇转过来时我差点儿栽出去。等窗口拧紧、一切就绪，我关上空气带上的阀门好帮助自己下沉，然后跳进了海里——脚先下水，因为我们没有梯子。我留下那艘小艇在颠簸，所有人都目不转睛地朝水里盯着我，而我的头则沉入了桅杆周围的海草和黑暗之中。我估摸着，哪怕是天下最谨慎的人，在这么荒凉的地方也不会费心去安排个望风的。那地方荒凉得直透出一股孤独味儿。

===Original===
“Of course you must understand that I was a greenhorn at diving. None of us were divers. We’d had to muck about with the thing to get the way of it, and this was the first time I’d been deep. It feels damnable. Your ears hurt beastly. I don’t know if you’ve ever hurt yourself yawning or sneezing, but it takes you like that, only ten times worse. And a pain over the eyebrows here—splitting—and a feeling like influenza in the head. And it isn’t all heaven in your lungs and things. And going down feels like the beginning of a lift, only it keeps on. And you can’t turn your head to see what’s above you, and you can’t get a fair squint at what’s happening to your feet without bending down something painful. And being deep it was dark, let alone the blackness of the ashes and mud that formed the bottom. It was like going down out of the dawn back into the night, so to speak.

===Chinese===
“当然你得明白，我在潜水这行当上还是个生手。我们一伙人都不是潜水员。我们只能瞎摆弄那玩意儿摸索出门道，而这还是我头一次下深水。那滋味真是糟透了。耳朵疼得要命。我不知道你有没有过打哈欠或打喷嚏时伤到自己，那感觉就类似那样，只不过厉害十倍。眉毛这儿还疼——劈裂似的——脑袋里像得了流感。肺和五脏六腑里也绝不是什么好受的滋味。下沉的感觉就像电梯刚开始下降那一刹那，只不过它一直不停。你没法回头去看头顶上是什么，想正眼瞧瞧脚下发生了什么，就得弯下腰去，疼得厉害。水又深，自然是暗的，更别说海底全是黑色的火山灰和淤泥了。可以说，就像从黎明一路降回到黑夜里去。

===Original===
“The mast came up like a ghost out of the black, and then a lot of fishes, and then a lot of flapping red seaweed, and then whack I came with a kind of dull bang on the deck of the *Ocean Pioneer*, and the fishes that had been feeding on the dead rose about me like a swarm of flies from road stuff in summertime. I turned on the compressed air again—for the suit was a bit thick and mackintoshery after all, in spite of the rum—and stood recovering myself. It struck coolish down there, and that helped take off the stuffiness a bit.”

===Chinese===
“桅杆像幽灵一样从黑暗中升起，接着是一大群鱼，然后是大片飘动的红色海草，再然后，我‘砰’的一声闷响落在了‘海洋先驱号’的甲板上，那些一直在啃食尸体的鱼群在我四周惊起，像夏日里路上的粪堆惊起的一群苍蝇。我又拧开了压缩空气——毕竟这套衣服还是有些厚、有些胶皮味，朗姆酒也压不住——站定喘了口气。下面凉丝丝的，倒也让那股闷气消散了些。”

===Original===
“When I began to feel easier, I started looking about me. It was an extraordinary sight. Even the light was extraordinary, a kind of reddy-coloured twilight, on account of the streamers of seaweed that floated up on either side of the ship. And far overhead just a moony, deep green blue. The deck of the ship, except for a slight list to starboard, was level, and lay all dark and long between the weeds, clear except where the masts had snapped when she rolled, and vanishing into black night towards the forecastle. There wasn’t any dead on the decks, most were in the weeds alongside, I suppose; but afterwards I found two skeletons lying in the passengers’ cabins, where death had come to them. It was curious to stand on that deck and recognise it all, bit by bit; a place against the rail where I’d been fond of smoking by starlight, and the corner where an old chap from Sydney used to flirt with a widow we had aboard. A comfortable couple they’d been, only a month ago, and now you couldn’t have got a meal for a baby crab off either of them.

===Chinese===
“等我喘过劲来，便开始四下打量。那景象真是不同寻常。就连光线也透着古怪——是一种泛红的暮色，因为船体两侧飘浮着一缕缕的海草。而高远的头顶上，是一片月亮般深沉的绿蓝色。船的甲板除了略微向右舷倾斜之外，大体是平的，在海草之间又暗又长地铺展开，除了船身摇晃时折断桅杆的地方之外都空荡荡的，朝船头那头则消失在漆黑的夜里。甲板上没有尸体，大多数大概都漂到了旁边的海草里；但后来我在客舱里发现了两具骷髅，死神就是在那儿找到他们的。站在那片甲板上，一点一点把一切都认出来，那感觉很奇妙：栏杆边我从前爱在星光下抽烟的那个地方，还有一位从悉尼来的老伙计从前爱跟我们船上一位寡妇调情的那个角落。这一对相好的才不过一个月前还活得舒舒服服的，如今你就算想从他们身上刮下一点肉来喂一只小螃蟹都办不到了。

===Original===
“I’ve always had a bit of a philosophical turn, and I daresay I spent the best part of five minutes in such thoughts before I went below to find where the blessed dust was stored. It was slow work hunting, feeling it was for the most part, pitchy dark, with confusing blue gleams down the companion. And there were things moving about, a dab at my glass once, and once a pinch at my leg. Crabs, I expect. I kicked a lot of loose stuff that puzzled me, and stooped and picked up something all knobs and spikes. What do you think? Backbone! But I never had any particular feeling for bones. We had talked the affair over pretty thoroughly, and Always knew just where the stuff was stowed. I found it that trip. I lifted a box one end an inch or more.”

===Chinese===
“我向来有点儿哲思的癖好，我敢说，在下去找那些宝贝金粉存放在哪儿之前，我足足花了快五分钟做这番感慨。搜寻的工作进展很慢，多半只能靠摸，四下里漆黑一片，舱口处只有令人迷惑的蓝色微光。还有些东西在四处游动，有一次在我面罩玻璃上戳了一下，还有一次在我腿上掐了一把。我猜是螃蟹。我踢到了一堆叫人纳闷的零碎东西，弯腰摸起一样全是疙瘩和尖刺的物件。你猜是什么？脊骨！不过我对骨头向来没什么特别的感触。我们事先把这事商量得很透彻，奥尔韦斯清楚金子到底藏在哪儿。那一趟我就找到了。我把一只箱子的一头抬起了一英寸多。”

===Original===
He broke off in his story. “I’ve lifted it,” he said, “as near as that! Forty thousand pounds’ worth of pure gold! Gold! I shouted inside my helmet as a kind of cheer, and hurt my ears. I was getting confounded stuffy and tired by this time—I must have been down twenty-five minutes or more—and I thought this was good enough. I went up the companion again, and as my eyes came up flush with the deck, a thundering great crab gave a kind of hysterical jump and went scuttling off sideways. Quite a start it gave me. I stood up clear on deck and shut the valve behind the helmet to let the air accumulate to carry me up again—I noticed a kind of whacking from above, as though they were hitting the water with an oar, but I didn’t look up. I fancied they were signalling me to come up.

===Chinese===
他中断了叙述。“我把它抬起来了，”他说，“就差那么一点儿！四万英镑的纯金！黄金！我在头盔里大喊了一声权作欢呼，震得自己耳朵疼。到这时候我已经闷得要命、累得要命——我肯定在水下待了二十五分钟以上了——心想这就够了。我顺着舱口又爬了上去，眼睛刚与甲板齐平，一只硕大无朋的螃蟹像发了癔症似的一蹦，横着身子溜走了。吓了我好大一跳。我在甲板上挺直身子站好，关上头盔后面的阀门，好让空气积聚起来把我往上送——我注意到头顶上有一种啪啪的拍打声，好像他们正用桨拍打水面，但我没抬头看。我猜他们是在示意我上去。

===Original===
“And then something shot down by me—something heavy, and stood a-quiver in the planks. I looked, and there was a long knife I’d seen young Sanders handling. Thinks I, he’s dropped it, and I was still calling him this kind of fool and that—for it might have hurt me serious—when I began to lift and drive up towards the daylight. Just about the level of the top spars of the *Ocean Pioneer*, whack! I came against something sinking down, and a boot knocked in front of my helmet. Then something else, struggling frightful. It was a big weight atop of me, whatever it was, and moving and twisting about. I’d have thought it a big octopus, or some such thing, if it hadn’t been for the boot. But octopuses don’t wear boots. It was all in a moment, of course.

===Chinese===
“接着有件东西从我身旁射下去——沉甸甸的，扎进木板还在颤动。我一看，是一把长刀，我见过小桑德斯摆弄它。我心想，是他把刀弄掉了，我正把他这个那个地骂着傻瓜——那刀本可能把我伤得不轻呢——这时我开始上浮，朝光亮处冲去。大约到了‘海洋先驱号’最高桅桁的高度时，啪！我撞上了某个正在下沉的东西，一只靴子在我头盔前面磕了一下。然后又是别的什么东西，拼命地挣扎。不管那是什么，重重地压在我身上，还在扭来扭去。要不是那只靴子，我还当是一只大章鱼之类的玩意儿呢。可章鱼不穿靴子。当然，这都是一眨眼的事。

===Original===
“I felt myself sinking down again, and I threw my arms about to keep steady, and the whole lot rolled free of me and shot down as I went up—”
He paused.
“I saw young Sanders’s face, over a naked black shoulder, and a spear driven clean through his neck, and out of his mouth and neck what looked like spirts of pink smoke in the water. And down they went clutching one another, and turning over, and both too far gone to leave go. And in another second my helmet came a whack, fit to split, against the niggers’ canoe. It was niggers! Two canoes full.

===Chinese===
“我感到自己又往下沉，便张开双臂稳住身子，那一整团东西便从我身上滚开，我往上升时它们射了下去——”
他停了一下。
“我看见小桑德斯的脸，伏在一具赤裸的黑色肩膀上，一支长矛干净利落地洞穿了他的脖子，从他嘴里和脖子里喷出来的，在水里看来像是一团团粉红色的烟。他们紧紧攥着彼此，一路翻滚着沉下去，两个人都早已无力松手了。又过了一秒，我的头盔‘砰’的一声，险些裂开，撞上了那些黑人的独木舟。是黑人！满满两独木舟。

===Original===
“It was lively times I tell you? Overboard came Always with three spears in him. There was the legs of three or four black chaps kicking about me in the water. I couldn’t see much, but I saw the game was up at a glance, gave my valve a tremendous twist, and went bubbling down again after poor Always, in as awful a state of scare and astonishment as you can well imagine. I passed young Sanders and the nigger going up again and struggling still a bit, and in another moment I was standing in the dim again on the deck of the *Ocean Pioneer*.

===Chinese===
“那可真是热闹的时候呢，我告诉你？奥尔韦斯带着三支长矛翻下了水。我四周的水里，有三四个黑人的腿在乱蹬。我看不太清楚，但一眼就明白全完了，我把阀门狠狠一拧，冒着泡又沉下去，追着可怜的奥尔韦斯——那惊骇万状的模样，你尽可以想象。我上升时又与小桑德斯和那个黑人擦肩而过，他们还在挣扎，再过一会儿，我又站在了‘海洋先驱号’昏暗的甲板上。

===Original===
“Gummy, thinks I, here’s a fix! Niggers? At first I couldn’t see anything for it but Stifle below or Stabs above. I didn’t properly understand how much air there was to last me out, but I didn’t feel like standing very much more of it down below. I was hot and frightfully heady, quite apart from the blue funk I was in. We’d never reckoned with these beastly natives, filthy Papuan beasts. It wasn’t any good coming up where I was, but I had to do something. On the spur of the moment, I clambered over the side of the brig and landed among the weeds, and set off through the darkness as fast as I could. I just stopped once and knelt, and twisted back my head in the helmet and had a look up. It was a most extraordinary bright green-blue above, and the two canoes and the boat floating there very small and distant like a kind of twisted H. And it made me feel sick to squint up at it, and think what the pitching and swaying of the three meant.

===Chinese===
“‘乖乖，’我心想，‘这下可麻烦了！’黑人？起初我想不出别的出路，除了‘在底下闷死’或者‘在上面挨刀子’。我也搞不清自己还剩多少空气能撑下去，可我不想再在底下耗下去了。我浑身燥热、头昏脑涨，更别提心里那阵要命的恐惧了。我们压根儿没把这些该死的土著——那些肮脏的巴布亚（Papuan）畜生——算计在内。从我所在的地方冒上去是不行的，可我总得做点什么。情急之下，我翻过双桅帆船的船舷，落到海草丛中，拼命地在黑暗里穿行。我只停下来一次，跪下，在头盔里扭过头朝上望了一眼。头顶上方是一片奇异明亮的绿蓝色，那两只独木舟和小艇浮在那儿，又小又远，像一个扭曲的‘H’字形。仰望着它，想着那三艘船颠簸摇晃意味着什么，我只觉得一阵恶心。

===Original===
“It was just about the most horrible ten minutes I ever had, blundering about in that darkness—pressure something awful, like being buried in sand, pain across the chest, sick with funk, and breathing nothing as it seemed but the smell of rum and mackintosh. Gummy! After a bit, I found myself going up a steepish sort of slope. I had another squint to see if anything was visible of the canoes and boats, and then kept on. I stopped with my head a foot from the surface, and tried to see where I was going, but, of course, nothing was to be seen but the reflection of the bottom. Then out I dashed, like knocking my head through a mirror. Directly I got my eyes out of the water, I saw I’d come up a kind of beach near the forest. I had a look round, but the natives and the brig were both hidden by a big hummucky heap of twisted lava. The born fool in me suggested a run for the woods. I didn’t take the helmet off, but I eased open one of the windows, and, after a bit of a pant, went on out of the water. You’d hardly imagine how clean and light the air tasted.

===Chinese===
“那大概是我这辈子最难熬的十分钟了，在黑暗里跌跌撞撞——水压大得可怕，像被埋在沙子里，胸口一阵阵疼，吓得要吐，吸进去的仿佛全是朗姆酒和胶皮的气味。乖乖！过了一会儿，我发觉自己在爬一个相当陡的斜坡。我又偷瞧了一眼，看看独木舟和小艇是否在视野里，然后继续往前走。我在头部离水面一英尺处停下，想看清自己往哪儿走，可当然了，能看见的只有水底的倒影。然后我猛地冲了出去，像用脑袋撞穿一面镜子。眼睛一露出水面，我就看见自己上了一个靠近森林的海滩。我四下张望，可土著和双桅帆船都被一大堆坑坑洼洼、扭曲的熔岩挡住了。我天性里那股傻劲儿撺掇我往树林里跑。我没摘头盔，只是拧松了其中一扇小窗，喘了几口，便走出了水面。你简直想象不到那空气尝起来有多么清新、多么轻盈。

===Original===
“Of course, with four inches of lead in your boot soles, and your head in a copper knob the size of a football, and been thirty-five minutes under water, you don’t break any records running. I ran like a ploughboy going to work. And halfway to the trees I saw a dozen niggers or more, coming out in a gaping, astonished sort of way to meet me.

===Chinese===
“当然，靴底里垫着四英寸厚的铅，脑袋塞在一个足球大的铜疙瘩里，又在水底下待了三十五分钟，你跑起来可创不了任何纪录。我跑得像个下地干活的农家小子。离树林还有一半路时，我看见十几个黑人——也许更多——目瞪口呆、一脸惊愕地迎了出来。

===Original===
“I just stopped dead, and cursed myself for all the fools out of London. I had about as much chance of cutting back to the water as a turned turtle. I just screwed up my window again to leave my hands free, and waited for them. There wasn’t anything else for me to do.

===Chinese===
“我戛然止步，把自己骂成全伦敦头号大傻瓜。我想掉头跑回水里，机会跟一只四脚朝天的乌龟差不多。我干脆把小窗重新拧紧，腾出双手，等着他们。我也没别的办法。

===Original===
“But they didn’t come on very much. I began to suspect why. ‘Jimmy Goggles,’ I says, ‘it’s your beauty does it.’ I was inclined to be a little lightheaded, I think, with all these dangers about and the change in the pressure of the blessed air. ‘Who’re ye staring at?’ I said, as if the savages could hear me. ‘What d’ye take me for? I’m hanged if I don’t give you something to stare at,’ I said, and with that I screwed up the escape valve and turned on the compressed air from the belt, until I was swelled out like a blown frog. Regular imposing it must have been. I’m blessed if they’d come on a step; and presently one and then another went down on their hands and knees. They didn’t know what to make of me, and they was doing the extra polite, which was very wise and reasonable of them. I had half a mind to edge back seaward and cut and run, but it seemed too hopeless. A step back and they’d have been after me. And out of sheer desperation I began to march towards them up the beach, with slow, heavy steps, and waving my blown-out arms about, in a dignified manner. And inside of me I was singing as small as a tomtit.

===Chinese===
“可他们并没有怎么往前凑。我开始猜到原因了。‘吉米·护目镜，’我自言自语，‘是你这副尊容管用。’我想，在这重重危险之下，又加上那宝贝空气的气压变化，我有些犯晕乎了。‘你们盯着我瞧什么呢？’我说，好像那些野人能听见我似的。‘你们把我当成什么了？我要是不给你们点东西瞧瞧，我就不姓这个，’我说着便拧紧排气阀，又打开空气带上的压缩空气，直到自己胀得像一只鼓足了气的青蛙。那场面一定相当威风。他们硬是一步也不敢上前；不一会儿，一个接一个地双膝着地跪了下去。他们不知该怎么对付我，便格外恭敬起来——他们这么做可谓明智得很，合情合理。我半想朝海边挪、开溜拉倒，可又觉得太没指望。退一步，他们准会追上来。我只好硬着头皮，绝望地迈着缓慢沉重的步子，朝他们走去，挥舞着鼓胀的双臂，做出一副庄严的样子。可我心里头，却怯生生得像只小山雀。

===Original===
“But there’s nothing like a striking appearance to help a man over a difficulty—I’ve found that before and since. People like ourselves, who’re up to diving dresses by the time we’re seven, can scarcely imagine the effect of one on a simple-minded savage. One or two of these niggers cut and run, the others started in a great hurry trying to knock their brains out on the ground. And on I went as slow and solemn and silly-looking and artful as a jobbing plumber. It was evident they took me for something immense.

===Chinese===
“不过，再没有什么比一副惹眼的尊容更能帮人渡过难关了——我前后都不止一次领教过。像我们这样的人，七岁起就对潜水服见怪不怪，很难想象它对一个心思单纯的野人有怎样的效果。那一两个黑人掉头就跑，其余的则手忙脚乱地扑倒在地，好像要把自己的脑袋往地上撞。我继续向前走，慢吞吞、一本正经、一脸傻相又暗藏狡黠，活像一个打零工的水暖工。他们显然把我当成了某种了不起的存在。

===Original===
“Then up jumped one and began pointing, making extraordinary gestures to me as he did so, and all the others began sharing their attention between me and something out at sea. ‘What’s the matter now?’ I said. I turned slowly on account of my dignity, and there I saw, coming round a point, the poor old *Pride of Banya* towed by a couple of canoes. The sight fairly made me sick. But they evidently expected some recognition, so I waved my arms in a striking sort of noncommittal manner. And then I turned and stalked on towards the trees again. At that time I was praying like mad, I remember, over and over again: ‘Lord help me through with it! Lord help me through with it!’ It’s only fools who know nothing of danger can afford to laugh at praying.”

===Chinese===
“这时有一个人跳起来，一边朝我比划着各种古怪的手势，一边指指点点，其余的人都把注意力在我和海上某样东西之间来回分着。‘又怎么了？’我说。我顾及尊严，缓缓转过身，只见‘班尼亚的骄傲号’那可怜的老船被两只独木舟拖着，正绕过一处海角过来。那景象看得我心里直犯恶心。可他们显然期待我有所表示，我便挥动双臂，做出一种既引人注目又不表态的样子。然后我转身，迈着大步朝树林走去。我记得那时我疯了似的祈祷，一遍又一遍：‘主啊，保佑我熬过去！主啊，保佑我熬过去！’只有那些对危险一无所知的傻瓜，才笑得出人家祈祷。”

===Original===
“But these niggers weren’t going to let me walk through and away like that. They started a kind of bowing dance about me, and sort of pressed me to take a pathway that lay through the trees. It was clear to me they didn’t take me for a British citizen, whatever else they thought of me, and for my own part I was never less anxious to own up to the old country.

===Chinese===
“可这些黑人不会让我就这么穿过去走掉的。他们围着我跳起一种鞠躬似的舞蹈，半推半就地要我把脚步拐进一条穿过树林的小径。我很清楚，不管他们把我当成什么，绝不是把我当成英国公民，而就我自己来说，我也从没像此刻这样巴不得跟祖国撇清关系。

===Original===
“You’d hardly believe it, perhaps, unless you’re familiar with savages, but these poor, misguided, ignorant creatures took me straight to their kind of joss place to present me to the blessed old black stone there. By this time I was beginning to sort of realise the depth of their ignorance, and directly I set eyes on this deity I took my cue. I started a baritone howl, ‘wow-wow,’ very long on one note, and began waving my arms about a lot, and then very slowly and ceremoniously turned their image over on its side and sat down on it. I wanted to sit down badly, for diving dresses ain’t much wear in the tropics. Or, to put it different like, they’re a sight too much. It took away their breath, I could see, my sitting on their joss, but in less time than a minute they made up their minds and were hard at work worshipping me. And I can tell you I felt a bit relieved to see things turning out so well, in spite of the weight on my shoulders and feet.

===Chinese===
“你大概很难相信，除非你对野人有所了解，但这些可怜的、误入歧途的、愚昧无知的生灵，竟直接把我领到了他们的神庙之类的地方，把我引见给那里一块黑乎乎的老石头。到这时，我才算多少意识到他们无知到何种地步，一瞧见那尊神像，我便心领神会。我发出一声男中音般的嚎叫，‘呜——呜——’，一个调子拖得老长，胳膊大幅度地乱舞一气，然后慢条斯理、煞有介事地把他们的神像掀翻在地，一屁股坐了上去。我太想坐下来了，因为潜水服在热带可不大好穿。或者换个说法，它未免也太累赘了。我看得出来，我坐到他们的神像上让他们倒抽了一口冷气，可不到一分钟，他们就打定了主意，正儿八经地拜起我来。尽管肩上脚上还压着分量，事情能这样转危为安，我多少松了口气。

===Original===
“But what made me anxious was what the chaps in the canoes might think when they came back. If they’d seen me in the boat before I went down, and without the helmet on—for they might have been spying and hiding since over night—they would very likely take a different view from the others. I was in a deuce of a stew about that for hours, as it seemed, until the shindy of the arrival began.

===Chinese===
“可让我揪心的是，独木舟上那帮人回来时会怎么想。如果他们在我下水之前就看见我在小艇上，而且我没戴头盔——因为他们很可能从头天夜里就一直在窥探、躲藏——那他们多半会跟其他人有不同的看法。这事让我如坐针毡了好几个钟头，一直熬到他们抵达时那阵喧天闹腾开始。

===Original===
“But they took it down—the whole blessed village took it down. At the cost of sitting up stiff and stern, as much like those sitting Egyptian images one sees as I could manage, for pretty nearly twelve hours, I should guess at least, on end, I got over it. You’d hardly think what it meant in that heat and stink. I don’t think any of them dreamt of the man inside. I was just a wonderful leathery great joss that had come up with luck out of the water. But the fatigue! the heat! the beastly closeness! the mackintosheriness and the rum! and the fuss! They lit a stinking fire on a kind of lava slab there was before me, and brought in a lot of gory muck—the worst parts of what they were feasting on outside, the beasts—and burnt it all in my honour. I was getting a bit hungry, but I understand now how gods manage to do without eating, what with the smell of burnt-offerings about them. And they brought in a lot of the stuff they’d got off the brig and, among other stuff, what I was a bit relieved to see, the kind of pneumatic pump that was used for the compressed air affair, and then a lot of chaps and girls came in and danced about me something disgraceful. It’s extraordinary the different ways different people have of showing respect. If I’d had a hatchet handy I’d have gone for the lot of them—they made me feel that wild. All this time I sat as stiff as company, not knowing anything better to do. And at last, when nightfall came, and the wattle joss-house place got a bit too shadowy for their taste—all these here savages are afraid of the dark, you know—and I started a sort of ‘Moo’ noise, they built big bonfires outside and left me alone in peace in the darkness of my hut, free to unscrew my windows a bit and think things over, and feel just as bad as I liked. And Lord! I was sick.

===Chinese===
“可他们全信了——全村上下都信了。代价是我得直挺挺、严肃地坐着，尽我所能模仿那些坐姿的埃及神像的样子，一连坐了将近十二个钟头——我估摸着至少——才算过关。你简直想不到在那酷热和臭气里那是什么滋味。我估计他们谁也没梦见里面还藏着个人。在他们眼里，我不过是一具神奇的、皮革似的硕大神像，运气好得很，从水里冒了出来。可那份累！那份热！那股闷！胶皮味儿加朗姆酒味儿！还有那份忙乱！他们在面前的一块熔岩石板上点起一堆臭烘烘的火，搬来一堆血淋淋的脏东西——那些在外面大嚼的畜生挑出来的最差的部位——全烧了来敬我。我也开始有点饿了，可我现在总算明白神明们是怎样做到不用吃饭的了——身边尽是烧供品的气味嘛。他们还搬来了不少从双桅帆船上弄来的东西，其中——让我稍稍松了口气的是——有那种给压缩空气装置用的气泵，然后又进来一大群汉子和姑娘，围着我跳起不堪入目的舞来。不同的人表达敬意的方式竟如此不同，真是一桩奇事。要是我手边有把斧头，我非冲过去把他们全劈了不可——他们把我烦得那样火大。这期间我一直像招待客人似的端坐着，因为也想不出更好的招。末了，夜幕降临，那座枝条编的神庙在他们看来阴影太重——你知道，这些野人都怕黑——我又发出一种‘哞——’的声音，他们便在外面生起一堆堆大篝火，把我一个人留在小屋里清净，让我可以稍稍拧松几扇小窗，把事情盘算盘算，爱多难受就多难受。老天！我真是难受坏了。

===Original===
“I was weak and hungry, and my mind kept on behaving like a beetle on a pin, tremendous activity and nothing done at the end of it. Come round just where it was before. There was sorrowing for the other chaps, beastly drunkards certainly, but not deserving such a fate, and young Sanders with the spear through his neck wouldn’t go out of my mind. There was the treasure down there in the *Ocean Pioneer*, and how one might get it and hide it somewhere safer, and get away and come back for it. And there was the puzzle where to get anything to eat. I tell you I was fair rambling. I was afraid to ask by signs for food, for fear of behaving too human, and so there I sat and hungered until very near the dawn. Then the village got a bit quiet, and I couldn’t stand it any longer, and I went out and got some stuff like artichokes in a bowl and some sour milk. What was left of these I put away among the other offerings, just to give them a hint of my tastes. And in the morning they came to worship, and found me sitting up stiff and respectable on their previous god, just as they’d left me overnight. I’d got my back against the central pillar of the hut, and, practically, I was asleep. And that’s how I became a god among the heathen—false god, no doubt, and blasphemous, but one can’t always pick and choose.

===Chinese===
“我又虚又饿，脑子却像一只插在针上的甲虫，活动剧烈得很，到头来却什么也没想出来，又回到原来的地方。我为其他几个伙计悲伤——他们确实是些糟糕的酒鬼，但罪不至此——还有脖子里插着长矛的小桑德斯，老在我脑子里挥之不去。再有就是‘海洋先驱号’底下的那批金子，怎么才能把它弄到手、藏到一个更稳妥的地方，然后脱身，日后再回来取。还有从哪儿弄点吃的这个难题。我告诉你，我那脑子东想西想地乱跑。我不敢用手势讨吃的，怕显得太像凡人，于是我就那么坐着挨饿，一直挨到快天亮。后来村子里安静了些，我实在熬不住，便出去摸到了一碗洋蓟似的东西和一些酸牛奶。吃剩的我就混在其他供品里，好给他们透点我的口味。等到了早上，他们来膜拜，发现我仍端端正正、体体面面地坐在他们旧日神祇上，就像他们头天夜里把我留下的那样。我背靠着小屋中央的柱子，其实已经睡着了。我就是这样成了异教徒中的神——当然是个伪神，还是亵渎神明的，可人总不能事事挑挑拣拣。

===Original===
“Now, I don’t want to crack myself up as a god beyond my merits, but I must confess that while I was god to these people they was extraordinary successful. I don’t say there’s anything in it, mind you. They won a battle with another tribe—I got a lot of offerings I didn’t want through it—they had wonderful fishing, and their crop of pourra was exceptional fine. And they counted the capture of the brig among the benefits I brought ’em. I must say I don’t think that was a poor record for a perfectly new hand. And, though perhaps you’d scarcely credit it, I was the tribal god of those beastly savages for pretty nearly four months…
“What else could I do, man? But I didn’t wear that diving-dress all the time. I made ’em rig me up a sort of holy of holies, and a deuce of a time I had too, making them understand what it was I wanted them to do. That indeed was the great difficulty—making them understand my wishes. I couldn’t let myself down by talking their lingo badly, even if I’d been able to speak at all, and I couldn’t go flapping a lot of gestures at them. So I drew pictures in sand and sat down beside them and hooted like one o’clock. Sometimes they did the things I wanted all right, and sometimes they did them all wrong. They was always very willing, certainly. All the while I was puzzling how I was to get the confounded business settled. Every night before the dawn I used to march out in full rig and go off to a place where I could see the channel in which the *Ocean Pioneer* lay sunk, and once even, one moonlight night, I tried to walk out to her, but the weeds and rocks and dark clean beat me. I didn’t get back till full day, and then I found all those silly niggers out on the beach praying their sea-god to return to them. I was that vexed and tired, messing and tumbling about, and coming up and going down again, I could have punched their silly heads all round when they started rejoicing. Hanged if I like so much ceremony.

===Chinese===
“当然，我不想以神自吹、超过自己的功劳，但我得承认，在我做这些人的神期间，他们出奇地顺利。我可没说这跟我有什么关系，你懂的。他们打赢了跟另一个部落的一仗——为此我得了一大堆我不想要的供品——他们捕鱼丰收，蓬德拉（pourra）庄稼也格外好。他们还把俘获那艘双桅帆船算作我带给他们的恩惠。我得说，对一介新手来说，这成绩不算寒碜。而且，虽然你大概很难相信，我在那群该死的野人里头当了差不多四个月的部落神……
“我还能怎样呢，老兄？不过我并没有成天穿着那套潜水服。我让他们给我搭了个类似至圣所的地方，要让他们明白我想让他们干什么，可费了老鼻子劲了。那才是真正的难处——让他们明白我的心思。我不能自降身价，操一口蹩脚的土话跟他们说话——就算我能开口的话——又不能冲他们比划一大堆手势。于是我在沙地上画画，坐在旁边呜呜乱叫。有时他们把事情办得妥妥帖帖，有时又全办砸。不过他们倒总是十分殷勤。我一直在琢磨怎么把这桩破事收场。每天拂晓前，我都全副武装地出去，走到一个能看见‘海洋先驱号’沉没那条水道的地方，甚至有一次，一个月光之夜，我试着走过去，可海草、礁石和黑暗彻底把我打败了。我直到大天亮才回去，结果发现那帮傻乎乎的黑人全跪在海滩上，祈祷他们的海神归来。我又气又累，跌跌撞撞、上上下下地折腾，他们一开始欢天喜地，我简直想把他们一个个的傻脑袋全揍一遍。我才不稀罕这么多礼数呢。

===Original===
“And then came the missionary. That missionary! *What* a Guy! Gummy! It was in the afternoon, and I was sitting in state in my outer temple place, sitting on that old black stone of theirs, when he came. I heard a row outside and jabbering, and then his voice speaking to an interpreter. ‘They worship stocks and stones,’ he said, and I knew what was up, in a flash. I had one of my windows out for comfort, and I sang out straight away on the spur of the moment. ‘Stocks and stones!’ I says. ‘You come inside,’ I says, ‘and I’ll punch your blooming Exeter Hall of a head.’

===Chinese===
“后来来了个传教士。那个传教士！真是个活宝！乖乖！那是一个下午，我正威风凛凛地坐在外殿里，坐在他们那块黑色的老石头上，他就来了。我听见外面一阵喧哗和叽里呱啦，然后是他的声音在对一个翻译说话。‘他们崇拜木石，’他说，我一下子就明白了怎么回事。为了凉快，我开着一扇小窗，情急之下立马嚷了出来：‘木石！’我说。‘你进来，’我说，‘我揍扁你那颗该死的埃克塞特会堂脑袋。’

===Original===
“There was a kind of silence and more jabbering, and in he came, Bible in hand, after the manner of them—a little sandy chap in specks and a pith helmet. I flatter myself that me sitting there in the shadows, with my copper head and my big goggles, struck him a bit of a heap at first. ‘Well,’ I says, ‘how’s the trade in scissors?’ for I don’t hold with missionaries.

===Chinese===
“屋里静了一下，又是一阵叽里呱啦，然后他进来了，按他们那一行的做派，手捧《圣经》——一个头发沙色的小个子，戴着眼镜，顶着顶木髓帽。我倒敢说，我坐在阴影里，顶着一颗铜脑袋、一双大护目镜，一开始确实让他愣住了。‘哎呀，’我说，‘剪刀生意怎么样？’因为我看不上传教士。

===Original===
“I had a lark with that missionary. He was a raw hand, and quite outclassed by a man like me. He gasped out who was I, and I told him to read the inscription at my feet if he wanted to know. There wasn’t no inscription; why should there be? but down he goes to read, and his interpreter, being of course as superstitious as any of them, more so by reason of his seeing missionary close to, took it for an act of worship and plumped down like a shot. All my people gave a howl of triumph, and there wasn’t any more business to be done in my village after that journey, not by the likes of him.

===Chinese===
“我拿那传教士开了一回心。他是个生手，碰上我这样的人可完全不是对手。他喘着气问我是谁，我叫他要是想知道，就读读我脚边的铭文。哪儿有什么铭文；凭什么要有？可他还是低头去读，而他的翻译——当然和他们所有人一样迷信，甚至更甚，因为他在近处见识过传教士——把这当成膜拜，扑通一声就跪了下去。我的人都发出一声胜利的嚎叫，那一趟之后，我的村子里再也没法做什么传教的事了——至少他这种人是不行了。

===Original===
“But, of course, I was a fool to choke him off like that. If I’d had any sense I should have told him straight away of the treasure and taken him into Co. I’ve no doubt he’d have come into Co. A child, with a few hours to think it over, could have seen the connection between my diving dress and the loss of the *Ocean Pioneer*. A week after he left I went out one morning and saw the *Motherhood*, the salver’s ship from Starr Race, towing up the channel and sounding. The whole blessed game was up, and all my trouble thrown away. Gummy! How wild I felt! And guying it in that stinking silly dress! Four months!”

===Chinese===
“不过，当然了，我那样把他打发走是个蠢主意。要是我有脑子，就该直接把宝藏的事告诉他，拉他入伙。我毫不怀疑他会入伙的。一个孩子，只要给几个钟头琢磨，也能看出我的潜水服和‘海洋先驱号’的失踪之间的关联。他走后一个礼拜，一天早上我出去，看见‘母性号’（*Motherhood*）——那艘从斯塔尔雷斯来的打捞船——正拖着船在水道上行进，一边测着水深。整盘棋全完了，我的一番辛苦都付诸东流。乖乖！我心里那个懊恼啊！还要套着那身又臭又蠢的衣裳装神弄鬼！整整四个月！”

===Original===
The sunburnt man’s story degenerated again. “Think of it,” he said, when he emerged to linguistic purity once more. “Forty thousand pounds’ worth of gold.”
“Did the little missionary come back?” I asked.
“Oh yes! bless him! And he pledged his reputation there was a man inside the god, and started out to see as much with tremendous ceremony. But wasn’t—he got sold again. I always did hate scenes and explanations, and long before he came I was out of it all—going home to Banya along the coast, hiding in bushes by day, and thieving food from the villages by night. Only weapon, a spear. No clothes, no money. Nothing. My face, my fortune, as the saying is. And just a squeak of eight thousand pounds of gold—fifth share. But the natives cut up rusty, thank goodness, because they thought it was him had driven their luck away.”

===Chinese===
晒黑的人的故事又一次堕入粗话。“想想吧，”他再度回归文雅的言辞时说道，“四万英镑的黄金。”
“那个小个子传教士后来回来了吗？”我问。
“哦，回来了！上帝保佑他！他以自己的名誉担保神像里面藏着个人，还煞有介事地要查证一番。可是呢——他又上当了。我一向讨厌热闹场面和解释，早在他到来之前，我就已经金蝉脱壳了——沿着海岸往班尼亚（Banya）老家走，白天躲在灌木丛里，夜里从村子里偷吃的。唯一的武器，一支长矛。没衣裳，没钱。什么都没有。俗话说得好，我这脸就是我的本钱。至于那八千英镑的黄金——我那五分之一的份子——也不过险险擦肩罢了。好在土著们翻了脸，谢天谢地，因为他们以为是他赶走了他们的好运。”

## Miss Winchelsea’s Heart / 温切尔斯小姐的心

===Original===
Miss Winchelsea was going to Rome. The matter had filled her mind for a month or more, and had overflowed so abundantly into her conversation that quite a number of people who were not going to Rome, and who were not likely to go to Rome, had made it a personal grievance against her. Some indeed had attempted quite unavailingly to convince her that Rome was not nearly such a desirable place as it was reported to be, and others had gone so far as to suggest behind her back that she was dreadfully “stuck up” about “that Rome of hers.” And little Lily Hardhurst had told her friend Mr. Binns that so far as she was concerned Miss Winchelsea might “go to her old Rome and stop there; *she* (Miss Lily Hardhurst) wouldn’t grieve.” And the way in which Miss Winchelsea put herself upon terms of personal tenderness with Horace and Benvenuto Cellini and Raphael and Shelley and Keats—if she had been Shelley’s widow she could not have professed a keener interest in his grave—was a matter of universal astonishment. Her dress was a triumph of tactful discretion, sensible, but not too “touristy”—Miss Winchelsea had a great dread of being “touristy”—and her *Baedeker* was carried in a cover of grey to hide its glaring red. She made a prim and pleasant little figure on the Charing Cross platform, in spite of her swelling pride, when at last the great day dawned, and she could start for Rome. The day was bright, the Channel passage would be pleasant, and all the omens promised well. There was the gayest sense of adventure in this unprecedented departure.

===Chinese===
温切尔斯小姐（Miss Winchelsea）要去罗马了。这件事在她的心头盘旋了一个多月，又如此充沛地漫溢到她的言谈里，以至于相当一些并不打算去罗马、也未必有机会去罗马的人，都把它当作了她对个人的一种冒犯。有些人确实徒劳地试图说服她，说罗马并不像传闻里那样值得向往；还有些人则在她背后议论，说她"那副罗马的派头"简直傲慢得要命。小莉莉·哈德赫斯特（Lily Hardhurst）也告诉她的朋友宾斯先生（Mr. Binns），就她而言，温切尔斯小姐"尽可以上她那宝贝罗马去，待在那儿别回来；她（莉莉·哈德赫斯特小姐）才不心疼呢。"而温切尔斯小姐把贺拉斯（Horace）、本韦努托·切利尼（Benvenuto Cellini）、拉斐尔（Raphael）、雪莱（Shelley）、济慈（Keats）这些人物都当作可以私交亲密的知己——她纵是雪莱的遗孀，对他那座坟的热衷也不过如此——这一层叫众人无不称奇。她的衣着是得体审慎的胜利之作，朴素大方，又不太"游客气"——温切尔斯小姐最怕自己显得"游客气"——而她那本《贝德克尔》（Baedeker）旅游指南则套了一只灰色封皮，好遮住那扎眼的红封面。等那伟大的日子终于来临、她可以启程赴罗马之时，她站在查令十字（Charing Cross）站台上，虽满心膨胀着骄傲，整个人却是一副整洁秀气、悦目可人的小小模样。那天阳光明媚，海峡的横渡想必会一路惬意，种种征兆都预示着顺利。这次史无前例的远行里，荡漾着一种最欢快的探险之感。

===Original===
She was going with two friends who had been fellow-students with her at the training college, nice honest girls both, though not so good at history and literature as Miss Winchelsea. They both looked up to her immensely, though physically they had to look down, and she anticipated some pleasant times to be spent in “stirring them up” to her own pitch of aesthetic and historical enthusiasm. They had secured seats already, and welcomed her effusively at the carriage door. In the instant criticism of the encounter she noted that Fanny had a slightly “touristy” leather strap, and that Helen had succumbed to a serge jacket with side pockets, into which her hands were thrust. But they were much too happy with themselves and the expedition for their friend to attempt any hint at the moment about these things. As soon as the first ecstasies were over—Fanny’s enthusiasm was a little noisy and crude, and consisted mainly in emphatic repetitions of “Just *fancy*! we’re going to Rome, my dear!—Rome!”—they gave their attention to their fellow-travellers. Helen was anxious to secure a compartment to themselves, and, in order to discourage intruders, got out and planted herself firmly on the step. Miss Winchelsea peeped out over her shoulder, and made sly little remarks about the accumulating people on the platform, at which Fanny laughed gleefully.

===Chinese===
与她同行的还有两位朋友，是她当年在师范学院的同窗，都是善良诚实的姑娘，只是历史和文学上的造诣不如温切尔斯小姐。两人都从心底里仰慕她——虽然就身材而言，她们得俯视她——她也盘算着，这趟旅途里要愉快地花些工夫"把她们撩拨起来"，让她俩也达到自己那种美学与历史热忱的高度。她们已经占好了座位，在车厢门口热络地迎接她。在这场相逢的一瞬间评论里，她已留意到范妮（Fanny）那条略带"游客气"的皮腰带，又留意到海伦（Helen）竟屈服于一件带侧兜的哔叽外套，把手插在那兜里。可这会儿她们对自己、对这次出行都欢喜得不得了，朋友不便立刻对这些事作任何暗示。第一阵狂喜过去之后——范妮的热忱有些吵闹粗率，主要表现为加重语气的反复叫喊："想想看！我们要去罗马了，亲爱的！——罗马！"——她们便把注意力转向了同车的旅客。海伦急于把一整个包厢据为己有，为了打消外人的闯入，她索性下车，坚定地守住车门台阶。温切尔斯小姐从她肩头探出头去窥望，对站台上越聚越多的人做着各种狡黠的小评论，引得范妮咯咯直笑。

===Original===
They were travelling with one of Mr. Thomas Gunn’s parties—fourteen days in Rome for fourteen pounds. They did not belong to the personally conducted party, of course—Miss Winchelsea had seen to that—but they travelled with it because of the convenience of that arrangement. The people were the oddest mixture, and wonderfully amusing. There was a vociferous red-faced polyglot personal conductor in a pepper-and-salt suit, very long in the arms and legs and very active. He shouted proclamations. When he wanted to speak to people he stretched out an arm and held them until his purpose was accomplished. One hand was full of papers, tickets, counterfoils of tourists. The people of the personally conducted party were, it seemed, of two sorts; people the conductor wanted and could not find, and people he did not want and who followed him in a steadily growing tail up and down the platform. These people seemed, indeed, to think that their one chance of reaching Rome lay in keeping close to him. Three little old ladies were particularly energetic in his pursuit, and at last maddened him to the pitch of clapping them into a carriage and daring them to emerge again. For the rest of the time, one, two, or three of their heads protruded from the window wailing inquiries about “a little wickerwork box” whenever he drew near. There was a very stout man with a very stout wife in shiny black; there was a little old man like an aged hostler.

===Chinese===
她们参加的是托马斯·冈恩先生（Mr. Thomas Gunn）办的旅行团——十四英镑游罗马十四天。她们当然不属于那种被全程带领的团员——这一点温切尔斯小姐早已打点妥当——但跟着这团走，是为图这种安排的便利。团里的人是五花八门的奇怪组合，奇妙得让人忍俊不禁。有一位满脸通红、嗓门洪亮、能说几国语言的私人领队，穿一身椒盐色的西服，胳膊和腿都很长，行动极其利索。他高声宣读着各种告示。每当他要跟人讲话，便伸出一臂把对方按住，直到把话说完。一只手里攥满了纸张、票券和游客们的票根。这支被全程带领的旅行团里的人，看起来分两种：一种是领队想找却找不到的人，另一种是领队不想找、却像越拉越长的尾巴一样尾随他上下站台的人。这些人似乎当真以为，要去罗马，唯一的指望就是死死贴着他。有三位瘦小的老太太追逐他得尤其卖力，终于把他逼得怒不可遏，索性把她们塞进一节车厢，扬言谁再出来试试。可自此之后，每当他走近，车厢窗里总要伸出一颗、两颗或三颗脑袋，哀哀地打听"一只小小的柳条盒子"下落。有一位极胖的先生，携着一位同样极胖、一身黑缎料子亮闪闪的太太；还有一位小老头，活像个上了年纪的马夫。

===Original===
“What *can* such people want in Rome?” asked Miss Winchelsea. “What can it mean to them?” There was a very tall curate in a very small straw hat, and a very short curate encumbered by a long camera stand. The contrast amused Fanny very much. Once they heard someone calling for “Snooks.” “I always thought that name was invented by novelists,” said Miss Winchelsea. “Fancy! Snooks. I wonder which *is* Mr. Snooks.” Finally they picked out a very stout and resolute little man in a large check suit. “If he isn’t Snooks, he ought to be,” said Miss Winchelsea.

Presently the conductor discovered Helen’s attempt at a corner in carriages. “Room for five,” he bawled with a parallel translation on his fingers. A party of four together—mother, father, and two daughters—blundered in, all greatly excited. “It’s all right, Ma—you let me,” said one of the daughters, hitting her mother’s bonnet with a handbag she struggled to put in the rack. Miss Winchelsea detested people who banged about and called their mother “Ma.” A young man travelling alone followed. He was not at all “touristy” in his costume, Miss Winchelsea observed; his Gladstone bag was of good pleasant leather with labels reminiscent of Luxembourg and Ostend, and his boots, though brown, were not vulgar. He carried an overcoat on his arm. Before these people had properly settled in their places, came an inspection of tickets and a slamming of doors, and behold! they were gliding out of Charing Cross Station on their way to Rome.

===Chinese===
"这种人到罗马去能想要些什么呢？"温切尔斯小姐问，"这地方对他们又能有什么意义呢？"那里有一位个子极高、戴着极小一顶草帽的助理牧师，还有一位个子极矮、被一根长长的照相机架子拖累得狼狈不堪的助理牧师。这种反差让范妮觉得十分有趣。有一次她们听见有人在喊"斯努克斯（Snooks）"。"我一直以为这名字是小说家编出来的呢，"温切尔斯小姐说，"想想看！斯努克斯。我倒想知道哪一位才是斯努克斯先生。"末了她们挑中了一个极壮实、神态坚定的小个子男人，穿着一身大格子的西服。"他要不是斯努克斯，那他也本该是。"温切尔斯小姐说。

不一会儿，领队发现了海伦想独占一隅包厢的图谋。"能坐五个人，"他一边大声嚷道，一边用手指比出一份对应的翻译。一行四人——母亲、父亲和两个女儿——乱哄哄地挤了进来，个个激动得很。"没事儿，妈——您让我来，"其中一个女儿一边说，一边用她正费力往行李架上塞的手提包打到了母亲的帽子。温切尔斯小姐最讨厌那种到处乱撞、管自己母亲叫"妈"的人。紧接着上来的是一位独自旅行的青年男子。据温切尔斯小姐观察，他衣着毫不"游客气"；他那格拉德斯通（Gladstone）旅行皮包是上好、悦目的皮革制成，贴着让人想起卢森堡和奥斯坦德（Ostend）的标签；他的靴子虽是棕色的，却并不俗气。他臂上搭着一件外套。这些人还没好好坐定，便来了一场查票和一通摔门，看哪！他们已经滑出了查令十字车站，朝罗马驶去。

===Original===
“Fancy!” cried Fanny, “we are going to Rome, my dear! Rome! I don’t seem to believe it, even now.”

Miss Winchelsea suppressed Fanny’s emotions with a little smile, and the lady who was called “Ma” explained to people in general why they had “cut it so close” at the station. The two daughters called her “Ma” several times, toned her down in a tactless, effective way, and drove her at last to the muttered inventory of a basket of travelling requisites. Presently she looked up. “Lor!” she said, “I didn’t bring *them*!” Both the daughters said “Oh, Ma!” But what “them” was did not appear.

===Chinese===
"想想看！"范妮叫道，"我们要去罗马了，亲爱的！罗马！就是这会儿，我都像是不大相信呢。"

温切尔斯小姐微微一笑，按下了范妮的情绪。那位被唤作"妈"的太太则向众人解释她们何以在车站"赶得这么紧"。两个女儿喊了她好几声"妈"，用一种虽不体贴却行之有效的方式让她压低了声音，最后逼得她只好低声清点起一只旅行杂物篮子里的家什。忽然她抬起头来。"哎呀！"她说，"我竟没带*它们*！"两个女儿都说："噢，妈！"可那"它们"究竟是什么，始终不得而知。

===Original===
Presently Fanny produced Hare’s *Walks in Rome*, a sort of mitigated guidebook very popular among Roman visitors; and the father of the two daughters began to examine his books of tickets minutely, apparently in a search after English words. When he had looked at the tickets for a long time right way up, he turned them upside down. Then he produced a fountain pen and dated them with considerable care. The young man having completed an unostentatious survey of his fellow-travellers produced a book and fell to reading. When Helen and Fanny were looking out of the window at Chislehurst—the place interested Fanny because the poor dear Empress of the French used to live there—Miss Winchelsea took the opportunity to observe the book the young man held. It was not a guidebook but a little thin volume of poetry—*bound*. She glanced at his face—it seemed a refined, pleasant face to her hasty glance. He wore a little gilt *pince-nez*. “Do you think she lives there now?” said Fanny, and Miss Winchelsea’s inspection came to an end.

===Chinese===
不一会儿，范妮掏出了黑尔的《罗马漫步》（Walks in Rome），一本温和节制的导游手册，在游罗马的人中颇流行；那两位姑娘的父亲则开始细细检视他那叠票券，似乎在里头搜寻英文词。他把那些票券正着端详了许久，又把它们倒过来看。然后他掏出自来水笔，相当郑重地给它们一一注上日期。那位青年则不动声色地环顾完同车旅客之后，拿出一本书，埋头读了起来。趁海伦和范妮望向窗外奇斯尔赫斯特（Chislehurst）的当儿——那地方让范妮颇感兴趣，因为可怜可爱的法国皇后从前就住在那里——温切尔斯小姐便借机打量起青年手中的书。那不是一本导游手册，而是一本薄薄的小小诗集——精装的。她又飞快地瞟了一眼他的脸——粗粗一瞥之下，那是一张文雅而悦目的脸。他戴着一副小小的镀金夹鼻眼镜（pince-nez）。"您说她现在还住那儿吗？"范妮一问，温切尔斯小姐的观察便告一段落。

===Original===
For the rest of the journey Miss Winchelsea talked little, and what she said was as agreeable and as stamped with refinement as she could make it. Her voice was always low and clear and pleasant, and she took care that on this occasion it was particularly low and clear and pleasant. As they came under the white cliffs the young man put his book of poetry away, and when at last the train stopped beside the boat, he displayed a graceful alacrity with the impedimenta of Miss Winchelsea and her friends. Miss Winchelsea “hated nonsense,” but she was pleased to see the young man perceived at once that they were ladies, and helped them without any violent geniality; and how nicely he showed that his civilities were to be no excuse for further intrusions. None of her little party had been out of England before, and they were all excited and a little nervous at the Channel passage. They stood in a little group in a good place near the middle of the boat—the young man had taken Miss Winchelsea’s carryall there and had told her it was a good place—and they watched the white shores of Albion recede and quoted Shakespeare and made quiet fun of their fellow-travellers in the English way.

They were particularly amused at the precautions the bigger-sized people had taken against the little waves—cut lemons and flasks prevailed, one lady lay full length in a deck chair with a handkerchief over her face, and a very broad resolute man in a bright brown “touristy” suit walked all the way from England to France along the deck, with his legs as widely apart as Providence permitted. These were all excellent precautions, and nobody was ill. The personally-conducted party pursued the conductor about the deck with inquiries, in a manner that suggested to Helen’s mind the rather vulgar image of hens with a piece of bacon rind, until at last he went into hiding below. And the young man with the thin volume of poetry stood at the stern watching England receding, looking rather lonely and sad to Miss Winchelsea’s eye.

===Chinese===
在接下来的一程旅途里，温切尔斯小姐话不多，但凡说出口的，都尽可能又婉转、又印着她那一层修养。她的嗓音向来低而清亮悦耳，这次她尤其留心让它格外低、格外清亮悦耳。当他们驶近白色悬崖时，青年收起了他那本诗集；等火车终于停在那艘渡轮旁时，他显示出一种优雅的勤勉，主动张罗起温切尔斯小姐和她朋友们的随身行李来。温切尔斯小姐"最讨厌胡来"，可她很乐意地看到，这青年一眼便辨出她们是体面的女士，殷勤相助又不带任何过分的熟络；他又多么得体地表明，他这点礼数并不构成进一步攀谈的借口。她这一小队人马谁都没出过英格兰，对于横渡海峡，个个都既兴奋又有些紧张。她们在船中段一处好位置上聚成一小堆——是青年把温切尔斯小姐的手提包拎到那里，并告诉她那是处好位置——望着阿尔比恩（Albion）雪白的海岸渐渐远去，引着莎士比亚的句子，照英国人的做派悄悄地拿同船的旅客们取乐。

那些块头大些的人为这点小风小浪所做的种种防备，尤其叫她们好笑——切开的柠檬和小酒壶大为流行，一位太太整个人躺在帆布躺椅上，脸上盖着一条手帕，一位宽阔结实、穿一身鲜棕色"游客气"西服的先生则两腿尽可能大地叉开——大到老天所容许的限度——一路从英格兰走到法兰西。这都是绝佳的预防措施，谁也没晕船。被全程带领的那支队伍拿着各种问题在甲板上追着领队跑，那样子让海伦想起一群母鸡围着一块咸肉皮的颇为粗俗的画面，直到最后领队躲进底舱才算罢休。而那位夹着一薄册诗集的青年则站在船尾，望着英格兰渐渐远去，在温切尔斯小姐眼里，神情颇有些孤单与惆怅。

===Original===
And then came Calais and tumultuous novelties, and the young man had not forgotten Miss Winchelsea’s holdall and the other little things. All three girls, though they had passed Government examinations in French to any extent, were stricken with a dumb shame of their accents, and the young man was very useful. And he did not intrude. He put them in a comfortable carriage and raised his hat and went away. Miss Winchelsea thanked him in her best manner—a pleasing, cultivated manner—and Fanny said he was “nice” almost before he was out of earshot. “I wonder what he can be,” said Helen. “He’s going to Italy, because I noticed green tickets in his book.” Miss Winchelsea almost told them of the poetry, and decided not to do so. And presently the carriage windows seized hold upon them and the young man was forgotten. It made them feel that they were doing an educated sort of thing to travel through a country whose commonest advertisements were in idiomatic French, and Miss Winchelsea made unpatriotic comparisons because there were weedy little signboard advertisements by the rail side instead of the broad hoardings that deface the landscape in our land. But the north of France is really uninteresting country, and after a time Fanny reverted to Hare’s *Walks*, and Helen initiated lunch. Miss Winchelsea awoke out of a happy reverie; she had been trying to realise, she said, that she was actually going to Rome, but she perceived at Helen’s suggestion that she was hungry, and they lunched out of their baskets very cheerfully. In the afternoon they were tired and silent until Helen made tea. Miss Winchelsea might have dozed, only she knew Fanny slept with her mouth open; and as their fellow-passengers were two rather nice, critical-looking ladies of uncertain age—who knew French well enough to talk it—she employed herself in keeping Fanny awake. The rhythm of the train became insistent, and the streaming landscape outside became at last quite painful to the eye. They were already dreadfully tired of travelling before their night’s stoppage came.

===Chinese===
紧接着便是加来（Calais）和一片闹哄哄的新鲜事，那青年倒没忘记温切尔斯小姐的大旅行袋和那些零零碎碎。三个姑娘虽都通过了政府所办的各种法语考试，却都为自己发音的口音羞愧得张口结舌，那青年便派上了大用场。可他并不纠缠。他把她们安顿进一节舒适的车厢，举帽致意，便走开了。温切尔斯小姐以她最优美的风度——一种悦目而富于教养的风度——向他道谢；他几乎还没走远到听不见，范妮就说他人"真好"。"不知道他是做什么的呢，"海伦说，"他是要去意大利的，因为我瞧见他票券里有绿票。"温切尔斯小姐差一点要把诗集那件事告诉她们，犹豫了一下，又决定不说。不一会儿，车窗外的景致便攫住了她们，那青年便被忘到了脑后。穿行在一个连最普通的广告都用地道法语书写的国度里，让她们觉得自己在做一件颇见教养的事；温切尔斯小姐更因铁道旁只有些瘦弱寒碜的小招牌广告、而不是我国那种大肆污损风景的宽大广告牌，而做起了一些不太爱国的比较。不过法国北部实在是个无趣的地方，过了一阵，范妮又重新捧起黑尔的《罗马漫步》，海伦则张罗起午饭来。温切尔斯小姐从一段甜蜜的遐想里惊醒；她说她方才正努力让自己相信她真的要去罗马了，可海伦一提议，她便发觉自己饿了，于是她们愉快地从篮子里取出午饭吃了起来。下午她们都乏了，沉默着，直到海伦沏了茶。温切尔斯小姐本来可以打个盹，可她知道范妮一睡就张着嘴；而同车的两位旅客是两位年纪难辨、神情挑剔、看上去还算体面的女士——她们的法语好到能用来交谈——她便忙着不让范妮睡熟。火车的节奏越来越催人，窗外掠过的景色到末了竟叫人看得眼睛发疼。在夜里停下歇宿之前，她们早已对赶路厌倦得要命。

===Original===
The stoppage for the night was brightened by the appearance of the young man, and his manners were all that could be desired and his French quite serviceable.

His coupons availed for the same hotel as theirs, and by chance, as it seemed, he sat next Miss Winchelsea at the *table d’hôte*. In spite of her enthusiasm for Rome, she had thought out some such possibility very thoroughly, and when he ventured to make a remark upon the tediousness of travelling—he let the soup and fish go by before he did this—she did not simply assent to his proposition, but responded with another. They were soon comparing their journeys, and Helen and Fanny were cruelly overlooked in the conversation. It was to be the same journey, they found; one day for the galleries at Florence—“from what I hear,” said the young man, “it is barely enough,”—and the rest at Rome. He talked of Rome very pleasantly; he was evidently quite well read, and he quoted Horace about Soracte. Miss Winchelsea had “done” that book of Horace for her matriculation, and was delighted to cap his quotation. It gave a sort of tone to things, this incident—a touch of refinement to mere chatting. Fanny expressed a few emotions, and Helen interpolated a few sensible remarks, but the bulk of the talk on the girls’ side naturally fell to Miss Winchelsea.

===Chinese===
夜里停歇时，那青年一露面，便让这处落脚点都明亮起来；他的举止无懈可击，他的法语也相当顶用。

他的那些券正好与她们同一家旅店，而仿佛出于偶然，他在公膳桌（table d’hôte）上挨着温切尔斯小姐坐下。纵使她对罗马满怀热忱，其实她早已把这类可能设想得十分周全了，所以当他试探着就旅途的乏味发了一句话——他是等汤和鱼两道菜都过去之后才开口的——她并非仅仅附和他的话，而是另起一句作答。两人很快便比起各自的行程来，海伦和范妮在这场谈话里受到了残酷的冷落。原来他们将走的是同一段旅程：在佛罗伦萨（Florence）看一天画廊——"据我所知，"那青年说，"这时间勉强够用"——余下的时间都留在罗马。他谈起罗马来十分动听；他显然读过不少书，还引了贺拉斯写索拉克特山（Soracte）的句子。温切尔斯小姐当年为了升学考试，正巧"啃"过贺拉斯那一卷，便欣喜地用一句引文回敬了他。这件事给整桩际遇添了一种格调——给闲谈加上了一层文雅。范妮表达了若干感触，海伦也插进几句得体的话，但姑娘们这边的大半谈话，自然都落到了温切尔斯小姐头上。

===Original===
Before they reached Rome this young man was tacitly of their party. They did not know his name nor what he was, but it seemed he taught, and Miss Winchelsea had a shrewd idea he was an extension lecturer. At any rate he was something of that sort, something gentlemanly and refined without being opulent and impossible. She tried once or twice to ascertain whether he came from Oxford or Cambridge, but he missed her timid opportunities. She tried to get him to make remarks about those places to see if he would say “come up” to them instead of “go down,”—she knew that was how you told a ’Varsity man. He used the word “’Varsity”—not university—in quite the proper way.

They saw as much of Mr. Ruskin’s Florence as the brief time permitted; he met them in the Pitti Gallery and went round with them, chatting brightly, and evidently very grateful for their recognition. He knew a great deal about art, and all four enjoyed the morning immensely. It was fine to go round recognising old favourites and finding new beauties, especially while so many people fumbled helplessly with *Baedeker*. Nor was he a bit of a prig, Miss Winchelsea said, and indeed she detested prigs. He had a distinct undertone of humour, and was funny, for example, without being vulgar, at the expense of the quaint work of Beato Angelico. He had a grave seriousness beneath it all, and was quick to seize the moral lessons of the pictures. Fanny went softly among these masterpieces; she admitted “she knew so little about them,” and she confessed that to her they were “all beautiful.” Fanny’s “beautiful” inclined to be a little monotonous, Miss Winchelsea thought. She had been quite glad when the last sunny Alp had vanished, because of the staccato of Fanny’s admiration. Helen said little, but Miss Winchelsea had found her a trifle wanting on the aesthetic side in the old days and was not surprised; sometimes she laughed at the young man’s hesitating, delicate jests and sometimes she didn’t, and sometimes she seemed quite lost to the art about them in the contemplation of the dresses of the other visitors.

===Chinese===
还没到罗马之前，这位青年便默然成了她们一行中的一员。她们既不知他的姓名，也不知他的职业，但看样子他是教书先生，而温切尔斯小姐心里精明地猜测他是位大学推广讲师（extension lecturer）。无论如何，他是那一类人——有种绅士派头和文雅修养，既不阔绰到高不可攀，也不寒酸到无望。她有一两回想探出他是牛津（Oxford）还是剑桥（Cambridge）出身，可他每每错失她那怯生生的试探。她想引他对那两个地方说点什么，看他会不会用"上去（come up）"而非"下去（go down）"来称呼它们——她知道，这正是辨认一个大学出身之人的办法。他把"大学（'Varsity）"——而不说"university"——这个词用得颇为地道。

他们在短促的时日所允许的范围内，把罗斯金先生（Mr. Ruskin）笔下的佛罗伦萨看了个够；那青年在皮蒂画廊（Pitti Gallery）里与她们会合，陪着她们走了一圈，谈笑风生，显然对她们的赏识十分感激。他对艺术所知甚多，四个人那一上午过得极愉快。一路认出旧日心仪的画作、又发现新的美，是一件赏心乐事，尤其是有那么多人正手忙脚乱地翻着《贝德克尔》一筹莫展。而且他一点也不是个书呆子气十足的自命不凡之徒，温切尔斯小姐说——其实她最讨厌自命不凡之徒。他颇有一层暗藏的幽默，比如拿贝亚托·安杰利科（Beato Angelico）那古拙的画作打趣，就能既好笑又不俗。这一切底下，他还有一种端肃的严肃，对画作里的道德训诫也抓得很快。范妮在这些杰作之间走得很轻；她承认"自己对它们所知甚少"，又坦言在她看来它们"都是美的"。范妮这句"美的"，温切尔斯小姐觉得，未免有点单调。说起来，她简直巴不得最后那座阳光下的阿尔卑斯山（Alp）也消失在天边，就是因为范妮那断断续续、一惊一乍的赞叹。海伦话不多，可温切尔斯小姐从前就发觉她在审美一端稍有欠缺，并不觉得奇怪；她有时会笑那青年迟疑而精巧的笑话，有时不笑，有时又似乎完全沉浸在其他游客的衣着里，对身边的艺术视而不见。

===Original===
At Rome the young man was with them intermittently. A rather “touristy” friend of his took him away at times. He complained comically to Miss Winchelsea. “I have only two short weeks in Rome,” he said, “and my friend Leonard wants to spend a whole day at Tivoli looking at a waterfall.”

“What is your friend Leonard?” asked Miss Winchelsea abruptly.

“He’s the most enthusiastic pedestrian I ever met,” the young man replied—amusingly, but a little unsatisfactorily, Miss Winchelsea thought.

===Chinese===
到了罗马，那青年只是断断续续地与她们在一起。他有个颇"游客气"的朋友，时不时把他拉走。他半是好笑地向温切尔斯小姐抱怨："我在罗马只有短短两个礼拜，"他说，"可我的朋友伦纳德（Leonard）却要花上一整天去蒂沃利（Tivoli）看一道瀑布。"

"你那位朋友伦纳德是做什么的？"温切尔斯小姐冷不防问道。

"他是我所见过最热切的徒步爱好者，"那青年答道——答得颇有趣，温切尔斯小姐心想，却略嫌不太够。

===Original===
They had some glorious times, and Fanny could not think what they would have done without him. Miss Winchelsea’s interest and Fanny’s enormous capacity for admiration were insatiable. They never flagged—through pictures and sculpture galleries, immense crowded churches, ruins and museums, Judas trees and prickly pears, wine carts and palaces, they admired their way unflinchingly. They never saw a stone pine or a eucalyptus but they named and admired it; they never glimpsed Soracte but they exclaimed. Their common ways were made wonderful by imaginative play. “Here Caesar may have walked,” they would say. “Raphael may have seen Soracte from this very point.” They happened on the tomb of Bibulus. “Old Bibulus,” said the young man. “The oldest monument of Republican Rome!” said Miss Winchelsea.

“I’m dreadfully stupid,” said Fanny, “but who *was* Bibulus?”

There was a curious little pause.

“Wasn’t he the person who built the wall?” said Helen.

The young man glanced quickly at her and laughed. “That was Balbus,” he said. Helen reddened, but neither he nor Miss Winchelsea threw any light upon Fanny’s ignorance about Bibulus.

Helen was more taciturn than the other three, but then she was always taciturn, and usually she took care of the tram tickets and things like that, or kept her eye on them if the young man took them, and told him where they were when he wanted them. Glorious times they had, these young people, in that pale brown cleanly city of memories that was once the world. Their only sorrow was the shortness of the time. They said indeed that the electric trams and the ’70 buildings, and that criminal advertisement that glares upon the Forum, outraged their aesthetic feelings unspeakably; but that was only part of the fun. And indeed Rome is such a wonderful place that it made Miss Winchelsea forget some of her most carefully prepared enthusiasms at times, and Helen, taken unawares, would suddenly admit the beauty of unexpected things. Yet Fanny and Helen would have liked a shop window or so in the English quarter if Miss Winchelsea’s uncompromising hostility to all other English visitors had not rendered that district impossible.

===Chinese===
他们度过了几段光辉灿烂的日子，范妮简直不知道没有他他们会怎么办。温切尔斯小姐的好奇心和范妮那巨大的赞叹能力都永无餍足。她们从不懈怠——穿过画廊与雕塑馆、巨大拥挤的教堂、废墟与博物馆、犹大树和刺梨仙人掌、运酒车和宫殿，他们一路赞叹，毫不畏缩。她们每见一棵石松或一棵桉树，必要叫出名字赞叹一番；每瞥见索拉克特山，必要惊呼一声。他们用想象的发挥把寻常景物点化成奇观。"凯撒（Caesar）或许就是从这儿走过的，"他们会说，"拉斐尔或许就是从这一点望见索拉克特山的。"他们偶然撞见了毕布卢斯（Bibulus）的墓。"老毕布卢斯，"那青年说。"罗马共和国时代最古老的纪念物！"温切尔斯小姐说。

"我真是笨透了，"范妮说，"可是毕布卢斯到底是谁啊？"

出现了一阵古怪而短暂的沉默。

"他不是修那道墙的人吗？"海伦说。

那青年飞快地瞟了她一眼，笑了起来。"那是巴尔布斯（Balbus），"他说。海伦脸红了，但他和温切尔斯小姐都没有为范妮对毕布卢斯的无知作任何解说。

海伦比另外三人都沉默寡言些，不过她一向就是寡言的，而且通常由她管电车票之类的零碎，或者当这些东西由那青年拿着时，她就盯着点，等他要票时好告诉他放在哪儿。这些年轻人，在那座曾经独步天下的记忆之城——那座浅棕色、洁净的城市里——度过了多么光辉的时光。他们唯一的遗憾是时间太短。他们确实说过，那些电车、七十年代盖的房子，还有那块对着古罗马广场（Forum）虎视眈眈的广告牌——简直是犯罪——无一不冒犯他们的审美感情，不可言说地冒犯；可这不过是乐趣的一部分。罗马到底是个奇妙的地方，竟使温切尔斯小姐有时把自己精心准备好的某些热忱也忘了；海伦猝不及防时，也会突然承认一些意想不到之物的美。只是，若不是温切尔斯小姐对所有其他英国游客都不妥协的敌意使那一带成了禁区，范妮和海伦原本是愿意在英国人聚居区里逛上一两个橱窗的。

===Original===
The intellectual and aesthetic fellowship of Miss Winchelsea and the scholarly young man passed insensibly towards a deeper feeling. The exuberant Fanny did her best to keep pace with their recondite admiration by playing her “beautiful” with vigour, and saying “Oh! *let’s* go,” with enormous appetite whenever a new place of interest was mentioned. But Helen developed a certain want of sympathy towards the end that disappointed Miss Winchelsea a little. She refused to see “anything” in the face of Beatrice Cenci—Shelley’s Beatrice Cenci!—in the Barberini Gallery; and one day, when they were deploring the electric trams, she said rather snappishly that “people must get about somehow, and it’s better than torturing horses up these horrid little hills.” She spoke of the Seven Hills of Rome as “horrid little hills”!

And the day they went on the Palatine—though Miss Winchelsea did not know of this—she remarked suddenly to Fanny, “Don’t hurry like that, my dear; *they* don’t want us to overtake them. And we don’t say the right things for them when we *do* get near.”

“I wasn’t trying to overtake them,” said Fanny, slackening her excessive pace; “I wasn’t indeed.” And for a minute she was short of breath.

===Chinese===
温切尔斯小姐与这位好学的青年之间那种智识与审美上的同道之谊，不知不觉地朝着一种更深的情意滑去。兴致勃勃的范妮竭力跟上他们那些深奥的品鉴，元气十足地搬出她那句"美的"，每逢一个新景点被提起，便食欲旺盛地说一声："噢！咱们去吧。"可海伦到末了渐渐显出某种缺乏共鸣的样子，叫温切尔斯小姐略有些失望。在巴尔贝里尼画廊（Barberini Gallery）里，她对着贝雅特丽齐·琴契（Beatrice Cenci）的那张脸——雪莱笔下的贝雅特丽齐·琴契！——竟不肯从中看出"任何东西"来；有一天，他们正哀叹那些电车，她竟相当没好气地说："人总得有个法子出门啊，这可比在这些讨厌的小山丘上折磨马匹强。"她竟把罗马的七座山丘唤作"讨厌的小山丘"！

而他们去帕拉蒂尼山（Palatine）那天——温切尔斯小姐对此一无所知——海伦忽然对范妮说："亲爱的，别那么赶；*他们*并不想让我们追上。再说我们就算*凑*近了，也说不出合他们心意的话。"

"我没想追上他们呀，"范妮说着，放缓了她那过急的步子；"我真没有。"她有一阵子还喘不过气来。

===Original===
But Miss Winchelsea had come upon happiness. It was only when she came to look back across an intervening tragedy that she quite realised how happy she had been pacing among the cypress-shadowed ruins, and exchanging the very highest class of information the human mind can possess, the most refined impressions it is possible to convey. Insensibly emotion crept into their intercourse, sunning itself openly and pleasantly at last when Helen’s modernity was not too near. Insensibly their interest drifted from the wonderful associations about them to their more intimate and personal feelings. In a tentative way information was supplied; she spoke allusively of her school, of her examination successes, of her gladness that the days of “Cram” were over. He made it quite clear that he also was a teacher. They spoke of the greatness of their calling, of the necessity of sympathy to face its irksome details, of a certain loneliness they sometimes felt.

That was in the Colosseum, and it was as far as they got that day, because Helen returned with Fanny—she had taken her into the upper galleries. Yet the private dreams of Miss Winchelsea, already vivid and concrete enough, became now realistic in the highest degree.
