我走回去，重新点着一支，正点着，我看见其中一面镜子右侧壁灯里的蜡烛一闪，干脆利落地灭了，紧接着它的同伴也几乎立刻随之而灭。这绝没有看错。火苗消失了，仿佛烛芯被一根手指和一根拇指突然一掐灭了似的，留下的烛芯既不泛红，也不冒烟，而是黑的。我目瞪口呆地站着，床脚那支蜡烛又灭了，那些阴影似乎又朝我逼近了一步。
"这可不行！"我说；壁炉台上的蜡烛也一支接一支地灭了。
"怎么搞的？"我喊道，嗓子里也不知怎么冒出了一种古怪的高音。话音刚落，衣柜上的那支蜡烛灭了，紧接着我在壁龛里重新点着的那支也灭了。
"稳住！"我说，"这些蜡烛可少不了。"我用一种半歇斯底里的诙谐口吻说着，一边赶忙擦火柴去点壁炉台上的烛台。我的手抖得厉害，两次都没擦着火柴盒那粗糙的擦面。等到壁炉台再度从黑暗中浮现出来，窗户远处那一头的两支蜡烛又灭了。但借着这同一根火柴，我又把那面大镜子前的两支、门口地上那几支也一并重新点着了，所以一时之间，我似乎在这场熄灭战中占了上风。可紧接着，一阵齐射般，屋角各处同时又有四点火光熄了；我哆嗦着赶忙又擦着一根火柴，站着犹豫该把它拿到哪儿去。

===Original===
As I stood undecided, an invisible hand seemed to sweep out the two candles on the table. With a cry of terror, I dashed at the alcove, then into the corner, and then into the window, relighting three, as two more vanished by the fireplace; then, perceiving a better way, I dropped the matches on the iron-bound deed-box in the corner, and caught up the bedroom candlestick. With this I avoided the delay of striking matches; but for all that the steady process of extinction went on, and the shadows I feared and fought against returned, and crept in upon me, first a step gained on this side of me and then on that. It was like a ragged storm-cloud sweeping out the stars. Now and then one returned for a minute, and was lost again. I was now almost frantic with the horror of the coming darkness, and my self-possession deserted me. I leaped panting and dishevelled from candle to candle, in a vain struggle against that remorseless advance.

===Chinese===
正当我犹豫不决，一只看不见的手似乎一把抹掉了桌上的两支蜡烛。我惊叫一声，朝壁龛扑去，又扑向角落，再扑到窗前，重新点着了三支；可壁炉旁又有两支灭了；接着我想出个更好的办法，把火柴扔在屋角那只铁箍文契箱上，抓起了那盏卧室烛台。有了它，我便免去了擦火柴的耽搁；可即便如此，那一场稳扎稳打的熄灭仍在进行，我所惧怕、所与之相搏的阴影又回来了，悄悄向我逼近——一会儿从我这一侧进逼一步，一会儿又从那一侧。这就像一片破絮般的暴风雨云，把繁星一颗颗抹掉。时不时有一颗又亮回来一分钟，旋即再次消失。此时我几乎被那节节逼近的黑暗吓得发了狂，自持之力也弃我而去。我气喘吁吁、披头散发地从一支蜡烛扑到另一支蜡烛，徒劳地与那无情的进逼相抗。

===Original===
I bruised myself on the thigh against the table, I sent a chair headlong, I stumbled and fell and whisked the cloth from the table in my fall. My candle rolled away from me, and I snatched another as I rose. Abruptly this was blown out, as I swung it off the table by the wind of my sudden movement, and immediately the two remaining candles followed. But there was light still in the room, a red light that staved off the shadows from me. The fire! Of course I could still thrust my candle between the bars and relight it!

===Chinese===
我的大腿在桌角上撞得生疼，我把一张椅子撞得飞了出去，绊了一跤，跌倒时把桌布也掀了下来。我的蜡烛从我手里滚了出去，我爬起来时一把抓起另一支。可我刚把它从桌上扬起，自己动作太猛带起的风便把它一下吹灭了，紧接着仅剩的两支也跟着灭了。可屋里还有光——一种红光，替我把阴影挡在了外头。炉火！当然啦，我还能把蜡烛伸进炉栅里重新点着它！

===Original===
I turned to where the flames were still dancing between the glowing coals, and splashing red reflections upon the furniture, made two steps towards the grate, and incontinently the flames dwindled and vanished, the glow vanished, the reflections rushed together and vanished, and as I thrust the candle between the bars darkness closed upon me like the shutting of an eye, wrapped about me in a stifling embrace, sealed my vision, and crushed the last vestiges of reason from my brain. The candle fell from my hand. I flung out my arms in a vain effort to thrust that ponderous blackness away from me, and, lifting up my voice, screamed with all my might—once, twice, thrice. Then I think I must have staggered to my feet. I know I thought suddenly of the moonlit corridor, and, with my head bowed and my arms over my face, made a run for the door.

===Chinese===
我转向炉火——火苗仍在烧得通红的煤块之间跳动，把红色的反光泼洒在四壁的家具上——朝炉栅迈了两步，可就在这一刻，火苗忽地缩小、熄灭，那通红的光焰熄了，那些反光也骤然并到一起、消失不见；我把蜡烛往炉栅之间一伸，黑暗便如同一只眼睛闭上一般合拢上来，以一种窒息的拥抱把我裹住，封死了我的视线，把我脑中最后一丝理性的残痕碾得粉碎。蜡烛从我手中跌落。我张开双臂，徒然想推开那沉重如铅的黑；我放开喉咙，用尽全身力气尖叫——一声，两声，三声。然后我想，我必定是踉跄着站了起来。我只知道自己忽然想起了那条月色下的走廊，便低下头，把双臂挡在脸前，朝门口冲了过去。

===Original===
But I had forgotten the exact position of the door, and struck myself heavily against the corner of the bed. I staggered back, turned, and was either struck or struck myself against some other bulky furniture. I have a vague memory of battering myself thus, to and fro in the darkness, of a cramped struggle, and of my own wild crying as I darted to and fro, of a heavy blow at last upon my forehead, a horrible sensation of falling that lasted an age, of my last frantic effort to keep my footing, and then I remember no more.

===Chinese===
可我记不清门的确切位置了，一头重重撞在了床角上。我踉跄着退了几步，转过身，要么是被什么撞了，要么是自己又撞上了别的一件笨重家具。我依稀记得自己就这样在黑暗中东一头西一头地乱撞，一阵憋屈的挣扎；记得自己来回乱窜时疯狂的喊叫；记得最后额头上挨了重重一下，一阵漫长得仿佛有一个世纪的下坠感；记得自己最后一次发狂似的想稳住脚步——然后，我便什么也记不得了。

---

===Original===
I opened my eyes in daylight. My head was roughly bandaged, and the man with the withered arm was watching my face. I looked about me, trying to remember what had happened, and for a space I could not recollect. I rolled my eyes into the corner, and saw the old woman, no longer abstracted, pouring out some drops of medicine from a little blue phial into a glass. "Where am I?" I asked; "I seem to remember you, and yet I cannot remember who you are."
They told me then, and I heard of the haunted Red Room as one who hears a tale. "We found you at dawn," said he, "and there was blood on your forehead and lips."

===Chinese===
我在日光之中睁开了眼睛。我的头被人马马虎虎地缠着绷带，那手臂萎缩的男人正盯着我的脸看。我四下环顾，努力回想发生过什么，一时间却什么也记不起来。我把目光转向屋角，看见那老妇人——她不再神情恍惚了——正从一只蓝色的小药瓶里，往玻璃杯里滴药水。"我在哪儿？"我问，"我好像记得你们，可又想不起你们是谁。"
于是他们告诉了我，我便像一个听故事的人一样，听他们讲起了那间闹鬼的红房间。"天亮时我们找到了您，"他说，"您的前额和嘴唇上都有血。"

===Original===
It was very slowly I recovered my memory of my experience. "You believe now," said the old man, "that the room is haunted?" He spoke no longer as one who greets an intruder, but as one who grieves for a broken friend.
"Yes," said I; "the room is haunted."
"And you have seen it. And we, who have lived here all our lives, have never set eyes upon it. Because we have never dared… Tell us, is it truly the old earl who—"

===Chinese===
我是十分缓慢地，才回忆起自己那一番经历的。"这回您相信了吧，"那老人说，"那间屋子真闹鬼？"他说这话的口气，已不再像是对着一个闯入者的招呼，倒像是在为一个垮掉的朋友而哀伤。
"是的，"我说，"那屋子闹鬼。"
"您是见着它了。我们在这里住了一辈子，却从未亲眼见过。因为我们从来不敢……您跟我们说说，当真是那位老伯爵在——"

===Original===
"No," said I; "it is not."
"I told you so," said the old lady, with the glass in her hand. "It is his poor young countess who was frightened—"
"It is not," I said. "There is neither ghost of earl nor ghost of countess in that room, there is no ghost there at all; but worse, far worse—"
"Well?" they said.

===Chinese===
"不，"我说，"不是他。"
"我就说嘛，"老太太手里拿着杯子说，"准是他那可怜的年轻的伯爵夫人，让人给吓——"
"不是的，"我说，"那间屋子里既没有伯爵的鬼，也没有伯爵夫人的鬼；那里头压根儿没有什么鬼；可却有比鬼更坏的，远远更坏的东西——"
"什么？"他们问。

===Original===
"The worst of all the things that haunt poor mortal man," said I; "and that is, in all its nakedness—Fear that will not have light nor sound, that will not bear with reason, that deafens and darkens and overwhelms. It followed me through the corridor, it fought against me in the room—"
I stopped abruptly. There was an interval of silence. My hand went up to my bandages.
Then the man with the shade sighed and spoke. "That is it," said he. "I knew that was it. A power of darkness. To put such a curse upon a woman! It lurks there always. You can feel it even in the daytime, even of a bright summer's day, in the hangings, in the curtains, keeping behind you however you face about. In the dusk it creeps along the corridor and follows you, so that you dare not turn. There is Fear in that room of hers—black Fear, and there will be—so long as this house of sin endures."

===Chinese===
"是所有作祟于可怜凡人之物中最坏的一种，"我说，"说到底，赤裸裸地讲，便是——一种不要光、不要声的恐惧，一种容不得理喻的恐惧，它使人聋，使人盲，把人整个儿淹没。它一路跟着我穿过走廊，又在那间屋子里与我相搏——"
我猛地住了口。一阵沉默。我的手抬起来，按在绷带上。
随后那戴眼罩的老人叹了口气，开了口。"就是这样，"他说，"我早知道就是这样。一种黑暗的力量。竟这样诅咒一个女人！它始终潜伏在那里。即便在大白天，即便在明媚的夏日里，你也感觉得到它——在帷幔里，在窗帘里，无论你怎样转身，它始终在你背后。暮色里，它便沿着走廊悄然游走，跟着你，叫你不敢回头。她的那间屋子里有恐惧——漆黑的恐惧，而且将永远有——只要这座罪孽之屋还存在一日。"

### I / 一

===Original===
The transitory mental aberration of Sidney Davidson, remarkable enough in itself, is still more remarkable if Wade’s explanation is to be credited. It sets one dreaming of the oddest possibilities of intercommunication in the future, of spending an intercalary five minutes on the other side of the world, or being watched in our most secret operations by unsuspected eyes. It happened that I was the immediate witness of Davidson’s seizure, and so it falls naturally to me to put the story upon paper.

When I say that I was the immediate witness of his seizure, I mean that I was the first on the scene. The thing happened at the Harlow Technical College, just beyond the Highgate Archway. He was alone in the larger laboratory when the thing happened. I was in a smaller room, where the balances are, writing up some notes. The thunderstorm had completely upset my work, of course. It was just after one of the louder peals that I thought I heard some glass smash in the other room. I stopped writing, and turned round to listen. For a moment I heard nothing; the hail was playing the devil’s tattoo on the corrugated zinc of the roof. Then came another sound, a smash—no doubt of it this time. Something heavy had been knocked off the bench. I jumped up at once and went and opened the door leading into the big laboratory.

===Chinese===
西德尼·戴维森（Sidney Davidson）那场短暂的精神错乱，本身已足够离奇；倘若韦德（Wade）的解释可信，那就更显得匪夷所思了。它叫人做起种种最离奇的遐想：想象未来人与人之间互通的种种古怪可能，想象在世界另一头偷得闰余般的五分钟，想象在我们最为隐秘的举动之间，竟有不曾为人察觉的眼睛在窥伺。碰巧我是戴维森突然发病时最近的目击者，于是把这故事形诸笔墨，自然也就落到了我的头上。

我说自己是发病时最近的目击者，意思是说我是头一个赶到现场的人。事情发生在海格特拱道（Highgate Archway）那头不远处的哈洛技术学院（Harlow Technical College）。事情发生时，他独自待在那间大实验室里。我则在另一间小些的屋子里——天平就摆在那儿——正整理着一些笔记。那场雷雨自然把我的工作搅得一塌糊涂。就在其中一声格外响亮的雷鸣过后，我仿佛听见隔壁屋里有什么玻璃器皿打碎了。我停下笔，转过身来侧耳细听。一时间我什么也没听见，只有冰雹正把瓦楞锌皮屋顶敲得咚咚作响，像魔鬼擂鼓一般。紧接着又是一声响，一声摔碎的脆响——这回是错不了了。准是什么沉重的东西从实验台上被撞了下来。我立刻跳起身，走过去推开通往大实验室的那扇门。

===Original===
I was surprised to hear a queer sort of laugh, and saw Davidson standing unsteadily in the middle of the room, with a dazzled look on his face. My first impression was that he was drunk. He did not notice me. He was clawing out at something invisible a yard in front of his face. He put out his hand, slowly, rather hesitatingly, and then clutched nothing. “What’s come to it?” he said. He held up his hands to his face, fingers spread out. “Great Scott!” he said. The thing happened three or four years ago, when everyone swore by that personage. Then he began raising his feet clumsily, as though he had expected to find them glued to the floor.

“Davidson!” cried I. “What’s the matter with you?” He turned round in my direction and looked about for me. He looked over me and at me and on either side of me, without the slightest sign of seeing me. “Waves,” he said; “and a remarkably neat schooner. I’d swear that was Bellow’s voice. *Hullo!*” He shouted suddenly at the top of his voice.

I thought he was up to some foolery. Then I saw littered about his feet the shattered remains of the best of our electrometers. “What’s up, man?” said I. “You’ve smashed the electrometer!”

===Chinese===
我吃了一惊，只听得一种古怪的笑声，又看见戴维森摇摇晃晃地站在屋子中央，一脸目眩神迷的神情。我的头一个念头是他醉了。他并没留意到我，正朝面前一码开外某个看不见的东西乱抓乱摸。他把手伸出去，慢慢地，颇为迟疑地，结果一把抓了个空。"这是怎么回事？"他说。他把双手举到眼前，十指张开。"老天爷！"他喊道。这事发生在三四年前，那时人人都爱拿这位大人物来赌咒发誓。接着他笨拙地抬起一只脚，又抬起一只脚，仿佛原以为它们是牢牢粘在地板上的。

"戴维森！"我喊道，"你这是怎么啦？"他朝我这方向转过身来，四处找我。他的目光从我头顶扫过，又落在我身上，再从我左右两边掠过，却丝毫没有看见我的样子。"海浪，"他说，"还有一条漂亮极了的双桅纵帆船。我敢起誓，那准是贝洛斯（Bellows）的声音。喂——！"他突然扯着嗓子高喊了一声。

我还当他是在搞什么恶作剧。可紧接着我便看见，我们那台最好的静电计摔得粉碎的残骸，七零八落地散在他脚边。"怎么回事，老兄？"我说，"你把静电计砸啦！"

===Original===
“Bellows again!” said he. “Friends left, if my hands are gone. Something about electrometers. Which way *are* you, Bellows?” He suddenly came staggering towards me. “The damned stuff cuts like butter,” he said. He walked straight into the bench and recoiled. “None so buttery that!” he said, and stood swaying.

I felt scared. “Davidson,” said I, “what on earth’s come over you?”

He looked round him in every direction. “I could swear that was Bellows. Why don’t you show yourself like a man, Bellows?”

===Chinese===
"又是贝洛斯！"他说，"手没了，好在朋友还在。说什么静电计。你到底在哪儿，贝洛斯？"他忽然踉踉跄跄地朝我冲过来。"这该死的东西像切黄油似的，一划就开。"他说。他径直撞上了实验台，反震得退了一步。"可不大像黄油呢！"他说，站在那里晃来晃去。

我心里害怕起来。"戴维森，"我说，"你究竟中了什么邪？"

他朝四面八方张望着。"我敢起誓那是贝洛斯。你怎么不拿出点男子气概，露个面呢，贝洛斯？"

===Original===
It occurred to me that he must be suddenly struck blind. I walked round the table and laid my hand upon his arm. I never saw a man more startled in my life. He jumped away from me, and came round into an attitude of self-defence, his face fairly distorted with terror. “Good God!” he cried. “What was that?”

“It’s I—Bellows. Confound it, Davidson!”

He jumped when I answered him and stared—how can I express it?—right through me. He began talking, not to me, but to himself. “Here in broad daylight on a clear beach. Not a place to hide in.” He looked about him wildly. “Here! I’m *off*.” He suddenly turned and ran headlong into the big electromagnet—so violently that, as we found afterwards, he bruised his shoulder and jawbone cruelly. At that he stepped back a pace, and cried out with almost a whimper, “What, in Heaven’s name, has come over me?” He stood, blanched with terror and trembling violently, with his right arm clutching his left, where that had collided with the magnet.

===Chinese===
我忽然想到：他准是突然瞎了。我绕过桌子，把手搭上他的胳膊。我这辈子没见过谁吓成那副模样。他猛地从我身边跳开，摆出一副自卫的架势，整张脸都让恐惧扭歪了。"老天爷！"他叫起来，"那是什么？"

"是我——贝洛斯。真见鬼，戴维森！"

我应声回答时，他又是一跳，直勾勾地瞪着——我该怎么说才好呢？——径直透过我望了过去。他开口说话，不是冲着我，而是自言自语。"光天化日之下，就在一片空荡荡的海滩上。连个藏身的地方都没有。"他狂乱地四下张望。"这儿！我——走！"他猛地一转身，一头撞向那座大电磁铁——撞得那样狠，后来我们发现，他的肩膀和颌骨都给撞得厉害极了。他向后退了一步，几乎是带着哭腔喊道："看在上天的份上，我究竟怎么了？"他脸色煞白，浑身剧烈地颤抖着站在那里，右臂紧紧攥着左臂——正是那条撞上磁铁的胳膊。

===Original===
By that time I was excited and fairly scared. “Davidson,” said I, “don’t be afraid.”

He was startled at my voice, but not so excessively as before. I repeated my words in as clear and as firm a tone as I could assume. “Bellows,” he said, “is that you?”

“Can’t you see it’s me?”

He laughed. “I can’t even see it’s myself. Where the devil are we?”

“Here,” said I, “in the laboratory.”

===Chinese===
到了这时，我既激动又着实害怕。"戴维森，"我说，"别怕。"

听见我的声音他吓了一跳，但不像方才那样厉害了。我尽可能用清晰而坚定的口吻把那句话又说了一遍。"贝洛斯，"他说，"是你吗？"

"难道你看不见是我吗？"

他笑了。"我连看不见的是我自己都看不见。咱们到底在哪儿？"

"这儿，"我说，"在实验室里。"

===Original===
“The laboratory!” he answered in a puzzled tone, and put his hand to his forehead. “I *was* in the laboratory—till that flash came, but I’m hanged if I’m there now. What ship is that?”

“There’s no ship,” said I. “Do be sensible, old chap.”

“No ship!” he repeated, and seemed to forget my denial forthwith. “I suppose,” said he slowly, “we’re both dead. But the rummy part is I feel just as though I still had a body. Don’t get used to it all at once, I suppose. The old shop was struck by lightning, I suppose. Jolly quick thing, Bellows—eigh?”

“Don’t talk nonsense. You’re very much alive. You are in the laboratory, blundering about. You’ve just smashed a new electrometer. I don’t envy you when Boyce arrives.”

===Chinese===
"实验室！"他满脸困惑地应道，伸手按住额头，"我刚才——的确是在实验室——可那道闪光一闪，我眼下要还敢说自己在这儿才怪。那条是什么船？"

"哪儿有什么船，"我说，"讲点道理吧，老伙计。"

"没有船！"他重复了一句，似乎立马便把我这话抛在脑后。"我估摸着，"他慢吞吞地说，"咱俩都归了西吧。可怪就怪在，我觉得自己好像还照旧有副身板。一下子没法子习惯过来，我瞧。老店叫雷给劈了，我估摸着。麻利得很哪，贝洛斯——啊？"

"别说胡话了。你好端端活着呢。你现在就在实验室里，跌跌撞撞地瞎转悠。你方才还砸坏了一只崭新的静电计。等博伊斯（Boyce）回来，我看你怎么交代。"

===Original===
He stared away from me towards the diagrams of cryohydrates. “I must be deaf,” said he. “They’ve fired a gun, for there goes the puff of smoke, and I never heard a sound.”

I put my hand on his arm again, and this time he was less alarmed. “We seem to have a sort of invisible bodies,” said he. “By Jove! there’s a boat coming round the headland. It’s very much like the old life after all—in a different climate.”

I shook his arm. “Davidson,” I cried, “wake up!”

===Chinese===
他的目光从我身上移开，直直地盯着那些冰盐合晶（cryohydrates）的图解。"我准是聋了，"他说，"他们开了一炮呢，瞧那团烟冒起来了，可我连一点声响也没听见。"

我又把手搁到他胳膊上，这一回他惊惶得轻多了。"看样子咱俩都成了某种看不见的身躯了，"他说，"老天！有一条小船正绕过海岬驶过来。到底儿还是跟从前的生活一个样——只是换了片天候。"

我摇了摇他的胳膊。"戴维森，"我喊道，"醒醒！"

### I / 一

===Original===
Until the extraordinary affair at Sidmouth, the peculiar species *Haploteuthis ferox* was known to science only generically, on the strength of a half-digested tentacle obtained near the Azores, and a decaying body pecked by birds and nibbled by fish, found early in 1896 by Mr. Jennings, near Land’s End.

In no department of zoological science, indeed, are we quite so much in the dark as with regard to the deep-sea cephalopods. A mere accident, for instance, it was that led to the Prince of Monaco’s discovery of nearly a dozen new forms in the summer of 1895, a discovery in which the before-mentioned tentacle was included. It chanced that a cachalot was killed off Terceira by some sperm whalers, and in its last struggles charged almost to the Prince’s yacht, missed it, rolled under, and died within twenty yards of his rudder. And in its agony it threw up a number of large objects, which the Prince, dimly perceiving they were strange and important, was, by a happy expedient, able to secure before they sank. He set his screws in motion, and kept them circling in the vortices thus created until a boat could be lowered. And these specimens were whole cephalopods and fragments of cephalopods, some of gigantic proportions, and almost all of them unknown to science!

===Chinese===
直到锡德茅斯（Sidmouth）发生那桩离奇事件之前，"*凶猛简乌贼*（Haploteuthis ferox）"这一奇特的物种在科学界只是笼统地为人所知，所凭的不过是亚速尔群岛（the Azores）附近得到的一段半消化的触手，以及一具被鸟啄鱼咬、腐烂不堪的尸体——这具尸体是 1896 年初，詹宁斯先生（Mr. Jennings）在兰兹角（Land’s End）附近发现的。

说实在的，在动物学的任何一个分支里，再没有比深海头足类（cephalopods）更让我们两眼一抹黑的了。比方说，1895 年夏天摩纳哥亲王（the Prince of Monaco）之所以能发现将近一打新种，纯粹出于一次偶然——前文所提的那段触手便是这次发现中的一件。事情是这样的：一条抹香鲸（cachalot）在特塞拉岛（Terceira）外海被几名捕抹香鲸者击杀，它在临终的挣扎中几乎冲到亲王的游艇跟前，擦身而过，从船底翻滚过去，死在距船舵不足二十码之处。它在剧痛之中吐出了好些庞大的东西，亲王隐隐约约看出这些东西既古怪又重要，便巧施一计，趁它们沉下去之前把它们都收了上来。他启动螺旋桨，让水流在船尾打着旋涡，把这些东西围在旋涡里团团转，直到能放下一艘小艇去打捞。这些标本有的是完整的头足类，有的是头足类的残块，有些体型庞大得惊人，而且几乎全部是科学界前所未见的！

===Original===
It would seem, indeed, that these large and agile creatures, living in the middle depths of the sea, must, to a large extent, forever remain unknown to us, since under water they are too nimble for nets, and it is only by such rare, unlooked-for accidents that specimens can be obtained. In the case of *Haploteuthis ferox*, for instance, we are still altogether ignorant of its habitat, as ignorant as we are of the breeding-ground of the herring or the seaways of the salmon. And zoologists are altogether at a loss to account for its sudden appearance on our coast. Possibly it was the stress of a hunger migration that drove it hither out of the deep. But it will be, perhaps, better to avoid necessarily inconclusive discussion, and to proceed at once with our narrative.

===Chinese===
说起来，这些体型庞大、身手矫健的生物栖息在大海的中层深处，恐怕在很大程度上将永远不为我们所知，因为在水里它们机敏异常，网具对它们无可奈何，只有靠这种罕见的、出乎意料的偶然事件，才能得到标本。就以"*凶猛简乌贼*"来说吧，我们对它的栖息之地至今一无所知，正如我们不知鲱鱼的产卵场何在，不知鲑鱼洄游的海道何在一样。动物学家们对于它何以会突然出现在我国沿海，也完全说不出个所以然来。也许是饥荒所迫，促成了一场迁徙，把它们从深海里赶到了这里。不过，与其纠缠这场注定得不出结论的讨论，倒不如立刻接着往下讲我们的故事。

===Original===
The first human being to set eyes upon a living *Haploteuthis*—the first human being to survive, that is, for there can be little doubt now that the wave of bathing fatalities and boating accidents that travelled along the coast of Cornwall and Devon in early May was due to this cause—was a retired tea-dealer of the name of Fison, who was stopping at a Sidmouth boardinghouse. It was in the afternoon, and he was walking along the cliff path between Sidmouth and Ladram Bay. The cliffs in this direction are very high, but down the red face of them in one place a kind of ladder staircase has been made. He was near this when his attention was attracted by what at first he thought to be a cluster of birds struggling over a fragment of food that caught the sunlight, and glistened pinkish-white. The tide was right out, and this object was not only far below him, but remote across a broad waste of rock reefs covered with dark seaweed and interspersed with silvery shining tidal pools. And he was, moreover, dazzled by the brightness of the further water.

In a minute, regarding this again, he perceived that his judgment was in fault, for over this struggle circled a number of birds, jackdaws and gulls for the most part, the latter gleaming blindingly when the sunlight smote their wings, and they seemed minute in comparison with it. And his curiosity was, perhaps, aroused all the more strongly because of his first insufficient explanations.

As he had nothing better to do than amuse himself, he decided to make this object, whatever it was, the goal of his afternoon walk, instead of Ladram Bay, conceiving it might perhaps be a great fish of some sort, stranded by some chance, and flapping about in its distress. And so he hurried down the long steep ladder, stopping at intervals of thirty feet or so to take breath and scan the mysterious movement.

===Chinese===
第一个目睹活着的"*凶猛简乌贼*"的人——确切地说，是第一个目睹之后还能活下来的人，因为如今几乎可以断定，五月初沿康沃尔（Cornwall）与德文（Devon）沿海一带接连发生的沐浴溺亡和划船事故，皆出于此因——是一位名叫法伊森（Fison）的退休茶叶商，当时他正在锡德茅斯一家寄宿公寓小住。那天下午，他正沿着锡德茅斯与拉德拉姆湾（Ladram Bay）之间的悬崖小径散步。这一带的悬崖极高，但在崖壁赭红的某一处，修有一道梯级式的栈道。他走到近处时，被一样东西吸引了注意力；起初他以为那是一群鸟，正为一块反光的食饵争抢撕扯，那东西闪烁着粉白色的光泽。那时正值退潮，那东西不仅远远在他脚下的崖底，而且要隔着一大片宽阔的礁石滩才望得见——礁石上覆着深色海藻，其间散布着银光闪闪的潮水洼。再者，远处海面明亮得使他睁不开眼。

过了一分钟再细看，他发觉自己判断错了，因为有数只鸟在那一团挣扎的上空盘旋，多半是寒鸦与海鸥；阳光打在海鸥的翅膀上，反光耀目欲盲，而它们与那东西相比，显得极小。也许正因为最初的解释过于草率，他的好奇心倒被勾得更加强烈了。

他反正闲着无事，不如寻点消遣，便决定把这东西——管它是什么——当作下午散步的目标，不再去拉德拉姆湾了，心里揣测它大概是一条搁浅的什么大鱼，不知怎的上了岸，正困顿地拍打着挣扎。于是他匆匆顺着那又长又陡的梯子往下走，每走三十来英尺就停下喘口气，再望一望那神秘的动静。

===Original===
At the foot of the cliff he was, of course, nearer his object than he had been; but, on the other hand, it now came up against the incandescent sky, beneath the sun, so as to seem dark and indistinct. Whatever was pinkish of it was now hidden by a skerry of weedy boulders. But he perceived that it was made up of seven rounded bodies distinct or connected, and that the birds kept up a constant croaking and screaming, but seemed afraid to approach it too closely.

Mr. Fison, torn by curiosity, began picking his way across the wave-worn rocks, and finding the wet seaweed that covered them thickly rendered them extremely slippery, he stopped, removed his shoes and socks, and rolled his trousers above his knees. His object was, of course, merely to avoid stumbling into the rocky pools about him, and perhaps he was rather glad, as all men are, of an excuse to resume, even for a moment, the sensations of his boyhood. At any rate, it is to this, no doubt, that he owes his life.

He approached his mark with all the assurance which the absolute security of this country against all forms of animal life gives its inhabitants. The round bodies moved to and fro, but it was only when he surmounted the skerry of boulders I have mentioned that he realised the horrible nature of the discovery. It came upon him with some suddenness.

===Chinese===
到了崖脚，他自然是离那东西更近了；可另一方面，这时它正衬在白炽的天空里，正对着太阳底下，看上去反倒幽暗而模糊。那一点粉白色的部分，此刻已被一丛长满海藻的巨石遮住了。但他看得出，那东西是由七个浑圆的、或分或连的身子构成的，鸟儿们一直在不停地呱呱尖叫，却似乎不敢过于靠近。

法伊森先生被好奇心搅得心痒难耐，便蹚着浪洗过的礁石朝那边摸过去；见礁石上密密地覆着湿海藻，滑得厉害，他便停下来，脱去鞋袜，把裤管卷到膝盖以上。他这样做的本意，自然只是为了不在身边的礁石水洼里栽跟头，不过，兴许他也像所有男人一样，乐得找个借口，哪怕是片刻也好，重温一下少年时代的滋味。无论如何，多半正因这一念，他才得以保住性命。

他满怀这个国家的居民所特有的那种十足安全感——这国家原本就绝无任何凶猛走兽可言——大大咧咧地朝目标走去。那几个圆滚滚的身子来回蠕动，可直到他翻过我方才提到的那一丛巨石，他才意识到自己发现的是何等恐怖的东西。这真相来得颇为突然。

===Original===
The rounded bodies fell apart as he came into sight over the ridge, and displayed the pinkish object to be the partially devoured body of a human being, but whether of a man or woman he was unable to say. And the rounded bodies were new and ghastly-looking creatures, in shape somewhat resembling an octopus, with huge and very long and flexible tentacles, coiled copiously on the ground. The skin had a glistening texture, unpleasant to see, like shiny leather. The downward bend of the tentacle-surrounded mouth, the curious excrescence at the bend, the tentacles, and the large intelligent eyes, gave the creatures a grotesque suggestion of a face. They were the size of a fair-sized swine about the body, and the tentacles seemed to him to be many feet in length. There were, he thinks, seven or eight at least of the creatures. Twenty yards beyond them, amid the surf of the now returning tide, two others were emerging from the sea.

Their bodies lay flatly on the rocks, and their eyes regarded him with evil interest; but it does not appear that Mr. Fison was afraid, or that he realised that he was in any danger. Possibly his confidence is to be ascribed to the limpness of their attitudes. But he was horrified, of course, and intensely excited and indignant, at such revolting creatures preying upon human flesh. He thought they had chanced upon a drowned body. He shouted to them, with the idea of driving them off, and finding they did not budge, cast about him, picked up a big rounded lump of rock, and flung it at one.

===Chinese===
他翻过石脊一露头，那几个圆滚滚的身子便四散开来，露出那件粉白色的东西——原来是一具被啃食过半的人尸，是男是女他已分辨不清。而那几个圆滚滚的身子，则是从没见过的、面目可憎的生物，形状略似章鱼（octopus），长着粗大、极长而柔韧的触手，在地面缠缠绕绕堆作一堆。表皮泛着一种亮光的质感，像光面皮革，看着叫人难受。被触手围住的口部朝下弯着，弯处还有一个古怪的赘生物；再配上那些触手和那一双双颇有灵气的大眼睛，使这怪物恍惚间有了一张怪诞的"脸"。它们的身躯约莫一头中等大小的猪那么大，那些触手在他看来足有好几英尺长。他估摸着，这群怪物至少有七八只。在它们往外二十码开外，正涨回的潮水打着浪花，又有两只正从海里冒上岸来。

它们的身子平平地贴在礁石上，眼睛不怀好意地盯着他；但法伊森先生似乎并不害怕，似乎也没意识到自己身处险境。他这份胆气，也许是由于它们那副懒洋洋的姿态所致。不过，见到这样令人作呕的怪物竟在啃食人肉，他自然是又惊骇、又激奋、又义愤填膺。他只当它们是偶然捞到了一具溺尸。便朝它们大喝一声，想把它们赶走，见它们纹丝不动，便四下里张望，捡起一块滚圆的大石头，朝其中一只砸去。

===Original===
And then, slowly uncoiling their tentacles, they all began moving towards him—creeping at first deliberately, and making a soft purring sound to each other.

In a moment Mr. Fison realised that he was in danger. He shouted again, threw both his boots, and started off, with a leap, forthwith. Twenty yards off he stopped and faced about, judging them slow, and behold! the tentacles of their leader were already pouring over the rocky ridge on which he had just been standing!

At that he shouted again, but this time not threatening, but a cry of dismay, and began jumping, striding, slipping, wading across the uneven expanse between him and the beach. The tall red cliffs seemed suddenly at a vast distance, and he saw, as though they were creatures in another world, two minute workmen engaged in the repair of the ladder-way, and little suspecting the race for life that was beginning below them. At one time he could hear the creatures splashing in the pools not a dozen feet behind him, and once he slipped and almost fell.

===Chinese===
于是，那些触手缓缓地舒展开来，它们全体开始朝他移动——起初是从从容容地匍匐而来，彼此之间还发出一种轻柔的、呼噜般的声响。

一刹那间，法伊森先生意识到自己处境危险了。他又大喝一声，把两只靴子都朝它们扔去，随即纵身一跃，撒腿就跑。跑出二十码他停下回头，本以为它们爬得慢，谁知——天哪！带头那一只的触手，已经汩汩地漫过他方才所站的那道石脊了！

这一下他又喊了一声，这回不是叱喝，而是一声绝望的惊呼，便开始连蹦带跳、大步流星、跌跌滑滑、蹚水而过，朝他与沙滩之间那片坎坷不平的礁石地奔去。那高高的赭红悬崖忽然显得远在天边，他望见——仿佛是另一个世界里的生灵一般——两个小小的工人在修理那条梯道，全然想不到脚下正开始一场为性命的赛跑。有一阵子，他听得见那怪物就在身后不出十二英尺的礁石水洼里哗哗地拍水追来，他还滑了一跤，险些跌倒。

===Original===
They chased him to the very foot of the cliffs, and desisted only when he had been joined by the workmen at the foot of the ladder-way up the cliff. All three of the men pelted them with stones for a time, and then hurried to the cliff top and along the path towards Sidmouth, to secure assistance and a boat, and to rescue the desecrated body from the clutches of these abominable creatures.

===Chinese===
它们一路追到悬崖脚下，直到那两个工人从梯道下来与他汇合，才罢休。三个人朝怪物掷了一阵石头，便匆匆登上崖顶，沿着小径直奔锡德茅斯，去搬救兵、叫船，好把那具被亵渎的尸体从这群可憎怪物的爪牙之下夺回来。

## The Star / 星

===Original===
It was on the first day of the new year that the announcement was made, almost simultaneously from three observatories, that the motion of the planet Neptune, the outermost of all the planets that wheel about the Sun, had become very erratic. Ogilvy had already called attention to a suspected retardation in its velocity in December. Such a piece of news was scarcely calculated to interest a world the greater portion of whose inhabitants were unaware of the existence of the planet Neptune, nor outside the astronomical profession did the subsequent discovery of a faint remote speck of light in the region of the perturbed planet cause any very great excitement. Scientific people, however, found the intelligence remarkable enough, even before it became known that the new body was rapidly growing larger and brighter, that its motion was quite different from the orderly progress of the planets, and that the deflection of Neptune and its satellite was becoming now of an unprecedented kind.

Few people without a training in science can realise the huge isolation of the solar system. The Sun with its specks of planets, its dust of planetoids, and its impalpable comets, swims in a vacant immensity that almost defeats the imagination. Beyond the orbit of Neptune there is space, vacant so far as human observation has penetrated, without warmth or light or sound, blank emptiness, for twenty million times a million miles. That is the smallest estimate of the distance to be traversed before the very nearest of the stars is attained. And, saving a few comets more unsubstantial than the thinnest flame, no matter had ever to human knowledge crossed this gulf of space until early in the twentieth century this strange wanderer appeared. A vast mass of matter it was, bulky, heavy, rushing without warning out of the black mystery of the sky into the radiance of the Sun. By the second day it was clearly visible to any decent instrument, as a speck with a barely sensible diameter, in the constellation Leo near Regulus. In a little while an opera glass could attain it.

===Chinese===
正是在新年的第一天，几乎三家天文台同时发布通告，称在所有绕日运转的行星中位于最外缘的海王星，其运行已变得极不规则。早在十二月，奥格尔维（Ogilvy）就已提请人们注意其速度似有减慢。这样一条新闻，几乎引不起世人的兴趣——世上大多数人本就不知道海王星的存在；而后来在那颗受扰行星所在区域发现了一个暗淡遥远的光点，除天文学界之外，也未引起什么轰动。然而科学界人士却觉得这消息颇值得注意——即使在当时还不知道这新天体正迅速变得更大更亮，不知道它的运行与诸行星井然有序的进程迥然不同，也不知道海王星及其卫星的偏移已变得前所未有。

未经科学训练的人，很少能体会太阳系是何等孤绝。太阳带着它那几粒尘埃般的行星、星尘般的小行星、和近乎无形的彗星，在一片空旷的浩瀚中游弋，那浩瀚几乎超乎想象。在海王星轨道之外，是一片空间，就人类目力所及一片空空，没有温暖、没有光、没有声音，是一片空白的虚无，绵延两千万个百万英里之遥。这还只是抵达最近一颗恒星所需跨越的距离的最小估计。而且，除几颗比最稀薄的火焰还要虚空的彗星之外，就人类所知，从未有任何物质跨越过这道空间的深渊，直到二十世纪初年，这位奇异的流浪者出现。那是一大团物质，庞大，沉重，毫无征兆地从天空的黑色幽冥中冲出，闯入太阳的光辉之中。到第二天，任何像样的仪器都能清楚地看见它，是狮子座轩辕十四（Regulus）附近一个直径仅可分辨的微点。不久之后，一具看戏用的小望远镜就能捕捉到它了。

===Original===
On the third day of the new year the newspaper readers of two hemispheres were made aware for the first time of the real importance of this unusual apparition in the heavens. “A Planetary Collision,” one London paper headed the news, and proclaimed Duchaine’s opinion that this strange new planet would probably collide with Neptune. The leader-writers enlarged upon the topic. So that in most of the capitals of the world, on January 3rd, there was an expectation, however vague, of some imminent phenomenon in the sky; and as the night followed the sunset round the globe, thousands of men turned their eyes skyward to see—the old familiar stars just as they had always been.

Until it was dawn in London and Pollux setting and the stars overhead grown pale. The Winter’s dawn it was, a sickly filtering accumulation of daylight, and the light of gas and candles shone yellow in the windows to show where people were astir. But the yawning policeman saw the thing, the busy crowds in the markets stopped agape, workmen going to their work betimes, milkmen, the drivers of news-carts, dissipation going home jaded and pale, homeless wanderers, sentinels on their beats, and, in the country, labourers trudging afield, poachers slinking home, all over the dusky quickening country it could be seen—and out at sea by seamen watching for the day—a great white star, come suddenly into the westward sky!

===Chinese===
新年第三天，南北两半球读报的人才头一回意识到天空中这一异常景象的真正分量。一家伦敦报纸以「行星相撞」为题刊出这条消息，并宣布了迪夏恩（Duchaine）的见解：这颗奇异的新行星很可能会与海王星相撞。各报主笔就此大加发挥。于是，一月三日，在世界大多数都城中，人们对天空中某种将至的现象怀着一种或明或暗的期待；随着黑夜随日落绕行全球，成千上万人抬头仰望——所见的仍是那一张张旧日熟悉、亘古如一的星空。

直到伦敦天将破晓，北河三（Pollux）西沉，头顶的群星渐渐黯淡。那是冬日的黎明，一种病恹恹的、滤过似的积聚起来的天光，煤气灯和蜡烛的黄光从窗户里透出来，显示着哪儿有人已经起身。但是打哈欠的警察看见了它，市场里忙碌的人群张口结舌地停下脚步，趁早上工的工人、送奶人、送报车的车夫、寻欢作乐一夜后疲惫苍白地回家的人、无家可归的流浪者、巡逻的哨兵，在乡间还有趟着露水下地的农夫、偷偷摸摸回家的偷猎者——在那片正渐渐苏醒的昏暗乡野上，处处都可以看见它——出海的水手在等候天明时也看见了——一颗巨大的白色星，突然出现在西边的天空！

===Original===
Brighter it was than any star in our skies; brighter than the evening star at its brightest. It still glowed out white and large, no mere twinkling spot of light, but a small, round, clear shining disc, an hour after the day had come. And where science has not reached, men stared and feared, telling one another of the wars and pestilences that are foreshadowed by these fiery signs in the Heavens. Sturdy Boers, dusky Hottentots, Gold Coast negroes, Frenchmen, Spaniards, Portuguese, stood in the warmth of the sunrise watching the setting of this strange new star.

And in a hundred observatories there had been suppressed excitement, rising almost to shouting pitch, as the two remote bodies had rushed together, and a hurrying to and fro, to gather photographic apparatus and spectroscope, and this appliance and that, to record this novel, astonishing sight, the destruction of a world. For it was a world, a sister planet of our Earth, far greater than our Earth indeed, that had so suddenly flashed into flaming death. Neptune it was had been struck, fairly and squarely, by the strange planet from outer space, and the heat of the concussion had incontinently turned two solid globes into one vast mass of incandescence. Round the world that day, two hours before the dawn, went the pallid great white star, fading only as it sank westward and the Sun mounted above it. Everywhere men marvelled at it, but of all those who saw it none could have marvelled more than those sailors, habitual watchers of the stars, who far away at sea had heard nothing of its advent and saw it now rise like a pygmy Moon and climb zenithward and hang overhead and sink westward with the passing of the night.

===Chinese===
它比我们天空中的任何一颗星都更亮；比金星在最亮时还要亮。天亮之后一小时，它仍又白又大地发着光，不再是一个眨眼的微光点，而是一个小小的、圆圆的、清清楚楚的发光圆盘。而在科学未及之处，人们盯着它心怀恐惧，相互诉说天空中这些火光之兆所预示的战争与瘟疫。健壮的布尔人、黝黑的霍屯督人（Hottentots）、黄金海岸的黑人、法国人、西班牙人、葡萄牙人，都站在日出暖意中，望着这颗陌生新星的西沉。

而在上百座天文台里，当那两个遥远的天体猛然撞到一起时，曾有过一种压抑着的兴奋，几近欢呼；人们来回奔忙，搬来摄影器材和分光镜，还有这样那样的仪器，来记录下这一新奇而骇人的景象——一个世界的毁灭。因为那确实是一个世界，是我们地球的姊妹星，实际上远比我们的地球大得多——就这样猝然闪入熊熊的死亡。遭撞击的是海王星——被那颗来自外层空间的怪星正正地撞中，撞击产生的热量一下子把两个坚实的球体变成了一大团白热化之物。那天，在黎明前两小时，那颗惨白巨大的白星绕行世界一周，只在它沉向西边、太阳从其上升起时才渐渐黯淡。处处人们对它惊叹不已，但所有看见它的人中，最惊叹的莫过于那些水手——他们惯于观星，远在海中，对它的到来一无所闻，此刻却看见它如一轮小小的月亮般升起，爬向天顶，悬于头顶，又随夜的流逝而沉向西方。

===Original===
And when next it rose over Europe everywhere were crowds of watchers on hilly slopes, on house-roofs, in open spaces, staring eastward for the rising of the great new star. It rose with a white glow in front of it, like the glare of a white fire, and those who had seen it come into existence the night before cried out at the sight of it. “It is larger,” they cried. “It is brighter!” And indeed the Moon, a quarter full and sinking in the west, was in its apparent size beyond comparison, but scarcely in all its breadth had it as much brightness now as the little circle of the strange new star.

“It is brighter!” cried the people clustering in the streets. But in the dim observatories the watchers held their breath and peered at one another. “*It is nearer!*” they said. “*Nearer!*”

===Chinese===
等到它下一次从欧洲升起时，处处都有成群结队的守望者，在山坡上、在屋顶上、在空旷地里，凝望东方，等候这颗巨大的新星升起。升起时它前方带着一片白光，像白热火焰的强光，那些昨夜亲眼见它出现的人，此刻一见便失声叫了出来。「它变大了，」他们喊道，「它更亮了！」的确，那上弦四分之一、正在西沉的月亮，看上去比它大得无可比拟，但月亮整个盘面的亮度，此刻竟还不及这颗陌生新星的那个小圆圈。

「它更亮了！」挤在街上的人们喊道。但在昏暗的天文台里，观天者们屏住呼吸，面面相觑。「*它更近了！*」他们说，「*更近了！*」

===Original===
And voice after voice repeated, “It is nearer,” and the clicking telegraph took that up, and it trembled along telephone wires, and in a thousand cities grimy compositors fingered the type. “It is nearer.” Men writing in offices, struck with a strange realisation, flung down their pens, men talking in a thousand places suddenly came upon a grotesque possibility in those words, “It is nearer.” It hurried along awakening streets, it was shouted down the frost-stilled ways of quiet villages, men who had read these things from the throbbing tape stood in yellow-lit doorways shouting the news to the passersby. “It is nearer,” Pretty women, flushed and glittering, heard the news told jestingly between the dances, and feigned an intelligent interest they did not feel. “Nearer! Indeed. How curious! How very, very clever people must be to find out things like that!”

Lonely tramps faring through the wintry night murmured those words to comfort themselves—looking skyward. “It has need to be nearer, for the night’s as cold as charity. Don’t seem much warmth from it if it *is* nearer, all the same.”

“What is a new star to me?” cried the weeping woman, kneeling beside her dead.

===Chinese===
一个声音接一个声音地重复：「它更近了。」嗒嗒作响的电报机接过了这句话，它在电话线里颤动；在成千座城市里，满手油墨的排字工人摸着铅字。「它更近了。」写字楼里写字的人被一种奇异的顿悟击中，摔下笔来；成千处地方正在交谈的人们，忽然在这几个字里撞见了一种荒诞的可能——「它更近了。」这句话顺着正在醒来的街道一路飞传，在霜降无声的恬静村落小路上也被高声喊出；从嗒嗒跳动的纸带上读到这消息的人，站在昏黄灯火的门口向过路人高声报信。「它更近了。」容光焕发、珠光宝气的漂亮女人，在舞曲间歇里听人以打趣的口吻讲起这条新闻，装出一副她们并未感到的、心领神会的兴致。「更近了！真的吗。多稀奇啊！那些聪明人是多么非常、非常的了不起，竟能发现这种事！」

在冬夜里赶路的孤独流浪者，仰望天空，喃喃念着这句话来宽慰自己。「它倒真该再近一些才好，这夜里冷得像施舍一样无情。就算它真的更近了，看样子也并不见得能从中得到多少暖气呢。」

「一颗新星与我何干？」那个跪在亡者身旁、泪流满面的女人喊道。

===Original===
The schoolboy, rising early for his examination work, puzzled it out for himself—with the great white star shining broad and bright through the frost-flowers of his window. “Centrifugal, centripetal,” he said, with his chin on his fist. “Stop a planet in its flight, rob it of its centrifugal force, what then? Centripetal has it, and down it falls into the Sun! And this—!

“Do *we* come in the way? I wonder—”

The light of that day went the way of its brethren, and with the later watches of the frosty darkness rose the strange star again. And it was now so bright that the waxing Moon seemed but a pale yellow ghost of itself, hanging huge in the sunset. In a South African city a great man had married, and the streets were alight to welcome his return with his bride. “Even the skies have illuminated,” said the flatterer. Under Capricorn, two negro lovers, daring the wild beasts and evil spirits for love of one another, crouched together in a cane brake where the fireflies hovered. “That is our star,” they whispered, and felt strangely comforted by the sweet brilliance of its light.

===Chinese===
那个为准备考试早早起身的小学生，自己一个人琢磨出了个究竟——那颗又大又白的星，正透过窗上的霜花，又宽又亮地照进来。「离心，向心，」他一手托着下巴说。「叫一颗行星停下飞奔，夺去它的离心力，那便如何？向心力一上手，它便径直落进太阳里去！那么这一颗——！

「我们会不会挡在路上？我倒要想想——」

那天的光也像它的兄弟们一样归去了，在霜寒之夜的更深时分，那颗怪星又升了起来。此刻它已亮到这种地步，那上弦的月亮与其相比，仿佛只是自身一团惨黄的鬼影，庞大地悬在日落之中。在一座南非的城市里，一位大人物成了婚，街道灯火通明，迎接他偕新娘归来。「连天上也点起了灯来庆贺呢，」逢迎的人说。在南回归线之下，两个相爱的黑人恋人，为着彼此的爱情不顾野兽和邪灵，相偎蹲在一片萤火虫飞舞的甘蔗丛里。「那是咱们的星呢，」他们悄声说，它那甜美的光辉令他们感到一种说不出的安慰。

===Original===
The master mathematician sat in his private room and pushed the papers from him. His calculations were already finished. In a small white phial there still remained a little of the drug that had kept him awake and active for four long nights. Each day, serene, explicit, patient as ever, he had given his lecture to his students, and then had come back at once to this momentous calculation. His face was grave, a little drawn and hectic from his drugged activity. For some time he seemed lost in thought. Then he went to the window, and the blind went up with a click. Halfway up the sky, over the clustering roofs, chimneys, and steeples of the city, hung the star.

He looked at it as one might look into the eyes of a brave enemy. “You may kill me,” he said after a silence. “But I can hold you—and all the universe for that matter—in the grip of this small brain. I would not change. Even now.”

===Chinese===
那位大师数学家坐在自己的私室里，把面前的稿纸一一推开。他的计算已经做完了。一只小小的白色药瓶里，还剩下一点那种曾让他连续四个漫长之夜保持清醒与精力充沛的药。每一天，他一如既往地从容、清晰、耐心，给学生讲完课，便立即回到这项紧要的计算上来。他面色凝重，因药物支撑的劳累而微微憔悴、泛着潮红。有一阵子，他似乎陷入了沉思。然后他走到窗前，百叶窗咔哒一声升了上去。在半空中，在城市层层叠叠的屋顶、烟囱、和尖塔之上，悬着那颗星。

他望着它，像一个人望着一名勇敢的敌人的眼睛。「你尽可以杀了我，」他静了一会儿说，「但我能把你——也把整个宇宙——攥在我这小小的脑壳里。我不愿与之交换。哪怕此刻。」

===Original===
He looked at the little phial. “There will be no need of sleep again,” he said. The next day at noon, punctual to the minute, he entered his lecture theatre, put his hat on the end of the table as his habit was, and carefully selected a large piece of chalk. It was a joke among his students that he could not lecture without that piece of chalk to fumble in his fingers, and once he had been stricken to impotence by their hiding his supply. He came and looked under his grey eyebrows at the rising tiers of young fresh faces, and spoke with his accustomed studied commonness of phrasing.

“Circumstances have arisen—circumstances beyond my control,” he said, and paused, “which will debar me from completing the course I had designed. It would seem, gentlemen, if I may put the thing clearly and briefly, that—Man has lived in vain.”

===Chinese===
他看了看那只小药瓶。「不会再需要睡了，」他说。第二天正午，他分秒不差地走进讲堂，照老习惯把帽子搁在桌子一头，仔细地挑了一支大粉笔。学生们中间有个笑话——说他没有那支粉笔在指间摩挲，就讲不成课；有一次他们藏起了他的粉笔，他果然张口结舌讲不下去了。他走上去，从灰眉毛下面望着层层升起的、一张张年轻的、焕发朝气的脸，以他惯常的那种刻意平常的措辞开口说话。

「出现了某些情况——某些我无力左右的情况，」他说着，停顿了一下，「使我无法完成我原先设计的课程。先生们，请允许我清楚而简短地把事情说一遍——人类，是白白活了一场。」

===Original===
The students glanced at one another. Had they heard aright? Mad? Raised eyebrows and grinning lips there were, but one or two faces remained intent upon his calm grey-fringed face. “It will be interesting,” he was saying, “to devote this morning to an exposition, so far as I can make it clear to you, of the calculations that have led me to this conclusion. Let us assume—”

He turned towards the blackboard, meditating a diagram in the way that was usual to him. “What was that about ‘lived in vain’?” whispered one student to another. “Listen,” said the other, nodding towards the lecturer.

And presently they began to understand.

===Chinese===
学生们面面相觑。他们听对了吗？疯了？有人挑起眉毛，有人咧嘴窃笑，但一两个人仍目不转睛地注视着他那张沉静的、镶着灰眉毛的脸。「这倒会很有趣，」他正说着，「用今天上午的时间，向诸位——在我力所能及、能说清楚的范围内——解说一下把我引向这一结论的各项计算。我们假设——」

他转身面向黑板，像往常一样在心里盘算着一幅图。「他说什么『白白活了一场』来着？」一个学生悄声问另一个。「听下去，」另一个说，朝讲台那边点了点头。

不久，他们开始明白了。

---
===Original===
That night the star rose later, for its proper eastward motion had carried it some way across Leo towards Virgo, and its brightness was so great that the sky became a luminous blue as it rose, and every star was hidden in its turn, save only Jupiter near the zenith, Capella, Aldebaran, Sirius, and the pointers of the Bear. It was very white and beautiful. In many parts of the world that night a pallid halo encircled it about. It was perceptibly larger; in the clear refractive sky of the tropics it seemed as if it were nearly a quarter the size of the Moon. The frost was still on the ground in England, but the world was as brightly lit as if it were midsummer moonlight. One could see to read quite ordinary print by that cold, clear light, and in the cities the lamps burnt yellow and wan.

And everywhere the world was awake that night, and throughout Christendom a sombre murmur hung in the keen air over the countryside like the belling of bees in the heather, and this murmurous tumult grew to a clangour in the cities. It was the tolling of the bells in a million belfry towers and steeples, summoning the people to sleep no more, to sin no more, but to gather in their churches and pray. And overhead, growing larger and brighter, as the Earth rolled on its way and the night passed, rose the dazzling star.

===Chinese===
那天夜里，那颗星升得更晚了，因为它本身的东向运行已带着它越过狮子座、朝室女座（Virgo）走了一段路；它的光亮如此之强，以至于它升起时，天空变成了一片明亮的蓝色，每颗星都依次被它的光淹没，只剩下天顶附近的木星、五车二（Capella）、毕宿五（Aldebaran）、天狼星（Sirius），以及北斗的指极星。它非常白，非常美。那天夜里，在世界许多地方，它的周围笼着一圈惨白的光晕。它明显更大了；在热带清澄、折射分明的天空下，它看上去差不多有月亮的四分之一大。英格兰地上还铺着霜，可这世界被照得亮堂堂的，仿佛是仲夏的月光。借着那清冷澄澈的光，人可以毫不费力地读普通的铅字；而城市里的灯火反倒烧得昏黄惨淡。

那一夜，全世界都醒着；在整个基督教世界里，一种阴沉的低语像石楠花丛中蜜蜂的嗡鸣一样，悬在乡野凛冽的空气里，而这种低语的喧响到了城市里便壮大为一片钟鸣。那是上百万座钟楼和尖塔里传来的钟声，在召唤人们：不要再睡，不要再犯罪，而要聚到各自的教堂里去祈祷。而头顶上，随着地球继续前行、黑夜流逝，那颗炫目的星愈升愈大、愈亮。

===Original===
And the streets and houses were alight in all the cities, the shipyards glared, and whatever roads led to high country were lit and crowded all night long. And in all the seas about the civilized lands, ships with throbbing engines, and ships with bellying sails, crowded with men and living creatures, were standing out to ocean and the north. For already the warning of the master mathematician had been telegraphed all over the world and translated into a hundred tongues. The new planet and Neptune, locked in a fiery embrace, were whirling headlong, ever faster and faster towards the Sun. Already every second this blazing mass flew a hundred miles, and every second its terrific velocity increased. As it flew now, indeed, it must pass a hundred million of miles, wide of the Earth and scarcely affect it. But near its destined path, as yet only slightly perturbed, spun the mighty planet Jupiter and his moons sweeping splendid round the Sun. Every moment now the attraction between the fiery star and the greatest of the planets grew stronger. And the result of that attraction? Inevitably Jupiter would be deflected from its orbit into an elliptical path, and the burning star, swung by his attraction wide of its sunward rush, would “describe a curved path,” and perhaps collide with, and certainly pass very close to, our Earth. “Earthquakes, volcanic outbreaks, cyclones, sea waves, floods, and a steady rise in temperature to I know not what limit”—so prophesied the master mathematician.

And overhead, to carry out his words, lonely and cold and livid blazed the star of the coming doom.

===Chinese===
所有城市的街道和房屋都灯火通明，船厂里灯光炫目，凡是通往高地的道路整夜被照得通亮，挤满了人。在文明诸国四周的所有海洋上，机器突突跳动的船、帆鼓如肚的船，满载着人和生灵，正向着大洋和北方驶去。因为大师数学家的警告早已电传世界各地，被译成上百种语言。那颗新行星与海王星，紧紧地火一般地搂作一团，正一路狂转，越来越快地朝太阳奔去。此时这团烈火般的物质每一秒钟已飞越一百英里，每一秒它那骇人的速度仍在增加。按它此刻的飞行路线，它确会在离地球一亿英里之外掠过，几乎不会对地球有所影响。但在它既定的路径附近——目前仅受到轻微扰动——旋转着那颗巨大的行星木星，木星带着它的众卫星，壮丽地绕日而行。此时此刻，那火热的星与这最大的行星之间的引力正越来越强。而那引力的结果呢？木星势必会被扯离它的轨道，转入一条椭圆路径；那燃烧的星，则被木星的引力一拽，偏离直冲太阳的方向，将「划出一条曲线」，也许会撞上我们的地球，至少也必从离地球极近处掠过。「地震、火山喷发、旋风、海啸、洪水，以及一场持续不断的升温——升到什么限度我说不准」——大师数学家如此预言。

而头顶上，为了应验他的话，那主掌将临之灾的星，孤零零、冷冰冰、惨白地燃烧着。

===Original===
To many who stared at it that night until their eyes ached it seemed that it was visibly approaching. And that night, too, the weather changed, and the frost that had gripped all Central Europe and France and England softened towards a thaw.

But you must not imagine, because I have spoken of people praying through the night and people going aboard ships and people fleeing towards mountainous country, that the whole world was already in a terror because of the star. As a matter of fact, use and wont still ruled the world, and save for the talk of idle moments and the splendour of the night, nine human beings out of ten were still busy at their common occupations. In all the cities the shops, save one here and there, opened and closed at their proper hours, the doctor and the undertaker plied their trades, the workers gathered in the factories, soldiers drilled, scholars studied, lovers sought one another, thieves lurked and fled, politicians planned their schemes. The presses of the newspapers roared through the nights, and many a priest of this church and that would not open his holy building to further what he considered a foolish panic. The newspapers insisted on the lesson of the year 1000—for then, too, people had anticipated the end. The star was no star—mere gas—a comet; and were it a star it could not possibly strike the Earth. There was no precedent for such a thing. Common sense was sturdy everywhere, scornful, jesting, a little inclined to persecute the obdurate fearful. That night, at seven-fifteen by Greenwich time, the star would be at its nearest to Jupiter. Then the world would see the turn things would take. The master mathematician’s grim warnings were treated by many as so much mere elaborate self-advertisement. Common sense at last, a little heated by argument, signified its unalterable convictions by going to bed. So, too, barbarism and savagery, already tired of the novelty, went about their nightly business, and, save for a howling dog here and there, the beast world left the star unheeded.

===Chinese===
那夜，许多盯着它看、直看到眼酸的人，都觉得它分明正在逼近。也正是在那夜，天气变了；一直笼罩整个中欧、法兰西和英格兰的严霜，开始松动，向解冻转变。

但你千万别以为，因为我说到有人彻夜祈祷、有人登船、有人往山地逃，全世界便都已因这颗星而陷入恐慌。事实上，习惯和常规仍在统治着世界；除了闲谈时说说、夜里看看奇景之外，十个人里倒有九个仍照旧忙着各自的营生。所有城市里的店铺，除零星几家外，都按时开张关门；医生和殡葬人各自操持本行，工人们聚入工厂，士兵操练，学者读书，恋人相觅，窃贼潜伏又逃窜，政客们谋划他们的勾当。报社的印刷机整夜轰鸣，而这一派那一派的许多牧师都不肯开启他们神圣的殿堂来助长一场他们所认为的愚蠢恐慌。报纸们搬出公元 1000 年的教训——那一年，人们也曾经预言过末日。这颗星根本不是星——不过是一团气——一颗彗星；就算是星，也绝不可能撞上地球。这种事史无前例。常识处处都很坚固，它嘲弄、打趣，略微有些想要迫害那些顽固的恐惧者。那夜，格林尼治时间七点十五分，那颗星将抵达离木星最近处。那时世人便会看见事情的走向。大师数学家那阴森的警告，被许多人当作无非是煞费苦心的自我宣传。常识到末了——被一番争辩稍稍激热了——以上床睡觉来表明它不可更改的信念。野蛮与蒙昧也是如此，早已厌倦了这份新奇，照旧忙它们每夜的营生；除了一只两只到处嚎叫的狗，兽类世界对这颗星不闻不问。

===Original===
And yet, when at last the watchers in the European States saw the star rise, an hour later, it is true, but no larger than it had been the night before, there were still plenty awake to laugh at the master mathematician—to take the danger as if it had passed.

But hereafter the laughter ceased. The star grew—it grew with a terrible steadiness hour after hour, a little larger each hour, a little nearer the midnight zenith, and brighter and brighter, until it had turned night into a second day. Had it come straight to the Earth instead of in a curved path, had it lost no velocity to Jupiter, it must have leapt the intervening gulf in a day; but as it was, it took five days altogether to come by our planet. The next night it had become a third the size of the Moon before it set to English eyes, and the thaw was assured. It rose over America near the size of the Moon, but blinding white to look at, and *hot*; and a breath of hot wind blew now with its rising and gathering strength, and in Virginia, and Brazil, and down the St. Lawrence valley, it shone intermittently through a driving reek of thunderclouds, flickering violet lightning, and hail unprecedented. In Manitoba was a thaw and devastating floods. And upon all the mountains of the Earth the snow and ice began to melt that night, and all the rivers coming out of high country flowed thick and turbid, and soon—in their upper reaches—with swirling trees and the bodies of beasts and men. They rose steadily, steadily in the ghostly brilliance, and came trickling over their banks at last, behind the flying population of their valleys.

===Chinese===
然而，当欧洲诸国的守望者终于看见那颗星升起——晚了一小时，不错，但并不比昨夜更大——仍有的是醒着的人在嘲笑那位大师数学家——仿佛危险已经过去。

但自此笑声止息。那颗星长大了——它以一种可怕的稳定一小时一小时地长大，每小时都大上一点，离午夜的天顶都近上一点，也越来越亮，终于把黑夜变成了第二个白昼。要是它当初径直朝地球来，而非走一条曲线路径；要是它没有因木星而失掉一些速度，那它必在一日之内便跨越中间这道深渊；但事实上，它一共花了五天才从我们这颗行星旁边经过。第二天夜里，在英国人眼中落下之前，它已经长到月亮的三分之一大；解冻已是定局。它升起于美洲上空时已近月亮大小，却白得刺目，且发着热；它升起时，一股热风随之而起，且越来越猛；在弗吉尼亚、巴西、沿圣劳伦斯（St. Lawrence）河谷一带，它透过翻涌的雷雨云瘴、闪烁的紫色闪电、和前所未有的冰雹，时隐时现地照下来。曼尼托巴（Manitoba）是解冻，是毁灭性的洪水。那夜，地球所有山岭上的冰雪都开始融化，所有出自高地的河流都浑浊汹涌地奔流，不久——在它们的上游——还裹挟着打旋的树木和人与兽的尸首。河水在那幽魅的光辉中稳稳地、稳稳地上涨，终于漫过两岸，在河谷逃奔的人群身后潺潺流来。

===Original===
And along the coast of Argentina and up the South Atlantic the tides were higher than had ever been in the memory of man, and the storms drove the waters in many cases scores of miles inland, drowning whole cities. And so great grew the heat during the night that the rising of the Sun was like the coming of a shadow. The earthquakes began and grew until all down America from the Arctic Circle to Cape Horn, hillsides were sliding, fissures were opening, and houses and walls crumbling to destruction. The whole side of Cotopaxi slipped out in one vast convulsion, and a tumult of lava poured out so high and broad and swift and liquid that in one day it reached the sea.

===Chinese===
沿着阿根廷海岸、沿南大西洋而上，潮水高过了人类记忆所及的任何一次；风暴把海水赶到许多地方内陆几十英里之远，整城整城地淹没。夜间热到如此地步，以至于太阳的升起反倒像一片阴影的降临。地震开始了，并愈来愈烈，直到整个美洲——从北极圈到合恩角（Cape Horn）——山坡都在滑塌，裂缝都在张开，房屋和墙壁都在崩塌成墟。科托帕希（Cotopaxi）的整整一面山体在一次巨大的痉挛中崩塌下来，一股熔岩奔涌而出，又高又宽又急又稀，一日之内便流到了海里。

===Original===
So the star, with the wan Moon in its wake, marched across the Pacific, trailed the thunderstorms like the hem of a robe, and the growing tidal wave that toiled behind it, frothing and eager, poured over island and island and swept them clear of men: until that wave came at last—in a blinding light and with the breath of a furnace, swift and terrible it came—a wall of water, fifty feet high, roaring hungrily, upon the long coasts of Asia, and swept inland across the plains of China. For a space the star, hotter now and larger and brighter than the Sun in its strength, showed with pitiless brilliance the wide and populous country; towns and villages with their pagodas and trees, roads, wide cultivated fields, millions of sleepless people staring in helpless terror at the incandescent sky; and then, low and growing, came the murmur of the flood. And thus it was with millions of men that night—a flight nowhither, with limbs heavy with heat and breath fierce and scant, and the flood like a wall swift and white behind. And then death.

===Chinese===
于是那颗星，拖着惨白的月亮，越过太平洋，身后曳着雷暴雨如同曳着长袍的下摆；而在它身后辛劳跟进的那道愈涨愈大的海啸，白沫翻腾、急不可耐，漫过一个又一个岛屿，把岛上的人扫荡净尽：直到那道浪终于来临——在炫目的强光中，带着一股炉火般的气息，又快又恐怖地来了——一堵五十英尺高的水墙，饥饿地咆哮着，扑上亚洲漫长的海岸，又横扫而入，越过中华大平原。有一阵子，那颗此刻比盛时太阳更热、更大、更亮的星，以无情的强光照出这片辽阔而人烟稠密的大地——城镇和村落，连同它们的宝塔和树木、道路、广阔的田地，成百万无眠的人，在无助的恐惧中瞪着那白热化的天空；接着，低低的、越来越响地传来了洪水的轰鸣。那一夜，对成百万的人便是如此——一场无处可逃的奔逃，四肢因酷热而沉重，呼吸凶猛而短促，身后是一道又快又白如墙的洪水。然后是死亡。

===Original===
China was lit glowing white, but over Japan and Java and all the islands of Eastern Asia the great star was a ball of dull red fire because of the steam and smoke and ashes the volcanoes were spouting forth to salute its coming. Above was the lava, hot gases and ash, and below the seething floods, and the whole Earth swayed and rumbled with the earthquake shocks. Soon the immemorial snows of Tibet and the Himalaya were melting and pouring down by ten million deepening converging channels upon the plains of Burma and Hindostan. The tangled summits of the Indian jungles were aflame in a thousand places, and below the hurrying waters around the stems were dark objects that still struggled feebly and reflected the bloodred tongues of fire. And in a rudderless confusion a multitude of men and women fled down the broad river-ways to that one last hope of men—the open sea.

Larger grew the star, and larger, hotter, and brighter with a terrible swiftness now. The tropical ocean had lost its phosphorescence, and the whirling steam rose in ghostly wreaths from the black waves that plunged incessantly, speckled with storm-tossed ships.

===Chinese===
中华大地被照得通白发光，但在日本、爪哇（Java）和东亚所有岛屿上空，那颗巨星却因火山为迎接它的到来而喷出的蒸汽、浓烟和灰烬，变成了一团暗红的火球。头顶是熔岩、灼热的气体和灰烬，脚下是翻腾的洪水，整个地球随着地震的冲击摇晃轰鸣。不久，西藏和喜马拉雅（Himalaya）亘古不化的积雪开始融化，沿着千万条日益加深、相互汇合的河道，倾泻到缅甸（Burma）和印度斯坦（Hindostan）的平原上。印度丛林那纠缠错结的林冠在成千处地方烧了起来，而在下方、围着树干奔涌的水中，是一些黑色的东西，仍在微弱地挣扎，映出火舌那血红的颜色。在一片失舵般的混乱中，无数男女顺着宽阔的水道逃向人类那唯一最后的希望——大海。

那颗星越来越大，越来越大，越来越热、越来越亮，速度之快令人心惊。热带的海洋已失去了它的磷光，旋转的蒸汽像幽魂的花环，从那不停地翻扑的黑浪中袅袅升起，浪间点点的是被风暴抛掷的船只。

===Original===
And then came a wonder. It seemed to those who in Europe watched for the rising of the star that the world must have ceased its rotation. In a thousand open spaces of down and upland the people who had fled thither from the floods and the falling houses and sliding slopes of hill watched for that rising in vain. Hour followed hour through a terrible suspense, and the star rose not. Once again men set their eyes upon the old constellations they had counted lost to them forever. In England it was hot and clear overhead, though the ground quivered perpetually, but in the tropics, Sirius and Capella and Aldebaran showed through a veil of steam. And when at last the great star rose near ten hours late, the Sun rose close upon it, and in the centre of its white heart was a disc of black.

Over Asia it was the star had begun to fall behind the movement of the sky, and then suddenly, as it hung over India, its light had been veiled. All the plain of India from the mouth of the Indus to the mouths of the Ganges was a shallow waste of shining water that night, out of which rose temples and palaces, mounds and hills, black with people. Every minaret was a clustering mass of people, who fell one by one into the turbid waters, as heat and terror overcame them. The whole land seemed a-wailing, and suddenly there swept a shadow across that furnace of despair, and a breath of cold wind, and a gathering of clouds, out of the cooling air. Men looking up, near blinded, at the star, saw that a black disc was creeping across the light. It was the Moon, coming between the star and the Earth. And even as men cried to God at this respite, out of the East with a strange inexplicable swiftness sprang the Sun. And then star, Sun, and Moon rushed together across the heavens.

===Chinese===
接着，出现了一桩奇事。在欧洲守望这颗星升起的人们看来，世界必定是停止了自转。在上千处高地和丘陵的空旷地带，从洪水、倒塌的房屋和滑塌的山坡逃来的人们，白白等候着它的升起。一小时接一小时，在一种可怖的悬念中过去，那颗星没有升起。人们又一次把目光投向那些他们原以为永不再见的古老星座。英格兰上空炎热而清朗，尽管地面不停颤动；但在热带，天狼星、五车二和毕宿五是透过一层蒸汽的面纱显现出来的。而当那颗巨星终于升起时，已迟了将近十个小时；太阳紧跟在它后面升起，而在它那颗白色的心的正中，是一轮黑色的圆盘。

在亚洲上空，那颗星便已开始落后于天空的运转，随后，当它悬在印度上空时，它的光忽然被遮蔽了。那一夜，整个印度平原——从印度河（Indus）的河口到恒河（Ganges）诸河口——成了一片浅浅的、闪闪发光的水泽荒原，从水中升起的有庙宇和宫殿，有土丘和山冈，上面黑压压挤满了人。每一座清真寺的尖塔上都密密麻麻挤满了人，他们一个接一个地跌进浑浊的水中，因为酷热和恐惧终于压倒了他们。整片大地仿佛都在哀号；忽然，一片阴影扫过那座绝望的熔炉，一股冷风吹来，空中聚起了云——那是空气冷却所致。人们近乎目眩地抬头望那颗星，看见一轮黑色的圆盘正缓缓爬过它的光芒。那是月亮，来到了星与地球之间。而就在人们趁这喘息之机向上帝呼号之际，太阳从东方以一种奇异而不可解的速度跃起。接着，星、太阳和月亮一同急速划过天穹。

===Original===
So it was that presently to the European watchers star and Sun rose close upon each other, drove headlong for a space and then slower, and at last came to rest, star and Sun merged into one glare of flame at the zenith of the sky. The Moon no longer eclipsed the star but was lost to sight in the brilliance of the sky. And though those who were still alive regarded it for the most part with that dull stupidity that hunger, fatigue, heat and despair engender, there were still men who could perceive the meaning of these signs. Star and Earth had been at their nearest, had swung about one another, and the star had passed. Already it was receding, swifter and swifter, in the last stage of its headlong journey downward into the Sun.

And then the clouds gathered, blotting out the vision of the sky, the thunder and lightning wove a garment round the world; all over the Earth was such a downpour of rain as men had never before seen, and where the volcanoes flared red against the cloud canopy there descended torrents of mud. Everywhere the waters were pouring off the land, leaving mud-silted ruins, and the Earth littered like a storm-worn beach with all that had floated, and the dead bodies of the men and brutes, its children. For days the water streamed off the land, sweeping away soil and trees and houses in the way, and piling huge dykes and scooping out titanic gullies over the countryside. Those were the days of darkness that followed the star and the heat. All through them, and for many weeks and months, the earthquakes continued.

===Chinese===
于是，不久之后，在欧洲的守望者看来，星与太阳紧挨着一同升起，疾驰了一阵，又慢了下来，最后终于停住——星与太阳在天顶融为一片烈焰的强光。月亮不再遮蔽那颗星，而是在天空的强光中消失不见。虽然那些尚存一命的人，多半只以一种饥饿、疲惫、酷热和绝望所生的麻木的痴钝望着这一切，但仍然有人能看出这些征象的含义。星与地球已到了彼此最近之处，已绕着彼此转了一圈，那颗星过去了。它已在退去，越来越快，正处于它一路猛坠入太阳的旅途的最后阶段。

然后乌云四合，遮蔽了天空的景象，雷电为世界织成了一件衣裳；整个地球上下起了人类前所未见的倾盆大雨，在火山冲着云盖燃起红光之处，则倾泻下泥浆的洪流。处处水流正从陆地上退去，留下一片被泥沙淤塞的废墟；大地像一片被风暴蹂躏过的海滩，狼藉着所有曾漂浮过的东西，以及它的儿女——人和兽——的尸体。接连数日，水从陆地上奔流而下，一路卷走泥土、树木和房屋，在乡野之间堆起巨大的堤埂，冲出庞然的沟壑。那便是那颗星和那场酷热之后随之而来的黑暗时日。整个这段时间里——以及此后许多个星期、许多个月里——地震仍在继续。

===Original===
But the star had passed, and men, hunger-driven and gathering courage only slowly, might creep back to their ruined cities, buried granaries, and sodden fields. Such few ships as had escaped the storms of that time came stunned and shattered and sounding their way cautiously through the new marks and shoals of once familiar ports. And as the storms subsided men perceived that everywhere the days were hotter than of yore, and the Sun larger, and the Moon, shrunk to a third of its former size, took now fourscore days between its new and new.

But of the new brotherhood that grew presently among men, of the saving of laws and books and machines, of the strange change that had come over Iceland and Greenland and the shores of Baffin’s Bay, so that the sailors coming there presently found them green and gracious, and could scarce believe their eyes, this story does not tell. Nor of the movement of mankind, now that the Earth was hotter, northward and southward towards the poles of the Earth. It concerns itself only with the coming and the passing of the star.

===Chinese===
但那颗星毕竟过去了，人们为饥饿所驱、又只是慢慢地鼓起勇气，开始悄然爬回他们那成了废墟的城市、被掩埋的粮仓、和浸透水的田地。少数逃过当时风暴的船只，失魂落魄、千疮百孔地，谨慎地一路测着深浅，穿过那些曾经熟悉、如今却布满了新标记和新浅滩的港口。随着风暴平息，人们发觉到处都比从前更热了，太阳更大了，而月亮——缩小到原来的三分之一——如今从一次新月到下一次新月，竟要八十天。

至于此后人间新生的兄弟情谊，至于法律、书籍和机器的抢救留存，至于冰岛（Iceland）、格陵兰（Greenland）和巴芬湾（Baffin's Bay）沿岸所发生的奇异变化——水手们后来到了那儿，发现其地碧绿宜人，几乎不敢相信自己的眼睛——这些，本篇故事都不再叙述。也不叙述人类——如今地球更热了——向北极和南极的大迁徙。它所关心的，只是那颗星的来临与离去。

===Original===
The Martian astronomers—for there are astronomers on Mars, although they are very different beings from men—were naturally profoundly interested by these things. They saw them from their own standpoint of course. “Considering the mass and temperature of the missile that was flung through our solar system into the Sun,” one wrote, “it is astonishing what a little damage the Earth, which it missed so narrowly, has sustained. All the familiar continental markings and the masses of the seas remain intact, and indeed the only difference seems to be a shrinkage of the white discolouration (supposed to be frozen water) round either pole.” Which only shows how small the vastest of human catastrophes may seem at a distance of a few million miles.

===Chinese===
火星上的天文学家——因为火星上是有天文学家的，虽然他们与人类大不相同——自然对这些事情深感兴趣。他们当然是从他们自己的立场来看的。「考虑到那颗被甩过我们太阳系、撞入太阳的飞弹的质量和温度，」他们中的一位写道，「与之擦肩而过、失之毫厘的地球，所受的损害竟如此之小，实在令人惊讶。所有熟悉的大陆轮廓和海洋区域都完好无损，事实上，唯一的区别似乎只是两极周围那片白色斑迹（据猜测是冻结的水）的缩小。」这只不过说明：最浩大的人类灾难，在几百万英里之外看来，也可能是何等微不足道。

## The Stolen Bacillus / 偷来的杆菌

===Original===
“This again,” said the Bacteriologist, slipping a glass slide under the microscope, “is well﻿—a preparation of the Bacillus of cholera﻿—the cholera germ.”

The pale-faced man peered down the microscope. He was evidently not accustomed to that kind of thing, and held a limp white hand over his disengaged eye. “I see very little,” he said.

“Touch this screw,” said the Bacteriologist; “perhaps the microscope is out of focus for you. Eyes vary so much. Just the fraction of a turn this way or that.”

“Ah! now I see,” said the visitor. “Not so very much to see after all. Little streaks and shreds of pink. And yet those little particles, those mere atomies, might multiply and devastate a city! Wonderful!”

===Chinese===
“这一片呢，”细菌学家（Bacteriologist）一边说，一边把一块玻璃载玻片推到显微镜下，“是——嗯——一份霍乱杆菌的培养标本——也就是霍乱病菌。”

那个面色苍白的男人凑到显微镜前端详起来。他显然不习惯这玩意儿，一只没派上用处的眼睛被一只绵软发白的手遮着。“我看不大清。”他说。

“拧一拧这颗螺丝，”细菌学家说，“也许这显微镜对你来说没对好焦距。人和人的眼睛差别大着呢。往这边或那边稍微转那么一丁点就行。”

“啊！这下看见了。”客人说，“原来也没多少可看的。几丝几缕粉红色的痕迹罢了。可就这么些小颗粒，这么些微乎其微的小东西，却能繁衍开来，把一座城市化为废墟！不可思议！”

===Original===
He stood up, and releasing the glass slip from the microscope, held it in his hand towards the window. “Scarcely visible,” he said, scrutinising the preparation. He hesitated. “Are these﻿—alive? Are they dangerous now?”

“Those have been stained and killed,” said the Bacteriologist. “I wish, for my own part, we could kill and stain every one of them in the universe.”

“I suppose,” the pale man said, with a slight smile, “that you scarcely care to have such things about you in the living﻿—in the active state?”

“On the contrary, we are obliged to,” said the Bacteriologist. “Here, for instance﻿—” He walked across the room and took up one of several sealed tubes. “Here is the living thing. This is a cultivation of the actual living disease bacteria.” He hesitated. “Bottled cholera, so to speak.”

===Chinese===
他站起身，把那块玻璃片从显微镜下抽出来，举在手里对着窗户照看。“几乎看不见。”他打量着那份标本说。他迟疑了一下。“这些——是活的吗？它们现在有危险吗？”

“那些已经染色杀死了。”细菌学家说，“要是由着我，我倒恨不得把全天下每一个这样的东西都杀死、染上色。”

“我猜，”那苍白的人微微一笑，“你大概是不大愿意身边摆着这种活物——处于活跃状态的活物吧？”

“恰恰相反，我们不得不摆着。”细菌学家说，“比方说这一管——”他穿过房间，拿起几根密封试管中的一根。“这里头是活物。这是真正活着的致病细菌的培养物。”他顿了顿。“可以算是装进瓶里的霍乱。”

===Original===
A slight gleam of satisfaction appeared momentarily in the face of the pale man. “It’s a deadly thing to have in your possession,” he said, devouring the little tube with his eyes. The Bacteriologist watched the morbid pleasure in his visitor’s expression. This man, who had visited him that afternoon with a note of introduction from an old friend, interested him from the very contrast of their dispositions. The lank black hair and deep grey eyes, the haggard expression and nervous manner, the fitful yet keen interest of his visitor were a novel change from the phlegmatic deliberations of the ordinary scientific worker with whom the Bacteriologist chiefly associated. It was perhaps natural, with a hearer evidently so impressionable to the lethal nature of; his topic, to take the most effective aspect of the matter.

He held the tube in his hand thoughtfully. “Yes, here is the pestilence imprisoned. Only break such a little tube as this into a supply of drinking-water, say to these minute particles of life that one must needs stain and examine with the highest powers of the microscope even to see, and that one can neither smell nor taste﻿—say to them, ‘Go forth, increase and multiply, and replenish the cisterns,’ and death﻿—mysterious, untraceable death, death swift and terrible, death full of pain and indignity﻿—would be released upon this city, and go hither and thither seeking his victims. Here he would take the husband from the wife, here the child from its mother, here the statesman from his duty, and here the toiler from his trouble. He would follow the water-mains, creeping along streets, picking out and punishing a house here and a house there where they did not boil their drinking-water, creeping into the wells of the mineral water makers, getting washed into salad, and lying dormant in ices. He would wait ready to be drunk in the horse-troughs, and by unwary children in the public fountains. He would soak into the soil, to reappear in springs and wells at a thousand unexpected places. Once start him at the water supply, and before we could ring him in, and catch him again, he would have decimated the metropolis.”

He stopped abruptly. He had been told rhetoric was his weakness.

“But he is quite safe here, you know﻿—quite safe.”

===Chinese===
那苍白的人脸上一时闪过一丝满足的光彩。“你手里攥着这么个东西，真要命。”他说着，眼睛像要把那根小试管吞下去似的。细菌学家端详着客人脸上那股病态的喜悦。此人那天下午揣着一封老朋友的引荐信前来拜访他，恰恰因为两人性情截然相反，反倒勾起了他的兴趣。客人那平直服帖的黑发、深灰色的眼睛、憔悴的神情和神经质的举止，他那忽冷忽热却又异常专注的兴趣，与细菌学家日常打交道的那种不动声色、慢条斯理的普通科研工作者相比，是一种别样的新鲜。面对这样一位显然对他所讲这致命话题极易动容的听众，自然要从事情最能摄人心魄的那一面讲起。

他若有所思地把那根试管捏在手里。“不错，瘟疫就给关在这里头。只要把这么一根小试管敲碎，投进一处饮用水源里，对这些生命的微粒——这些非得染色、非得用最高倍显微镜才看得见的微粒，这些既闻不出也尝不出的微粒——对这些小东西说一声：‘去吧，繁衍增多，蓄满那些水窖吧’，于是死亡——神秘的、无从追查的死亡，迅猛而可怖的死亡，充满痛苦与屈辱的死亡——便会从这城里释放出来，四处游荡，寻觅它的牺牲品。在这里它要把丈夫从妻子身边夺走，在那里把孩童从母亲怀里掳去，在这里把政治家从他的职责上拽开，在那里把劳作者从他的辛苦中解脱出来。它会顺着自来水主管道走，沿着街道悄悄爬行，这里挑一户、那里挑一户地选中并惩罚那些不把饮用水烧开的人家，溜进矿泉水制造商的水井里，被冲洗进沙拉，潜伏在冰淇淋中。它会在马槽里伺机被人饮下，在公共喷泉旁等着不留神的孩童。它会渗进土壤，在一千个意想不到的地方从泉眼和水井里重新冒出来。一旦在水源放它出来，等不到我们把它围住、重新逮住它，它早就把这座大都会杀掉十分之一了。”

他猛地收住了话头。有人告诉过他，辞藻铺陈是他的毛病。

“可它在这儿是万无一失的，您放心——万无一失。”

===Original===
The pale-faced man nodded. His eyes shone. He cleared his throat. “These Anarchist﻿—rascals,” said he, “are fools, blind fools﻿—to use bombs when this kind of thing is attainable. I think﻿—”

A gentle rap, a mere light touch of the fingernails, was heard at the door. The Bacteriologist opened it. “Just a minute, dear,” whispered his wife.

When he reentered the laboratory his visitor was looking at his watch. “I had no idea I had wasted an hour of your time,” he said. “Twelve minutes to four. I ought to have left here by half-past three. But your things were really too interesting. No, positively I cannot stop a moment longer. I have an engagement at four.”

===Chinese===
那面色苍白的人点了点头。他眼睛发亮。他清了清嗓子。“那些无政府主义——恶棍，”他说，“都是蠢货，瞎了眼的蠢货——能弄到这种东西，还用得着炸弹。我看——”

门上响起轻轻的叩门声，不过是指甲轻轻一碰。细菌学家开了门。“就一分钟，亲爱的。”他妻子悄声说。

他再回到实验室时，客人正看着表。“我竟不知道占了您一个钟头。”他说，“差十二分四点。我本该三点半就走的。可您这些东西实在太有意思了。不，我说什么也不能再待了。我四点还有个约会。”

===Original===
He passed out of the room reiterating his thanks, and the Bacteriologist accompanied him to the door, and then returned thoughtfully along the passage to his laboratory. He was musing on the ethnology of his visitor. Certainly the man was not a Teutonic type nor a common Latin one. “A morbid product, anyhow, I am afraid,” said the Bacteriologist to himself. “How he gloated over those cultivations of disease germs!” A disturbing thought struck him. He turned to the bench by the vapour bath, and then very quickly to his writing-table. Then he felt hastily in his pockets and then rushed to the door. “I may have put it down on the hall table,” he said.

“Minnie!” he shouted hoarsely in the hall.

“Yes, dear,” came a remote voice.

“Had I anything in my hand when I spoke to you, dear, just now?”

Pause.

“Nothing, dear, because I remember﻿—”

“Blue ruin!” cried the Bacteriologist, and incontinently ran to the front door and down the steps of his house to the street.

===Chinese===
他一边连声道谢一边出了门，细菌学家送他到门口，又若有所思地沿着过道走回实验室。他心里琢磨着客人的种族类型。此人当然不是日耳曼型，也不是常见的拉丁型。“反正是个病态的产物，怕是。”细菌学家自言自语，“他对着那些病菌培养物那副幸灾乐祸的样子！”一个让他不安的念头猛地袭来。他转身走向蒸汽浴旁的台子，接着又飞快地转向写字台。然后他慌忙地在口袋里摸索，随即冲到门前。“我也许把它搁在门厅桌上了。”他说。

“明妮（Minnie）！”他在门厅里嘶声喊道。

“什么事，亲爱的？”一个远远的声音应道。

“我刚才跟你说话的时候，亲爱的，手里拿着东西没有？”

停顿。

“什么也没有，亲爱的，因为我记得——”

“糟了！”细菌学家大叫一声，急不可待地冲向前门，几步下了台阶，奔到街上。

===Original===
Minnie, hearing the door slam violently, ran in alarm to the window. Down the street a slender man was getting into a cab. The Bacteriologist, hatless, and in his carpet slippers, was running and gesticulating wildly towards this group. One slipper came off, but he did not wait for it. “He has gone *mad*!” said Minnie; “it’s that horrid science of his”; and, opening the window, would have called after him. The slender man, suddenly glancing round, seemed struck with the same idea of mental disorder. He pointed hastily to the Bacteriologist, said something to the cabman, the apron of the cab slammed, the whip swished, the horse’s feet clattered, and in a moment cab and Bacteriologist hotly in pursuit, had receded up the vista of the roadway and disappeared round the corner.

Minnie remained straining out of the window for a minute. Then she drew her head back into the room again. She was dumbfounded. “Of course he is eccentric,” she meditated. “But running about London﻿—in the height of the season, too﻿—in his socks!” A happy thought struck her. She hastily put her bonnet on, seized his shoes, went into the hall, took down his hat and light overcoat from the pegs, emerged upon the doorstep, and hailed a cab that opportunely crawled by. “Drive me up the road and round Havelock Crescent, and see if we can find a gentleman running about in a velveteen coat and no hat.”

“Velveteen coat, ma’am, and no ’at. Very good, ma’am.” And the cabman whipped up at once in the most matter-of-fact way, as if he drove to this address every day in his life.

===Chinese===
明妮听见门砰的一声撞上，慌忙跑到窗前。街道那头，一个瘦长身形的人正在钻进一辆马车。细菌学家光着头、脚踩着绒拖鞋，正疯狂地挥舞着手臂朝那一伙人追去。一只拖鞋甩掉了，他也顾不上等。“他这是疯了！”明妮说，“都是他那一套要命的科学闹的”；她推开窗，正要冲他喊。那瘦长身形的人猛地一回头，似乎也想到了对方精神失常这一层。他匆匆指了指细菌学家，对车夫说了句什么，马车的挡帘砰地落下，鞭子一甩，马蹄哒哒作响，转眼间马车和紧追不舍的细菌学家便顺着那条长街退远，消失在拐角处。

明妮探身窗外张望了一阵。然后她把头缩回房里。她一时说不出话来。“他这人是古怪，”她暗想，“可顶着社交旺季最热闹的时候，在伦敦大街上——只穿着袜子跑！”她忽然想到一个主意。她匆匆戴上女帽，抓起他的皮鞋，走进门厅，从挂钩上取下他的帽子和薄外套，出到门前的台阶上，招呼一辆正好慢悠悠驶过的马车。“拉着我顺着这条路、绕哈夫洛克新月街（Havelock Crescent）转一圈，看看能不能找到一位穿着平绒外套、没戴帽子的先生。”

“平绒外套，没戴帽子，太太。好嘞，太太。”车夫当即扬起鞭子，那副不慌不忙、见怪不怪的派头，仿佛这辈子天天都赶车去这个地点似的。

===Original===
Some few minutes later the little group of cabmen and loafers that collects round the cabman’s shelter at Haverstock Hill were startled by the passing of a cab with a ginger-coloured screw of a horse, driven furiously.

They were silent as it went by, and then as it receded﻿—“That’s ’Arry ’Icks. Wot’s *he* got?” said the stout gentleman known as Old Tootles.

“He’s a-using his whip, he is, *to* rights,” said the ostler boy.

“Hullo!” said poor old Tommy Byles; “here’s another bloomin’ loonatic. Blowed if there ain’t.”

“It’s old George,” said Old Tootles, “and he’s drivin’ a loonatic, *as* you say. Ain’t he a-clawin’ out of the keb? Wonder if he’s after ’Arry ’Icks?”

The group round the cabman’s shelter became animated. Chorus: “Go it, George!” “It’s a race.” “You’ll ketch ’em!” “Whip up!”

“She’s a goer, she is!” said the ostler boy.

“Strike me giddy!” cried Old Tootles. “Here! *I’m* a-goin’ to begin in a minute. Here’s another comin’. If all the cabs in Hampstead ain’t gone mad this morning!”

“It’s a fieldmale this time,” said the ostler boy.

“She’s a-followin’ *him*,” said Old Tootles. “Usually the other way about.”

“What’s she got in her ’and?”

“Looks like a ’igh ’at.”

“What a bloomin’ lark it is! Three to one on old George,” said the ostler boy. “Nexst!”

===Chinese===
几分钟之后，哈弗斯托克山（Haverstock Hill）那座车夫避雨棚周围聚着的一小群车夫和闲人，被一辆狂奔而来的马车吓了一跳——拉车的是一匹姜黄色的瘦马。

马车经过时他们鸦雀无声，待它驶远——“那是哈里·希克斯（’Arry ’Icks）。他拉着什么玩意儿？”那个被大伙儿叫作老图特尔斯（Old Tootles）的胖先生说。

“他可是真甩开鞭子了，没说的。”那个马夫小厮说。

“哟！”可怜的老汤米·拜尔斯（Tommy Byles）说，“这又来一个该死的疯子。活见鬼，真有一个。”

“是老乔治（George），”老图特尔斯说，“他这是拉着一个疯子，就像你说的。他不是正从车篷里探出身子吗？你们说他是不是在追哈里·希克斯？”

避雨棚那一圈人顿时来了精神。齐声嚷：“加油啊，乔治！”“这是赛跑！”“你能追上！”“快加鞭！”

“它可真能跑，这马！”马夫小厮说。

“我的老天！”老图特尔斯叫道，“嘿！我都要乐出毛病来了。又来一辆。汉普斯特德（Hampstead）所有的马车今儿早上是集体发疯了吗！”

“这回是个娘们儿。”马夫小厮说。

“她这是在追他，”老图特尔斯说，“通常是反过来。”

“她手里拿着啥？”

“看着像顶大礼帽。”

“这可真他娘的热闹！三赔一押老乔治。”马夫小厮说，“下一个！”

===Original===
Minnie went by in a perfect roar of applause. She did not like it, but she felt that she was doing her duty, and whirled on down Haverstock Hill and Camden Town High Street with her eyes ever intent on the animated back view of old George, who was driving her vagrant husband so incomprehensibly away from her.

The man in the foremost cab sat crouched in the corner, his arms tightly folded, and the little tube that contained such vast possibilities of destruction gripped in his hand. His mood was a singular mixture of fear and exultation. Chiefly he was afraid of being caught before he could accomplish his purpose, but behind this was a vaguer but larger fear of the awfulness of his crime. But his exultation far exceeded his fear. No Anarchist before him had ever approached this conception of his. Ravachol, Vaillant, all those distinguished persons whose fame he had envied dwindled into insignificance beside him. He had only to make sure of the water supply, and break the little tube into a reservoir. How brilliantly he had planned it, forged the letter of introduction and got into the laboratory, and how brilliantly he had seized his opportunity! The world should hear of him at last. All those people who had sneered at him, neglected him, preferred other people to him, found his company undesirable, should consider him at last. Death, death, death! They had always treated him as a man of no importance. All the world had been in a conspiracy to keep him under. He would teach them yet what it is to isolate a man. What was this familiar street? Great Saint Andrew’s Street, of course! How fared the chase? He craned out of the cab. The Bacteriologist was scarcely fifty yards behind. That was bad. He would be caught and stopped yet. He felt in his pocket for money, and found half a sovereign. This he thrust up through the trap in the top of the cab into the man’s face. “More,” he shouted, “if only we get away.”

===Chinese===
明妮在一阵喝彩声中呼啸而过。她并不喜欢这样，可她觉得自己是在尽本分，便一路飞驰下哈弗斯托克山，转入卡姆登镇（Camden Town）大街，两眼始终盯着老乔治那生动活跃的背影——正是这个老乔治，正不可理喻地把她那离家出走的丈夫越拉越远。

最前面那辆马车里，那男人蜷缩在角落，双臂紧紧抱在胸前，手里紧紧攥着那根装着无穷毁灭可能的小试管。他的心境是恐惧与狂喜的奇异交织。他主要是怕还没得手就被逮住，可在这层恐惧背后，还有一团更模糊却更庞大的对自己罪行之可怖的惧意。然而他的狂喜远远压过了恐惧。在他之前，没有一个无政府主义者曾经企及他这等构想。拉瓦肖尔（Ravachol）、瓦扬（Vaillant），所有那些他曾艳羡其声名的显赫人物，在他面前都黯然失色。他只需找到水源，把这根小试管敲碎投进蓄水池。他的计划何等周全——伪造引荐信混进实验室，又何等利落地抓住了机会！世人终于要听到他的名字了。所有那些嘲笑过他、冷落过他、宁可选别人也不选他、嫌和他作伴煞风景的人，终于要正眼看他了。死亡，死亡，死亡！他们一向把他当作一个无足轻重的人。整个世界都串通好了要把他压在底下。他终要让他们见识见识，把一个人孤立起来是怎么回事。这条眼熟的街道是哪儿？大圣安德鲁街（Great Saint Andrew’s Street），自然是！追得怎么样了？他探身车外。细菌学家就在不到五十码之后。这下不妙。他还是要被追上、被拦下来的。他在口袋里摸钱，摸到半索维林（sovereign）。他把钱从车顶的活动小窗塞上去，怼到车夫脸上。“跑掉了还有，”他喊道，“只要咱们能甩掉他。”

===Original===
The money was snatched out of his hand. “Right you are,” said the cabman, and the trap slammed, and the lash lay along the glistening side of the horse. The cab swayed, and the Anarchist, half-standing under the trap, put the hand containing the little glass tube upon the apron to preserve his balance. He felt the brittle thing crack, and the broken half of it rang upon the floor of the cab. He fell back into the seat with a curse, and stared dismally at the two or three drops of moisture on the apron.

He shuddered.

“Well, I suppose I shall be the first. *Phew!* Anyhow, I shall be a martyr. That’s something. But it is a filthy death, nevertheless. I wonder if it hurts as much as they say.”

Presently a thought occurred to him﻿—he groped between his feet. A little drop was still in the broken end of the tube, and he drank that to make sure. It was better to make sure. At any rate, he would not fail.

Then it dawned upon him that there was no further need to escape the Bacteriologist. In Wellington Street he told the cabman to stop, and got out. He slipped on the step, and his head felt queer. It was rapid stuff, this cholera poison. He waved his cabman out of existence, so to speak, and stood on the pavement with his arms folded upon his breast awaiting the arrival of the Bacteriologist. There was something tragic in his pose. The sense of imminent death gave him a certain dignity. He greeted his pursuer with a defiant laugh.

“*Vive l’Anarchie!* You are too late, my friend, I have drunk it. The cholera is abroad!”

===Chinese===
钱被人从他手里一把夺走。“好嘞您。”车夫说，活动小窗砰地关上，鞭梢啪地落在马那油光水滑的肋腹上。马车一晃，那无政府主义者半个身子立在活动小窗下，把攥着小玻璃试管的那只手撑在挡帘上稳住身形。他感到那脆薄的东西裂了，断裂的半截叮当落在车厢地板上。他骂了一句，跌回座位，沮丧地盯着挡帘上那两三滴湿痕。

他打了个寒噤。

“好吧，看来我得当头一个了。呸！不管怎样，我算是个殉道者了。这总算点儿什么。可这死法也真够恶心的。不知道疼起来是不是真像人家说的那样。”

过了一会儿，他脑子里冒出一个念头——他在两脚之间摸索。试管断裂的一端还留着一小滴，他把它喝了，图个保险。保险点儿好。无论如何，他不能失败。

随即他恍然明白，已经不必再躲细菌学家了。到了惠灵顿街（Wellington Street），他叫车夫停下，下了车。他在踏脚上一滑，脑袋发懵。这霍乱毒药劲儿真够冲的。他算是把车夫一挥手打发出了自己的世界，然后双臂抱胸站在人行道上，等着细菌学家赶来。他那个姿势带着几分悲壮。大限将至的感觉赋予了他一种尊严。他用一声桀骜的笑迎接追上来的人。

“无政府主义万岁（Vive l’Anarchie）！你来晚了，朋友，我已经把它喝了。霍乱放出来了！”

===Original===
The Bacteriologist from his cab beamed curiously at him through his spectacles. “You have drunk it! An Anarchist! I see now.” He was about to say something more, and then checked himself. A smile hung in the corner of his mouth. He opened the apron of his cab as if to descend, at which the Anarchist waved him a dramatic farewell and strode off towards Waterloo Bridge, carefully jostling his infected body against as many people as possible. The Bacteriologist was so preoccupied with the vision of him that he scarcely manifested the slightest surprise at the appearance of Minnie upon the pavement with his hat and shoes and overcoat. “Very good of you to bring my things,” he said, and remained lost in contemplation of the receding figure of the Anarchist.

“You had better get in,” he said, still staring. Minnie felt absolutely convinced now that he was mad, and directed the cabman home on her own responsibility. “Put on my shoes? Certainly, dear,” said he, as the cab began to turn, and hid the strutting black figure, now small in the distance, from his eyes. Then suddenly something grotesque struck him, and he laughed. Then he remarked, “It is really very serious, though.

“You see, that man came to my house to see me, and he is an Anarchist. No﻿—don’t faint, or I cannot possibly tell you the rest. And I wanted to astonish him, not knowing he was an Anarchist, and took up a cultivation of that new species of Bacterium I was telling you of that infest, and I think cause, the blue patches upon various monkeys; and, like a fool, I said it was Asiatic cholera. And he ran away with it to poison the water of London, and he certainly might have made things look blue for this civilised city. And now he has swallowed it. Of course, I cannot say what will happen, but you know it turned that kitten blue, and the three puppies﻿—in patches, and the sparrow﻿—bright blue. But the bother is, I shall have all the trouble and expense of preparing some more.

“Put on my coat on this hot day! Why? Because we might meet Mrs. Jabber. My dear, Mrs. Jabber is not a draught. But why should I wear a coat on a hot day because of Mrs.﻿—Oh! *very* well.”

===Chinese===
细菌学家坐在车里，隔着镜片古怪地笑眯眯望着他。“你把它喝了！一个无政府主义者！我这下明白了。”他还要再说点什么，又止住了。一丝笑意挂在他嘴角。他掀开马车的挡帘，像是要下车，那无政府主义者见状，朝他戏剧性地一挥手作别，便大步朝滑铁卢桥（Waterloo Bridge）走去，一路上刻意用自己那染了病身子去挤撞尽可能多的人。细菌学家满脑子都是他那副身影，及至明妮拿着他的帽子、皮鞋和外套出现在人行道上，他也几乎没显出半点惊讶。“难为你把我的东西送来。”他说着，仍出神地凝视着无政府主义者远去的背影。

“你还是上车吧。”他说，眼睛仍盯着前方。明妮这下彻底确信他是疯了，便自作主张吩咐车夫回家。“穿上我的鞋？当然，亲爱的。”他说着，马车开始转弯，把那个昂首阔步的黑色身影——此刻已远成一个小点——挡在了他的视线之外。忽然，他觉得有件事滑稽透顶，便笑了起来。随后他开口说：“不过，这事还真挺严重的。

“你看，这个人到我家来找我，而他是个无政府主义者。别——别晕过去，不然我没法把剩下的话讲给你听了。我想吓唬吓唬他，那时还不知道他是无政府主义者，就拿起我先前跟你提过的那种新细菌的培养物——就是那种寄生在、而且我想也正是它造成了各种猴子身上蓝色斑块的细菌——我像个傻瓜似的跟他说那是亚洲霍乱。他拿着它跑掉了，要去毒伦敦的水，他本来确实能让这座文明城市愁云惨淡。可现在他自己把它吞下去了。当然，我说不准会怎么样，可你知道它把那只小猫染成了蓝色，那三只小狗——一身斑块，还有那只麻雀——鲜蓝。麻烦的是，我又得费事费力、再花一笔钱重新培养一批了。

“这么热的天要我穿外套！为什么？因为咱们可能会撞见贾珀太太（Mrs. Jabber）。亲爱的，贾珀太太又不是一股穿堂风。可为什么为了贾珀太太——这么热的天我就得穿外套呢？哦！好好好。”

## The Stolen Body / 被盗的躯体

===Original===
